confirmed.title: Terminal exits call Navigator.pop() on whatever route is on top, so a rider cancel (or any authoritative outcome) while Chat/Preferences/a modal sheet is open leaves the dead trip screen mounted
confirmed.description: Every authoritative exit from the trip screen ends with a plain pop of the navigator: `_handleRiderCancelled` (lines 452-458 `final home = Navigator.of(context); if (next == null && home.canPop()) { IslandMessages.show(...); ... home.pop(); return; }` and 478-481), `_leaveAfterAuthoritativeOutcome` (388-389), `_leaveAfterRelease` (403-407) and `_submitTripCancellation` (1444-1446). `Navigator.pop()` removes the topmost route, not the AcceptRide route. The trip screen itself pushes other routes onto the same navigator while the trip is live: `_messageRider` pushes `Chat` (accept_ride_panel.dart:860-867), `_openRidePreferences` pushes `Preferences` (536-541), `_openDestinationPicker` pushes the picker, the island pushes `DriverRideHistory` (accept_ride.dart:1307-1308), plus modal sheets (trip options, rider profile, cash collect, waiting time, safety toolkit, the accessible-confirm AlertDialog). A realtime `rider_cancelled`/terminal/`searching` event arriving while any of those is on top therefore pops that page instead of the trip: `_handleRiderCancelled` has already journaled the cancel, set the lifecycle terminal, run `_pauseLiveUpdates()` (GPS off, wait timer off), `_waybills.discardCurrent()` and queued an island notice for a Home that is never shown. The driver is left on a terminal AcceptRide: the slide/arrive actions return silently (`_advanceRide` checks `_rideLifecycle.terminal`), cancel says it cannot be cancelled, `PopScope(canPop:false)` blocks Back. Reproduced with a throwaway widget test (Home -> AcceptRide waiting -> a page pushed on top -> `realtime.emit(riderCancelled)`): result `chatPopped=true tripStillMounted=true homeVisible=false island=Rider cancelled`. Rider cancelling while the driver is in the chat with that rider is a very plausible sequence.
confirmed.failure_scenario: Driver is waiting at pickup, opens Message rider (Chat page on top). The rider cancels; realtime delivers rider_cancelled. The Chat page closes, the trip screen stays with GPS stopped and the waybill discarded; nothing on it works any more and Back is blocked. The 'Rider cancelled' island notice is queued for Home, which is not reached.
confirmed.suggested_fix: Pop to the trip's own route instead of the top route: capture `ModalRoute.of(context)` in the trip state and use `navigator.popUntil((r) => r != tripRoute && !r.isCurrent ...)` / `removeRoute`-style exit (e.g. `Navigator.of(context).popUntil((route) => route.isFirst)` when Home is the root, or `navigator.removeRoute(tripRoute)` after closing routes above it); for the `pushReplacement` branches first pop everything above the trip route.

verdicts.reason: _handleRiderCancelled (accept_ride_trip.dart:452-458) calls `Navigator.of(context).pop()`, which removes the topmost route. The trip screen pushes routes on the same navigator while live: Chat via pushSingle (accept_ride_panel.dart:860-867), Preferences (:537-540), the destination picker and history (accept_ride.dart:1307). Nothing closes those routes before the pop. By then the cancel is journaled, the lifecycle is terminal, live updates are paused and the waybill is discarded. The driver is left on a dead AcceptRide, and the island notice is queued for a Home that is not shown. The same pattern is at :388-389 and :403-407.

Output: `RESULT chat=0 trip=1 homeVisible=0` (the pushed page was popped, AcceptRide is still mounted, Home is not visible); test passed.

verdicts.reason: _handleRiderCancelled (accept_ride_trip.dart:452-458) does `final home = Navigator.of(context); if (next == null && home.canPop()) { ... home.pop(); }`, and _leaveAfterAuthoritativeOutcome (388-389) and _leaveAfterRelease (403-407) do the same. Navigator.pop removes the topmost route, not the AcceptRide route. The trip screen pushes routes such as Chat (accept_ride_panel.dart:860-867) onto that same navigator, so a terminal event while one of them is on top pops it instead. By then the lifecycle is already terminal, GPS is paused and the waybill is discarded, so the trip screen stays mounted and dead, and the island notice waits for a Home that is never shown. No guard checks ModalRoute.isCurrent. Caveat: realtime events need the future backend adapter (driver_composition_guard.dart:9).

confirmed.title: After a driver cancel or no-show the session never ends the trip, so Home stays 'on trip': no offers and Go online does nothing
confirmed.original_title: After a driver cancel or no-show the session never ends the trip, so Home stays 'on trip': no offers and Go online does nothing
confirmed.description: Every other way a trip can end releases the trip in the session controller: rider cancel (accept_ride_trip.dart:456/469), an authoritative outcome (:379), an admin release (:402) and completion (ride_completed.dart:71) all call `widget.sessionController?.stayOnlineAfterTrip()` (endTrip). `_submitTripCancellation`, which handles both a driver cancel and the driver no-show, never calls it. It journals the trip, calls `_rideLifecycle.cancel/noShow`, shows a SnackBar and then just `navigator.pop()`s (1439-1445). Nothing else ends the trip: Home's push of AcceptRide (home_offer_radar.dart:940, home.dart:567) has no `.then`, and AcceptRide.dispose does not touch the session. The DriverSessionController therefore keeps `_activeTripId = <cancelled trip>` and `_status = onTrip`. On Home, `_isOnline => _liveVisible && _recoveryResolved && _driverSession.availableForOffers` (home.dart:335) is false because `availableForOffers` needs `status == online`. Tapping Go online runs `_goOnline` (home.dart:884), which calls `beginGoingOnline()`. That returns at once when `_activeTripId != null` (driver_session_controller.dart:129). The 1.4 s timer's `completeGoingOnline()` then does nothing because the status is not goingOnline, yet the island still shows the 'online' notice. `setOnline` during a trip only flips `_offlineAfterTrip`. `DrivingTimeClock.sync(online: isOnline)` keeps counting driving time, because `isOnline` is true for onTrip. `didPopNext` skips restore because `activeTripId != null`. The same happens when the driver cancels with a secured next trip: the next AcceptRide's `beginTrip(next.id)` is ignored (driver_session_controller.dart:58-61), so the session keeps the cancelled trip's id until some later trip completes. No test confirms a driver cancel and then checks Home (integration_test/driver_lifecycle_test.dart:165 and test/widget_test.dart:2659 both tap 'Keep trip').
confirmed.failure_scenario: The driver is online on Home and accepts a Radar trip. At pickup the wait passes the no-show time. The driver taps 'Rider didn't show' and confirms (or picks Cancel trip with any reason and confirms). The SnackBar 'Trip cancelled · …' appears and Home comes back, but the radar shows OFF and no offers ever arrive. Tapping OFF/Go online shows the 'online' island message, but the session stays onTrip and the driver never becomes available. The driving-time clock keeps running and can force a rest. Only an app restart recovers. Worked out by hand from the code; nothing was run.
confirmed.evidence: accept_ride_trip.dart:1384 `if (!await (noShow ? _rideLifecycle.noShow(clearSnapshot: false) : _rideLifecycle.cancel(clearSnapshot: false))) { _cancellationInFlight=false; return; }` ... 1439-1445 `final navigator = Navigator.of(context); if (nextRide != null) { navigator.pushReplacement(...); return; } if (navigator.canPop()) { navigator.pop(); }` (no stayOnlineAfterTrip). Compare accept_ride_trip.dart:456 `widget.sessionController?.stayOnlineAfterTrip(); home.pop();`. driver_session_controller.dart:129 `if (_disposed || _activeTripId != null || isSuspended) { return; }`; :34 `bool get availableForOffers => _status == DriverOnlineStatus.online;`; home.dart:335 `bool get _isOnline => _liveVisible && _recoveryResolved && _driverSession.availableForOffers;`
confirmed.suggested_fix: In `_submitTripCancellation`, call `widget.sessionController?.stayOnlineAfterTrip()` after the lifecycle cancel/noShow succeeds and before `pushReplacement`/`pop`, as the rider-cancel and authoritative paths do. Add a widget test that confirms a driver cancel and a no-show from Home and expects LIVE/availableForOffers.

verdicts.reason: In `_submitTripCancellation` (accept_ride_trip.dart:1356-1446), the successful path journals the trip, runs lifecycle cancel/noShow (:1384), shows a SnackBar and then calls `pushReplacement` or `pop` (:1439-1445). It never calls `widget.sessionController?.stayOnlineAfterTrip()`. The only callers of endTrip/stayOnlineAfterTrip in lib/ are accept_ride_trip.dart:379, 402, 456 and 469 and ride_completed.dart:71, and none of them is on this path. `ActiveRideController` gets no session (accept_ride.dart:492-496), so it cannot end the trip either, and AcceptRide.dispose (accept_ride.dart:675-710) never touches the session. That leaves `_activeTripId` set and `_status` stuck at onTrip. `availableForOffers` (driver_session_controller.dart:34) is then false. `beginGoingOnline` returns early because `_activeTripId != null` (:129), and `completeGoingOnline` does nothing because the status is not goingOnline (:141). `restore()` also returns early (:179), and Home's didPopNext skips its restore while activeTripId is non-null (home.dart:182). On the secured-next path, `beginTrip(next.id)` is rejected because a different trip id is still active (driver_session_controller.dart:58-61). DECISIONS.md:107-108 explains the status mapping but says nothing that would keep the driver occupied after their own cancel.
verdicts.repro: Read-only static trace; nothing was run. I read _submitTripCancellation and grepped lib/ for every caller of endTrip/stayOnlineAfterTrip and every use of sessionController in the accept-ride folder. I also read the full DriverSessionController (beginTrip, beginGoingOnline, completeGoingOnline, restore, endTrip) and Home's didPopNext at home.dart:176-186.

verdicts.reason: _submitTripCancellation (accept_ride_trip.dart:1360-1445) never calls sessionController.endTrip/stayOnlineAfterTrip. The only callers in lib are accept_ride_trip.dart:379/402/456/469 and ride_completed.dart:71. Nothing else clears the trip: AcceptRide.dispose does not touch the session, and the controller's only other clearing methods are reset(), called only from profile.dart:397, and endTrip. _yieldToAuthoritativeTerminal (897-902) returns false unless a terminal projection is pending. So after a driver cancel or no-show, _activeTripId stays set and _status stays onTrip. availableForOffers (driver_session_controller.dart:34) is false, beginGoingOnline returns early at :129, completeGoingOnline does nothing at :142, setOnline during a trip only flips _offlineAfterTrip (:108-113), and Home's didPopNext skips the restore because activeTripId != null (home.dart:182). With a secured next trip, the next AcceptRide's beginTrip(next.id) is ignored at :58-61, because a different id is already active.
verdicts.repro: Read-only, as the run required; nothing was run. I traced the cancel and no-show path through pop() and grepped every endTrip/stayOnlineAfterTrip/reset caller in lib, then followed the DriverSessionController state for a driver who was online before the trip: status onTrip, activeTripId set, and no transition back to online.

confirmed.title: Closing (×) the Radar card whose Match claim is in flight leaves Home permanently in "Matching": no other trip can be matched and the won claim is dropped
confirmed.description: RadarOfferCard always shows the corner × on Home (onClose is always passed; radar_offer_card.dart:589-616 draws it regardless of `state`, including `matching`). _closeRadarHomeOffer (home_offer_radar.dart:890-896) calls _dismissRadarHomeOffer, which removes the offer from _radarHomeOffers and _homeRadarMatchStates (479-492) but never clears _homeRadarMatchingOfferId or _claimedHomeOffer. From then on: every other card's onMatch is null (`blocked != null && blocked != id ? null : ...`, 1127-1129), the radar orb is `busy` ("Matching · please wait", home_map_sheet.dart:1753-1774), _canStartScheduled is false so a scheduled "Leave now" goes to the backup driver (home_scheduled.dart:166-170, 177-178). When the dispatch claim resolves successfully, _claimHomeRadarOffer passes its guard (`_homeRadarMatchingOfferId == offer.id`), _resolveHomeRadarMatchWon sets _claimedHomeOffer and _openClaimedHomeOffer → 850 ms → _acceptRadarHomeOffer returns because the offer is no longer in _radarHomeOffers (925-928). _claimedHomeOffer stays set, so every later _scheduleVisibleOffers (resume) returns early at 1167-1170. The only exit is going offline (which runs _cancelAllOfferTimers without preserveClaim). The same path is reachable through _setAcceptsCash/_onCategoriesChanged, which dismiss listed offers regardless of claim state (home_offer_rules.dart:31-35, 52-56). Reproduced with a throwaway widget test (two offers on the deck, Match on `first`, tap `radar-offer-close`, then complete the claim with ClaimResult.success): AcceptRide never opened, `radar-match-second` onPressed stayed null and the orb read "Matching" 30 s later. Test result: `00:07 +2: All tests passed!`.
confirmed.failure_scenario: Driver taps Match on a Radar card, then (within the claim's network latency) taps the small × on that card. Dispatch answers success: the trip is assigned to this driver on the server, but no trip opens; the remaining cards' Match buttons are disabled and the radar says "Matching / please wait" indefinitely. The driver cannot accept any trip until they go offline and online again; a scheduled "Leave now" in that state is handed to a backup driver.
confirmed.evidence: home_offer_radar.dart:890-896 `void _closeRadarHomeOffer(_HomeDirectOffer offer) { if (offer.groupId != null && _homeRadarStateFor(offer.id) == _HomeRadarMatchState.available) { unawaited(_dispatch.declineOffer(offer.id)); } _dismissRadarHomeOffer(offer); }` | home_offer_radar.dart:483-492 `_rebuild(() { _radarHomeOffers.removeWhere((item) => item.id == offer.id); ... _homeRadarMatchStates.remove(offer.id); ...` (no _homeRadarMatchingOfferId / _claimedHomeOffer reset) | home_offer_radar.dart:925-928 `void _acceptRadarHomeOffer(_HomeDirectOffer offer) { if (!_radarHomeOffers.any((item) => item.id == offer.id)) { return; } ...` | home_offer_radar.dart:1127-1129 `onMatch: blocked != null && blocked != id ? null : () => _startHomeRadarMatch(offer),` | home_offer_radar.dart:1167-1171 `if (_claimedHomeOffer != null) { _openClaimedHomeOffer(); return; } if (_homeRadarMatchingOfferId != null) { return; }` | radar_offer_card.dart:589-591 `final close = onClose; if (close == null) { return card; } return Stack(`
confirmed.suggested_fix: Refuse × (and rule-driven dismissals) while `_homeRadarMatchingOfferId == offer.id` (pass onClose: null for a matching card), or make _dismissRadarHomeOffer clear _homeRadarMatchingOfferId/_claimedHomeOffer and cancel _homeRadarNoticeTimer when it removes the matching offer; and let _acceptRadarHomeOffer open the trip from _claimedHomeOffer even if the card was removed.

verdicts.reason: The × is always wired on Home cards (onClose at home_offer_radar.dart:1133), including in matching state; radar_offer_card.dart:589-616 draws it whenever onClose != null. _closeRadarHomeOffer -> _dismissRadarHomeOffer (479-492) removes the card but never clears _homeRadarMatchingOfferId or _claimedHomeOffer. A later success passes the guard at 546, and _resolveHomeRadarMatchWon sets _claimedHomeOffer. After 850 ms _acceptRadarHomeOffer returns because the card is gone (926), so the trip never opens. Other cards stay blocked, since onMatch is null while blocked != id (1127-1129), and later _scheduleVisibleOffers calls return early at 1167-1171. Only going offline clears it.
verdicts.repro: Throwaway widget test (now deleted), based on home_claim_ownership_test setup. Tap radar-match-first, tap radar-offer-close, complete the claim with ClaimResult.success, then pump about 32 s. Output: `d71 first card after x: 0`, `d71 AcceptRide: 0`, `d71 second onPressed null: true`, `All tests passed!`.

verdicts.reason: RadarOfferCard draws the × whenever onClose is non-null (radar_offer_card.dart:589-606), and Home always passes onClose (home_offer_radar.dart:1136), even while the card is in the matching state. _closeRadarHomeOffer goes to _dismissRadarHomeOffer (890-896, 479-492), which never clears _homeRadarMatchingOfferId or _claimedHomeOffer. A later successful claim passes the guard at 546, and _resolveHomeRadarMatchWon sets _claimedHomeOffer. Then _acceptRadarHomeOffer returns because the offer is no longer in _radarHomeOffers (925-928). The ids stay set, so every other card's onMatch is null (1127-1129), and _scheduleVisibleOffers returns early on resume (1167-1171). Only going offline clears this state.
verdicts.repro: Throwaway widget test with the same harness. Steps: tap radar-match-first, tap the hit-testable radar-offer-close, which removed the first card (`D71 first card after close: 0`), then complete the claim with ClaimResult.success and pump. Output: `D71 AcceptRide: 0`, `D71 second onPressed null: true`, and `D71 second onPressed null after 30s: true`. All tests passed. The file was deleted afterwards.

confirmed.title: "Leave now" removes the accepted scheduled ride from the store before a push that silently does nothing when Home is not the current route
confirmed.description: `_planScheduled` arms `Timer(_clock.realUntil(start), () => _leaveNow(ride))` (line 161). These timers live in `_scheduled.timers`, which `_pauseHomeUpdates` (home.dart 192-203) never cancels, and `_leaveNow`/`_canStartScheduled` (lines 166-170, 175-189) only check `mounted`, `_recoveryResolved`, `_driverSession.availableForOffers`, `_claimedHomeOffer` and `_homeRadarMatchingOfferId`; neither `_routeVisible` nor `ModalRoute.isCurrent` is consulted. `availableForOffers` is `_status == online` (driver_session_controller.dart 34), which stays true while the driver is on any non-trip screen pushed over Home (Scheduled rides, Notifications, Settings, Support, Wallet, Ride history, a modal sheet such as the destination details sheet or the queue sheet). When the timer fires in that state, `_startScheduledTrip` (218-239) first calls `ScheduledRideStore.start(ride)` which is `_removeAccepted(ride) != null` (scheduled_rides.dart 638-660) and permanently drops the ride from Accepted, posts the "Leave now" island message and notification, and only then calls `_HomeOfferRadar(this)._openOfferTrip(...)` (home_offer_radar.dart 931-981) whose `pushSingle(context, ActiveRideTransition(AcceptRide(...)))` returns `Future.value()` without pushing because `ModalRoute.of(context)?.isCurrent == false` (single_route_entry.dart 11-13). `_planScheduled()` then re-plans for the *next* ride. Nothing re-opens or restores the removed ride; `didPopNext` only re-runs `_restoreActiveRideIfNeeded`, and no AcceptRide/persisted trip was ever created.
confirmed.failure_scenario: Driver is online, has an accepted reservation for 07:40, and at 07:0x opens Scheduled rides (or any other screen/sheet) over Home to check it. The "leave now" moment arrives while that screen is on top: the ride disappears from Scheduled rides › Accepted, the island later flashes "Leave now for 07:40" and a notification "Leave now for 07:40 pickup" appears, but no trip screen ever opens; returning to Home shows no trip and the ride is gone for good (no backup hand-off either, since `_scheduled.ride` was set to null).
confirmed.evidence:
home_scheduled.dart 166-170: `bool get _canStartScheduled => _recoveryResolved && _driverSession.availableForOffers && _claimedHomeOffer == null && _homeRadarMatchingOfferId == null;`
home_scheduled.dart 218-237: `final started = ScheduledRideStore.start(ride); ... if (!started) { return; } _scheduled..ride = null..lateSince = null; ... _HomeOfferRadar(this)._openOfferTrip(_HomeDirectOffer.fromRide(offer), tr.scheduledRide); _planScheduled();`
scheduled_rides.dart 638-639: `static bool start(ReservationRequestPreview ride) => _removeAccepted(ride) != null;`
home_offer_radar.dart 940-942: `pushSingle(context, ActiveRideTransition(AcceptRide(`
single_route_entry.dart 11-13: `if (!context.mounted || ModalRoute.of(context)?.isCurrent == false) { return Future<T?>.value(); }`
home.dart 192-203 (`_pauseHomeUpdates`) cancels offer/radar timers only; `_scheduled.timers` keep running while Home is covered.
confirmed.suggested_fix: Make `_canStartScheduled` require Home to be current/visible (e.g. `_routeVisible && ModalRoute.of(context)?.isCurrent == true`) and treat the not-current case like `_lateScheduled`/defer; or defer `_leaveNow` until `didPopNext` (store a pending ride and run it in `_resumeHomeUpdates`). Alternatively only call `ScheduledRideStore.start(ride)` after `pushSingle` has actually pushed (check its return/`navigator` state) and roll back on a no-op push.

verdicts.reason: The Leave-now timer is armed in _planScheduled (home_scheduled.dart:161). It is not cancelled when Home is covered: _pauseHomeUpdates (home.dart:192-203) only stops offer and radar timers, and didPushNext (home.dart:174) does nothing to _scheduled.timers. _canStartScheduled (home_scheduled.dart:166-170) never checks _routeVisible or isCurrent. So _startScheduledTrip runs while another route is on top. It first calls ScheduledRideStore.start(ride), which removes the ride from Accepted (scheduled_rides.dart:638-639), and posts 'Leave now'. It then calls _openOfferTrip, whose pushSingle (home_offer_radar.dart:940) returns Future.value() without pushing because ModalRoute.isCurrent == false (single_route_entry.dart:11-13). Nothing checks that result. No AcceptRide is built, so no snapshot is persisted. didPopNext (home.dart:176-185) only restores persisted snapshots, so the ride is lost for good.
verdicts.repro: Throwaway test test/_audit_c4b3_sched_test.dart (deleted afterwards), built on the home_scheduled_test.dart harness. It accepts the 07:40 ride, pumps Home online for 30 s, pushes a MaterialPageRoute over Home, pumps 25 s, pops and pumps 5 s. Output: 'AUDIT before=true afterCovered=false tripCovered=0 tripAfterPop=0 said=[Leave now for 07:40 pickup] upcoming=1' and '00:05 +1: All tests passed!'. The ride left Accepted, Leave now was announced, and no AcceptRide appeared before or after the pop.

verdicts.reason: _canStartScheduled (home_scheduled.dart:166-170) never checks whether Home is visible. The scheduled timers are not cancelled when another screen opens, because _pauseHomeUpdates (home.dart:192-203) leaves _scheduled.timers alone. When the timer fires, _startScheduledTrip (home_scheduled.dart:218-238) calls ScheduledRideStore.start(ride) first, which removes the ride from Accepted. It then posts "Leave now" and calls _openOfferTrip, whose pushSingle (home_offer_radar.dart:940) returns without pushing because `ModalRoute.of(context)?.isCurrent == false` (single_route_entry.dart:11-13). Its result is ignored. The ride is not persisted anywhere. didPopNext (home.dart:176-186) only restores persisted active rides, so nothing brings the trip back. No document records this as intended.
verdicts.repro: Wrote test/_audit_d74_test.dart, built on the harness from test/widget/home_scheduled_test.dart (ride accepted, driver online). After 30 s of the demo day it pushes a MaterialPageRoute over DriverHome, waits 20 s, pops, then waits 5 s and 30 s more. Output: `before: upcoming has ride=true`; `covered: AcceptRide=0 upcoming has ride=false said=[Leave now for 07:40 pickup]`; `after pop: AcceptRide=0 upcoming has ride=false backup=null`; `later: AcceptRide=0 upcoming has ride=false`. A modal bottom sheet in place of the page route gives the same output. Result: All tests passed. File deleted.

confirmed.title: Same defect as driver-74: "Leave now" removes the accepted ride from Accepted, then pushSingle silently does nothing while any route or sheet covers Home, so the trip never opens and the ride is lost
confirmed.description: _leaveNow() fires from a Timer planned in _planScheduled(). Its only guard is _canStartScheduled (home_scheduled.dart:166-170: _recoveryResolved, availableForOffers, no claim in flight); it never checks that Home is the current route. _startScheduledTrip() first calls ScheduledRideStore.start(ride) (line 220), which removes the ride from Accepted (scheduled_rides.dart:638-639 / 652-660), posts "Leave now" and then calls _HomeOfferRadar._openOfferTrip (line 234). _openOfferTrip cancels every offer timer and calls pushSingle(context, ActiveRideTransition(AcceptRide(...))) (home_offer_radar.dart:940). pushSingle returns Future.value() without pushing when `ModalRoute.of(context)?.isCurrent == false` or while another push's entry animation is running (single_route_entry.dart:11-15). The return value is ignored, the post-frame callback clears the offers, _planScheduled() moves on to the next ride. Nothing is persisted (AcceptRide is what writes the active-ride snapshot), so the ride is gone from the phone: not in Accepted, not an active trip. Home's didPopNext restore only re-opens persisted snapshots, so returning to Home does not recover it. Any pushed route over Home triggers this: Scheduled rides screen (where a driver is likely to be looking at exactly this ride), Wallet, Preferences, Support inbox, Ride history, Notifications, Documents, the Go-offline confirm dialog, the driving-time/performance/waybill/destination/safety modal sheets. Reproduced with a throwaway widget test (fast demo day, ride accepted, a MaterialPageRoute pushed over Home at ~07:33, then 12 s): `Leave now for 07:40 pickup` was posted, ScheduledRideStore.upcoming no longer contained the ride, find.byType(AcceptRide) was findsNothing before and after popping the covering route. Test result: `00:07 +2: All tests passed!`.
confirmed.failure_scenario: Driver has accepted the 07:40 reservation, is online, and opens Scheduled rides (or any other screen) at 07:33. The smart-gap timer fires "Leave now": the ride leaves Accepted, the island (hidden) says "Leave now", no trip screen opens. Driver returns to Home: no active trip, the reservation is no longer in Accepted, nothing is persisted. The rider's ride is silently lost on this phone.
confirmed.evidence: home_scheduled.dart:166-170 `bool get _canStartScheduled => _recoveryResolved && _driverSession.availableForOffers && _claimedHomeOffer == null && _homeRadarMatchingOfferId == null;` | home_scheduled.dart:218-222 `_scheduled.planning = true; final started = ScheduledRideStore.start(ride); ... if (!started) { return; }` | home_scheduled.dart:234-237 `_HomeOfferRadar(this)._openOfferTrip(_HomeDirectOffer.fromRide(offer), tr.scheduledRide);` | home_offer_radar.dart:940-943 `pushSingle(context, ActiveRideTransition(AcceptRide(` | single_route_entry.dart:11-13 `if (!context.mounted || ModalRoute.of(context)?.isCurrent == false) { return Future<T?>.value(); }` | scheduled_rides.dart:638-639 `static bool start(ReservationRequestPreview ride) => _removeAccepted(ride) != null;`

confirmed.title: On web the 8 s GPS time limit is not enforced (geolocator_web 4.1.4 passes microseconds as ms, with no Dart timeout), so a browser that never answers blocks the one-shot fix and the GPS subscription on Home and the trip
confirmed.description: `DriverLocationService.getCurrentPosition()` relies on `LocationSettings(timeLimit: 8 s)` to bound the one-shot fix. Both screens subscribe to `watchPosition()` only after that call resolves: `accept_ride_trip.dart:598-606` (`final position = await _locationService.getCurrentPosition(); ... _positionSubscription = _locationService.watchPosition(distanceFilterMeters: 0).listen(...)`) and `home_map_sheet.dart:38-45` (the catch path also subscribes, but only if the call completes). On native the platform-interface applies `.timeout(timeLimit)`, so after 8 s the service falls back to the last known fix or throws and the screens show `Location updating…` and keep working. On web the pinned geolocator_web 4.1.4 overrides `getCurrentPosition` with no Dart-side timeout and converts the limit with `timeout?.inMicroseconds` into the browser's millisecond `PositionOptions.timeout` (8 s becomes 8,000 s, about 2.2 h). The app's own guard therefore does not hold on its primary (web/PWA) deployment: when the browser's geolocation does not answer (device has location permission but no fix, e.g. indoors, or a slow provider), the one-shot neither resolves nor errors, no stream is ever subscribed, no `Location updating…` status is set, and on the trip no route request is made (`_refreshRoadRoute(force: true)` sits in the catch).
confirmed.failure_scenario: Driver opens the PWA on a phone whose browser cannot obtain a fix right away: Home stays on the locating placeholder and the trip map shows no live car, no route and no status for as long as the browser withholds an answer (up to ~2.2 h) instead of falling back after 8 s as on native.
confirmed.evidence: driver_location_service.dart:21-26: `LocationSettings get _settings => LocationSettings(accuracy: kIsWeb ? LocationAccuracy.high : LocationAccuracy.bestForNavigation, timeLimit: const Duration(seconds: 8));` 29-36: `await _ensurePermission(); try { final position = await Geolocator.getCurrentPosition(locationSettings: _settings);`. accept_ride_trip.dart:598-606: `final position = await _locationService.getCurrentPosition(); ... _positionSubscription = _locationService.watchPosition(distanceFilterMeters: 0).listen(`. geolocator_web-4.1.4 lib/src/html_geolocation_manager.dart:34-37: `timeout: timeout?.inMicroseconds ?? const Duration(days: 1).inMilliseconds,`; geolocator_web.dart:74-85 awaits `_geolocation.getCurrentPosition(...)` with no `.timeout`.
confirmed.suggested_fix: Wrap `Geolocator.getCurrentPosition` in a Dart-side `.timeout(_settings.timeLimit!)` in `DriverLocationService.getCurrentPosition` (and `requestPermission` if it can block), and/or subscribe to `watchPosition` before awaiting the one-shot so a hung one-shot cannot block the stream.

verdicts.corrected_title: On web the 8 s GPS time limit is not enforced (geolocator_web 4.1.4 passes microseconds as ms, with no Dart timeout), so a browser that never answers blocks the one-shot fix and the GPS subscription on Home and the trip

DriverLocationService.getCurrentPosition (driver_location_service.dart:21-36) relies only on `LocationSettings.timeLimit`. Both screens use the real DriverLocationService for normal trips (accept_ride.dart:584, home.dart:453-454), and web/PWA is a primary deployment (DECISIONS.md:81-87). Whether a browser hangs depends on the device (for example high accuracy indoors), but the documented guard is plainly broken on web.

verdicts.corrected_title: On web the 8 s one-shot GPS limit becomes 8,000 s (geolocator_web 4.1.4 passes microseconds as milliseconds and adds no Dart timeout), so a slow browser fix leaves Home and the trip with no position, no 'Location updating…' status and no route until the browser answers
verdicts.reason: driver_location_service.dart:21-26 relies on `LocationSettings.timeLimit: 8 s`. In the pinned geolocator_web 4.1.4 (pubspec.lock:354-361), geolocator_web.dart:74-85 forwards `timeLimit` without a Dart `.timeout`, and html_geolocation_manager.dart:35-36 sets `timeout: timeout?.inMicroseconds`. That is 8 s = 8,000,000, which the browser reads as 8,000,000 ms = 8,000 s, about 2 h 13 min. On native, geolocator_android.dart:122-123 (and the apple equivalent) apply `.timeout(timeLimit)`, so the 8 s fallback only works off the web. Both callers await the one-shot before doing anything else. accept_ride_trip.dart:597 subscribes to the stream and sets the status/route fallback only after the call resolves or throws (catch at 619-627). home_map_sheet.dart:38 only reaches `_listenToDriverLocation` or `_startLocationFailed` afterwards. No other Dart guard bounds the wait. The impact lasts as long as the browser withholds both an answer and an error, for example during a high-accuracy cold start indoors. It is not a fixed 2.2 h in every case, because a browser may still return POSITION_UNAVAILABLE earlier.
verdicts.repro: Traced by hand in the pub cache sources: ~/.pub-cache/hosted/pub.dev/geolocator_web-4.1.4/lib/src/html_geolocation_manager.dart:35-36 `timeout: timeout?.inMicroseconds ?? const Duration(days: 1).inMilliseconds`. Duration(seconds: 8).inMicroseconds = 8,000,000, read as ms by PositionOptions.timeout, gives 8,000 s. geolocator_web.dart:78-85 awaits the completer with no timeout, while geolocator_android-5.0.3 geolocator_android.dart:122-123 does `positionFuture.timeout(timeLimit)`. I did not run anything in a browser.

confirmed.title: Trip auto-resume timer that fires while suspended is dropped and never re-armed; resume() does not reschedule it
confirmed.description: `_scheduleResume()` arms a one-shot Timer whose callback returns early when `_suspended` is true without rescheduling, and `resume()` (lines 693-696) only calls `_request(immediate: true)`, which is a no-op in browsing mode (`_canFollow` is false). The trip screen relies on this timer to bring the camera back to the car 12 s after the driver lets go of the map (`accept_ride.dart:488` sets `autoResumeAfter = tripAutoResume`, `accept_ride_trip.dart:794` sets `onAutoResume`). `suspend()` is called from `_pauseLiveUpdates` (`accept_ride_trip.dart:117`) on every lifecycle pause. On Android and on the web (PWA tab in background) Dart timers keep firing while the app is hidden, so the 12 s timer runs during the pause, hits the `_suspended` guard and dies. After `resume()` nothing re-arms it: `mapActivity()` only reschedules when `_resumeTimer != null`, and a later `update()` only calls `_scheduleResume()` on `enteringGuidance`, which is false mid-trip. Reproduced with a throwaway Flutter test (controller with `autoResumeAfter` 50 ms: userGesture, touching=false, suspend, wait 120 ms, resume, wait 300 ms): `Expected: <1> Actual: <0> after resume the camera should still auto-return`, mode stayed `browsing`.
confirmed.failure_scenario: Driver on an active trip pans the map (camera enters Free), switches to another app for more than 12 s on Android, comes back: the trip map stays where it was panned indefinitely; the camera never returns to the car until the driver touches the map again or taps recenter.
confirmed.evidence: driver_camera_controller.dart:472-484: `_resumeTimer = Timer(after, () { _resumeTimer = null; if (_disposed || _touching || _suspended || !isGuidance || mode != DriverCameraMode.browsing) { return; } ...`; 693-696: `void resume() { _suspended = false; _request(immediate: true); }`; 460-462: `void mapActivity() { if (_resumeTimer != null) _scheduleResume(); }`. Test run: `00:00 +0 -1: auto-resume timer that fires while suspended is never rescheduled [E] Expected: <1> Actual: <0>`.
confirmed.suggested_fix: In the timer callback, when `_suspended` is true, leave `_resumeTimer` unset but have `resume()` call `_scheduleResume()` (it already checks mode/guidance/touching); alternatively cancel the timer in `suspend()` and re-arm it in `resume()`.

verdicts.reason: When the 12 s one-shot timer fires while _suspended is set, its callback clears _resumeTimer and returns (driver_camera_controller.dart:472-477). resume() (:693-696) only calls _request(immediate:true), which does nothing in browsing mode. mapActivity re-arms only when _resumeTimer != null (:460-462), and update() calls _scheduleResume only on enteringGuidance (:576-578). The trip's resume path (accept_ride.dart:715-719 -> accept_ride_trip.dart:137-153 _resumeLiveUpdates, plus _resyncTrip) never recenters or re-arms. didChangeAppLifecycleState also pauses on 'inactive', for example when the notification shade is pulled down, so this is easy to reach. The recenter button is the only way back.
verdicts.repro: Throwaway widget test test/_audit_c4b2cam_test.dart (now deleted). Steps: controller with tripAutoResume; userGesture, touching false, 2 s, suspend(), pump 20 s, resume(), then 60 s of fresh navigating fixes. Output: '20: mode after resume + 60s of fixes: DriverCameraMode.browsing'.

verdicts.reason: The callback set in _scheduleResume (driver_camera_controller.dart:472-484) returns early when _suspended is true and does not re-arm. resume() (lines 693-696) only calls _request, and _request does nothing in browsing mode because _canFollow requires following. mapActivity (line 460) re-arms only if _resumeTimer != null. update() re-arms only on enteringGuidance (line 576), which is false mid-trip. The trip side gives no fallback either. accept_ride.dart:715-725 calls _pauseLiveUpdates on inactive, hidden or paused, and that calls _camera.suspend(). _resumeLiveUpdates (accept_ride_trip.dart:137-153) calls _camera.resume() and _startLiveLocation, and that path reaches _followVehicle(force:false) without recenter (lines 728-735). So once the 12 s timer fires during any inactive or paused period, the map stays on the panned view until the driver touches it or taps recenter.
verdicts.repro: Throwaway widget test test/_audit_cam20_test.dart (deleted). Controller with autoResumeAfter=tripAutoResume and an onAutoResume counter. Steps: update(navigating) -> touching=true, userGesture, touching=false -> pump 5s -> suspend() -> pump 10s -> resume() -> 60 one-second updates. Printed `resumes=0 mode=DriverCameraMode.browsing`. All other code paths checked by hand.

confirmed.title: Corrupt local JSON records leak rider name, pickup/dropoff addresses (and trusted-contact phones) into DriverLog via FormatException source excerpts
confirmed.description: DriverLog's own contract (lib/core/logging/driver_log.dart:5-6: 'Messages must not contain rider names, phone numbers or free text') is violated by every storage reader that logs a jsonDecode error. Dart's FormatException.toString() appends ~78 characters of the offending source around the error offset, and the stored records are JSON blobs holding rider names, phone numbers and addresses (active ride), trusted-contact phone numbers (settings sections) and completion journals. Paths: PrefsActiveRideRepository.read -> `DriverLog.error('Active-ride snapshot parse failed', error, stack)` (line 81) and again through `_enqueue`'s catchError (line 57); LocalQuarantine.store builds `reason: '$error'` from callers (prefs_active_ride_repository.dart:125, completion_journal.dart:157, settings_repository.dart:84) and then logs it: `DriverLog.warn('Quarantined $source record as $key: $reason')` (local_quarantine.dart:62). The default sink prints with debugPrint (driver_log.dart:42-43), which is not stripped in release builds, so this lands in logcat / the browser console; the file also says a crash-reporting adapter will be attached to this sink later. Reproduced with a throwaway flutter test: a truncated active-ride snapshot produced a log line containing `"riderPhone":"+46701234567","pickup":"Sveavägen 12, Stockholm"`, and a truncated contacts section produced `"phone":"+46709998877"` in the quarantine warning.
confirmed.failure_scenario: localStorage/SharedPreferences holds a half-written movera_driver_active_ride (e.g. tab killed mid-write) -> next launch Home calls read() -> the rider's name, phone and pickup address are printed to the device/browser log in a release build and would be shipped to any future crash-reporting sink.
confirmed.evidence: prefs_active_ride_repository.dart:80-82 `} catch (error, stack) { DriverLog.error('Active-ride snapshot parse failed', error, stack); throw ActiveRideUnreadable(error); }`; local_quarantine.dart:62 `DriverLog.warn('Quarantined $source record as $key: $reason');`; settings_repository.dart:84 `reason: '$storageKey: $error',`; driver_log.dart:5-6 `/// Messages must not contain rider names, phone numbers or free text; trip IDs and status names are allowed.`; test output: `Active-ride snapshot parse failed: FormatException: Unexpected end of input (at character 123)\n...na Svensson","riderPhone":"+46701234567","pickup":"Sveavägen 12, Stockholm"`
confirmed.suggested_fix: Log only the exception type/message without the source excerpt (e.g. `error is FormatException ? error.message : error.runtimeType`), and pass a scrubbed `reason` to LocalQuarantine (the raw text is already stored in the quarantine payload, so the reason need not repeat it).

verdicts.reason: The default sink prints the source excerpt that FormatException.toString() carries. In driver_log.dart:39-42 it formats '${record.message}: ${record.error}' and sends it through debugPrint, which still prints in release builds (logcat / browser console). That breaks the contract in driver_log.dart:5-6 that log messages must not contain rider names. The leak happens at prefs_active_ride_repository.dart:81 (the parse error), again at :57 (the _enqueue catchError re-logs ActiveRideUnreadable), and in local_quarantine.dart:62 via reason '$error' (prefs_active_ride_repository.dart:125). No scrubbing guard exists on any of these paths. The trigger is an edge path: the record has to be corrupt, and SharedPreferences/localStorage writes are atomic, so 'killed mid-write' is unlikely. The app does build explicit quarantine handling for this case, though. The exposure is the device's local log, plus any future sink.
verdicts.repro: Ran the throwaway test test/_audit_d25log_test.dart (deleted afterwards). It put a truncated snapshot containing riderName/pickup under PrefsActiveRideRepository.key, captured DriverLog.sink, then called read() and quarantineUnreadable(). Output: 'LOG>> Active-ride snapshot parse failed: FormatException: Unterminated string (at character 130) ...erName":"Anna Svensson","pickup":"Sveavagen 12, Stockholm"...', the same excerpt again in 'Active-ride storage operation failed' and in 'Quarantined active_ride record as movera_driver_quarantine_active_ride_...'. Result: +1 All tests passed.

confirmed.title: Scheduled-ride waiting rule is found by searching the localized 'Scheduled ride' label, so French and Swedish drivers get different wait and no-show terms
confirmed.original_title: Scheduled-ride waiting rule is found by searching the localized 'Scheduled ride' label, so French and Swedish drivers get different wait and no-show terms
confirmed.description: AcceptRide builds `_waitTerms` from `WaitingRules.typeOf(matchedVia: widget.matchedVia, ...)` (accept_ride.dart:989-996). `typeOf` sees a scheduled ride only if `matchedVia.toLowerCase()` contains 'scheduled' or 'reservation'. 'Leave now' opens the trip with `matchedVia: tr.scheduledRide` (home_scheduled.dart:236). That is 'Scheduled ride' in English, 'Course planifiée' in French and 'Bokad resa' in Swedish, so in fr/sv the type falls back to `WaitingRideType.normal`. The scheduled rule is skipped: its free wait (`ScheduledRideRules.current.includedWaitingMinutes`), any admin perMin/noShowFee for `rideTypes.scheduled` (driver_app_config.dart reads them), and its 'Scheduled ride' rule label. The matchedVia string is also saved in the snapshot, so a restored trip keeps the wrong type.
confirmed.failure_scenario: Take a scheduled Movera XL reservation (category rule free 3 / no-show 3) and press Leave now. In English, termsFor applies XL, then scheduled sets free to 5, and the final guard lifts no-show to 5: 5 free minutes, no-show at 5 min. With the app in Swedish or French the same trip gets 3 free minutes and no-show at 3 min. Paid waiting therefore starts 2 minutes earlier (12,26 kr/min) and the driver can mark a no-show 2 minutes earlier, only because of the UI language. confirmed.title: Ride-check audio that is still starting when the card closes keeps the microphone recording with no UI, and dispose() never stops it after a later check opens
confirmed.description: `toggleRecording()` sets `_audio = starting`, awaits `recorder.requestPermission()` and then `recorder.start(...)` (lines 240-251). On native that start awaits `getApplicationDocumentsDirectory()`, `Directory.create` and the plugin. If the driver answers meanwhile (`imOk`/`done` → `_close()`), `_close()` calls `_stopRecording()` which returns immediately because `_audio != recording` (line 275), then marks the record answered and closes the card. When `start()` later completes, the only guard is `if (_disposed)` (line 260): `_audio` becomes `recording`, `_audioStartedAt` is set and a periodic 1 s ticker starts notifying listeners (lines 264-270) although the card is closed and `_answerable` is false, so nothing on screen shows a recording and no button can stop it. If a further Ride check opens later, `open()` resets `_audio = idle` (line 114) without touching the recorder or the ticker, after which `dispose()` skips the stop because `_audio != recording` (line 412) — the native recorder is never stopped for the rest of the process. Reproduced with a throwaway flutter test using a recorder whose `start()` awaits a Completer: after `imOk()` and completing start, `c.audio == RideCheckAudio.recording` and the fake recorder was still recording; after `open()` of a second event and `dispose()`, the recorder was still recording with `stops == 0` (test output: `after close: audio=RideCheckAudio.recording recorderRecording=true stops=0` / `after dispose: recorderRecording=true stops=0`). The test file was deleted afterwards.
confirmed.failure_scenario: Long-stop card opens, driver taps 'Record audio' and, while the OS mic permission sheet / recorder start is still in flight (hundreds of ms on a phone), taps 'I'm OK'. The card closes but the phone keeps recording the cabin to ride_check_audio/*.m4a with no indicator; after the next Ride check on the same trip and leaving the trip screen, the recorder is still running until the app process dies.
confirmed.evidence: ride_check_controller.dart:250-251 `if (_disposed || !_answerable) return;\n      await recorder.start(...)` · :260-265 `if (_disposed) { unawaited(recorder.cancel()); return; }\n    _audio = RideCheckAudio.recording;` (no `_answerable`/`_closing` check after the await) · :273-275 `Future<void> _stopRecording() async { final recorder = _recorder; if (recorder == null || _audio != RideCheckAudio.recording) return;` · :114 `_audio = RideCheckAudio.idle;` in `open()` · :412-415 `if (_audio == RideCheckAudio.recording) { unawaited(_recorder?.stop()...` in `dispose()`
confirmed.suggested_fix: After `await recorder.start(...)` re-check `_disposed || _closing || !_answerable` and cancel/stop the recorder if the card is no longer open; in `open()` and `dispose()` stop any recorder that was started regardless of the `_audio` flag (track a `_recorderRunning` bool set around start/stop).

confirmed.title: Saved Ride-preferences category choice is never restored at boot, so switched-off categories are offered again after every restart
confirmed.description: `DriverCategoryChoice.off` (ride_categories.dart:56) is the in-memory set that every offer filter reads (`DriverCategoryChoice.takes` in home_offer_rules.dart:13/21/30, home_reservation.dart:107/132, scheduled_rides.dart:545). The only writer is the Ride preferences screen: `_publishChoice()` runs after `_restoreSettings()` or a toggle (preferences.dart:118/172), i.e. only once that screen has been opened. The choice is persisted to the `categories` settings section (preferences.dart:140), but nothing reads it back at app start: `main.dart:41-49` restores `MapTrafficSetting` and `DriverLanguage` and nothing else, and `DriverCategoryChoice` has no restore method. After a cold start `off` is the empty const set, so `takes()` returns true for every allowed category. The class comment (`ride_categories.dart:51`, 'kept for the session') documents the in-memory nature but the persisted setting and the Q27 promise ('offers follow that choice') make the restart behaviour wrong. The same global is also not reset on logout (`main.dart:180-195` calls `MapTrafficSetting.reset()` / `DriverLanguage.reset()` but not `DriverCategoryChoice.reset()`), so after logout the cleared storage and the stale in-memory set disagree until Preferences is opened again.
confirmed.failure_scenario: Driver opens Ride preferences, switches off 'Movera Pet' (saved to settings), kills and relaunches the app, goes online. Home shows Radar/Exclusive/reservation offers in the Pet category (and scheduled Pet rides) because `DriverCategoryChoice.off` is empty; the filter only starts working again after the driver happens to open Ride preferences.

confirmed.suggested_fix: Add `DriverCategoryChoice.restore([SettingsRepository])` that reads the `categories` section the same way `_restoreSettings` does and publishes the off-set; call it from `main()` beside `MapTrafficSetting.restore()`, and call `DriverCategoryChoice.reset()` in `_logout`.

The choice is saved to SharedPreferences (settings_repository.dart:16; preferences.dart:140). The only reader of the 'categories' section is preferences.dart:105. main.dart:41-49 restores only MapTrafficSetting and DriverLanguage. So after a cold start `off` is the empty set from ride_categories.dart:56, and the offer filters let switched-off categories through: home_offer_rules.dart:13/21/30, home_reservation.dart:107/132, scheduled_rides.dart:545. It does not justify ignoring a choice the app persisted and shows as saved. The logout half is also real: main.dart:180-195 clears local data and resets traffic and language but never calls DriverCategoryChoice.reset() (ride_categories.dart:65). The previous driver's off-set therefore keeps filtering offers for the next session until Preferences is opened.

verdicts.reason: `DriverCategoryChoice.off` starts as the empty const set (lib/core/vehicle/ride_categories.dart:56-57). Its only writer is `_publishChoice` at lib/presentation/driver/preferences/preferences.dart:172. That runs only after the Ride preferences screen's `_restoreSettings` (initState) or a toggle, so only once that screen is opened. main() at lib/main.dart:41-49 restores MapTrafficSetting and DriverLanguage but never reads the `categories` section, and the class has no restore method. confirmed.title: WaybillPayment.fromFare reads only the first digit group of a thousands-grouped fare label, so earnings/fee are wrong for fares >= 1 000 kr
confirmed.description: Money.formatted groups thousands with a space ("1 234,50 kr", lib/core/money/money.dart:187 via _group). RideOffer.fareLabel (dispatch_repository.dart:114) and WaitingTerms.addFee (waiting_rules.dart:77, used for _fareWithWaiting on completion) both produce this format, and it is what reaches WaybillRecord.fare. WaybillPayment.fromFare parses the label with `RegExp(r'\d+(?:[.,]\d{1,2})?').firstMatch(fare)` which matches only the leading "1" of "1 234,50 kr", so fareOre becomes 100 and _comma is false. Consumers: waybill_sheet.dart:70 (`WaybillPayment.fromFare(record.fare, bonus: record.driverBonus)` -> "Your earnings" row) and OfferCardDetails.fare (offer_rules.dart:157, the net-fare mode admin can switch on for offer cards). Money.parseSekLabel already accepts the grouped form (money.dart:73), so the producer and this consumer disagree. Reproduced with a throwaway flutter test: `Money(minorUnits:123450).formatted` = "1 234,50 kr"; `WaybillPayment.fromFare(that)` gave fare=1.00 kr, fee=0.25 kr, earnings=0.75 kr; `OfferCardDetails(netFare:true).fare(label)` = "0.75 kr".
confirmed.failure_scenario: A driver completes a 1 234,50 kr trip (any backend Offer.fare >= 100000 minor units, or a demo fare pushed over 1 000 kr by waiting fees). Opening the waybill shows "Your earnings 0.75 kr" and "Service fee 0.25 kr" instead of about 925,88 kr / 308,62 kr; with netFare on, the offer card shows a 0.75 kr net fare for a 1 234 kr trip.
confirmed.evidence: waybill.dart:296 `final match = RegExp(r'\d+(?:[.,]\d{1,2})?').firstMatch(fare);` ... :301 `final fareOre = (value * 100).round();`  |  money.dart:187 `return '$sign${_group(int.parse(parts[0]))},${parts[1]} $symbol';` (groups thousands with a space)  |  waybill_sheet.dart:70 `final payment = WaybillPayment.fromFare(record.fare, bonus: record.driverBonus);`  |  test output: `formatted = "1 234,50 kr"` / `fare=1.00 kr fee=0.25 kr earnings=0.75 kr` / `netFare card = 0.75 kr` / `parseSekLabel = 123450`
confirmed.suggested_fix: Parse the fare with Money.parseLabel/parseSekLabel (which understand grouped thousands and the currency suffix) instead of the ad-hoc regex, e.g. `final money = Money.parseLabel(fare); if (money == null) return null; fareOre = money.minorUnits;` and keep the comma flag from the label. Add a test for a >= 1 000 kr label.

verdicts.reason: WaybillPayment.fromFare (lib/core/waybill/waybill.dart:296) reads only the first digit group of `RegExp(r'\d+(?:[.,]\d{1,2})?')`. Money.formatted puts a space between thousands (money.dart:187 `_group`), and both RideOffer.fareLabel (dispatch_repository.dart:114) and WaitingTerms.addFee produce that form. So any fare of 1 000 kr or more is read as its leading digits, and the waybill's 'Your earnings' and 'Service fee' rows (waybill_sheet.dart:70) and the net-fare card (offer_rules.dart:157) show nonsense amounts. No guard applies. The demo dispatch fares are all at most 300 kr, so today this only happens with a contract or backend fare of 1 000 kr or more (100 000 minor units) or a very long waiting fee. That makes it an edge path in the demo, though a normal one for long trips once real fares arrive.

RideOffer.fareLabel is fare.formatted (dispatch_repository.dart:114), and Home and Ride requests use it as the trip fare (home_offer_radar.dart:130, ride_requests.dart:151). WaybillPayment.fromFare (waybill.dart:296) uses `RegExp(r'\d+(?:[.,]\d{1,2})?').firstMatch`, which stops at the space, so it reads only '1' from '1 234,50 kr'. confirmed.title: An authoritative `completed` projection archives a cash trip without its payment method, cash collected or waiting fee
confirmed.description: The driver's own Finish (`_completeCurrentTrip`, lines 912-917) journals `_paidWaybill()` (fare incl. the driver's waiting fee) with `paymentMethod: 'Cash'` and `cashCollected` for a cash trip; `TripHistoryRecord.cashBalance` and the history 'Other earnings' cash accounting depend on `paymentMethod == 'cash'`. The realtime terminal path in `_drainProjection` (contract rows `complete` by admin from rider_onboard/in_trip/approaching_dropoff, or a server echo of `completed`) journals `_waybills.current ?? _buildCurrentWaybill()` with only `status` and `authoritative: true`. The archived row then has no `paymentMethod`/`cashCollected` and no waiting fee, so the driver's cash balance for that trip (what they owe or are owed) silently disappears from history, and with `authoritative: true` it also overwrites a correct local row if one was written first.

'Cash' : null, cashCollected: widget.paidByCash ? _cashToCollect : null);`; trip_history.dart:59 `bool get paidByCash => paymentMethod.trim().toLowerCase() == 'cash';`

confirmed.title: A repeated same-stage (onTrip) projection restarts the next-trip radar: an accepted (matching) or shown Exclusive offer is dropped, and the route and camera are re-fitted
confirmed.description: `_drainProjection` treats a successful `applyProjection` as a stage change: `if (!await _rideLifecycle.applyProjection(status)) { return; } if (mounted) { _rebuild(() {}); _resumeStageSideEffects(); }` (lines 340-342). But `ActiveRideController.applyProjection` returns true without changing anything when `next == _stage` (active_ride_controller.dart: 'Realtime may repeat the same stage each poll ... if (next == _stage) { return true; }'). Same-stage projections are normal: `reconnectAndResync` (called on every app resume, accept_ride.dart:719, and on every sequence gap, accept_ride_trip.dart:248) re-emits the cached projection with a new sequence (driver_realtime.dart:468-482), and a poll/echo would do the same. For `onTrip`, `_resumeStageSideEffects` (100-115) then calls `_rideCheckDetector.startTrip(...)` (forgetting any long-stop/off-route progress), `_demoDrive?.startTrip()`, `_startOnTripRadar()` (995-1008) which cancels `_nextTripRadarMatchTimer` and sets `scanning` with `_nextTripRadarOffer = null` — so an offer the driver has just accepted (900 ms `matching` window, 1190-1208) is silently discarded after `ExclusiveAnswers.accepted()` was already counted, and an offer on screen disappears — and finally `_refreshOnTripRoute(fitCamera: true)` forces a route re-fetch and camera re-follow. Reproduced with a throwaway widget test: on-trip demo offer shown, tap 'match next', emit an `in_trip` projection: `securedCardPresent=false offerVisible=true` (the same offer is re-presented as a new one instead of being secured).
confirmed.failure_scenario: Driver on trip accepts the Exclusive next-trip offer; within a second the app is resumed or a projection echo arrives with status in_trip. The match timer is cancelled, the state goes back to scanning, the accepted trip is lost and the same offer pops up again (or is gone if declined before); the long-stop ride-check timer also restarts from zero.
confirmed.suggested_fix: Only run `_resumeStageSideEffects()` when the stage actually changed (compare `_stage` before/after `applyProjection`, or have `applyProjection` report 'unchanged' distinctly), and make `_startOnTripRadar` a no-op when state is `matching`/`offerAvailable`.

verdicts.reason: active_ride_controller.dart:152-154 returns true when `next == _stage`. accept_ride_trip.dart:340-341 then always runs _resumeStageSideEffects. For onTrip, when radar state is not `secured`, that calls _startOnTripRadar (:995-1006). _startOnTripRadar cancels _nextTripRadarMatchTimer and sets state to scanning with _nextTripRadarOffer = null. That drops an offer in the 900 ms `matching` window after ExclusiveAnswers.accepted() (:1190-1208), or one on screen. Same-stage projections happen routinely: rider_onboard -> in_trip -> approaching_dropoff all map to onTrip (:142-144), including the system `near_dropoff`. Resume also calls _resyncTrip (accept_ride.dart:719), and MemoryDriverRealtime re-issues the projection with a new sequence (driver_realtime.dart:468-476), so the gate does not drop it as a duplicate. This also defeats D-05's intent that a shown offer keeps its deadline across a resume (:124-126). The finding overstates one part. RideCheckDetector.startTrip (ride_check_detector.dart:29 `_tripStartedAt ??= at`) and DemoTripDrive.startTrip (`_ticks ??= 0`) are idempotent, so ride-check progress is NOT reset. The other effects are real: a forced route refresh and a camera re-fit.

verdicts.corrected_title: A repeated same-stage (onTrip) projection restarts the next-trip radar: an accepted (matching) or shown Exclusive offer is dropped, and the route and camera are re-fitted
A same-stage projection (e.g. approaching_dropoff during onTrip) re-runs the onTrip side effects: an accepted next-trip offer in its matching window is dropped and the ride-check detector restarts
verdicts.reason: ActiveRideController.applyProjection returns true without changing anything when next == _stage (active_ride_controller.dart:150-153). rider_onboard, in_trip and approaching_dropoff all map to onTrip (142-144), so normal server progress within the trip is same-stage. _drainProjection (accept_ride_trip.dart:340-341) then calls _resumeStageSideEffects (100-115). That runs _rideCheckDetector.startTrip and, because the state is matching rather than secured, _startOnTripRadar (995-1008), which cancels _nextTripRadarMatchTimer and sets the radar back to scanning with offer null. The 900 ms match timer (1194-1199) never fires, so secureNext is never called, even though ExclusiveAnswers.accepted() was already counted. Nothing checks whether the stage changed.

confirmed.title: Re-tapping Continue on Add vehicle after taking document photos silently deletes the saved photos
confirmed.description: `_save` always upserts the bare identity map `submitted` = {id, make, model, year, plate} (lines 76-85) using the fixed `_vehicleId`. `LocalVehicleStore._upsertSnapshot` replaces the whole row for that id (`rows.removeWhere((row) => row['id'] == vehicle['id']); rows.insert(..., Map.of(vehicle))`, local_vehicle_store.dart) and skips photo fields that are null (`if (value == null) continue;`). After the driver has taken a registration/insurance photo on VehicleDocuments (which upserts the row with `registrationPhoto`/`insurancePhoto`), pressing Back returns to the still-mounted AddVehicle whose `_ready` is still true; tapping Continue again writes the row without the photo keys and the photos are gone. The new VehicleDocuments then restores `_registrationDone = false` and shows 'Recommended next step' again with no message. Reproduced at store level with a throwaway test (upsert identity -> upsert with photo -> upsert identity -> list: `registrationPhoto` absent), test deleted afterwards.

confirmed.suggested_fix: In `_save`, merge onto the existing row (`{...previousRow, ...submitted}`) or have the store preserve photo fields when the incoming map omits them; alternatively navigate with pushReplacement / disable re-save once the draft exists.

verdicts.reason: AddVehicle._save always upserts only the identity fields {id, make, model, year, plate}, using the fixed _vehicleId (add_vehicle.dart:41-42, 76-85). confirmed.title: AppLifecycleState.inactive is treated as not foreground, so Home renders the driver as offline (radar "OFF · Tap to scan", offline dock, no "Finding trips") while the session is online
confirmed.description: didChangeAppLifecycleState sets `_foreground = state == AppLifecycleState.resumed` (line 189); _isOnline (line 335) is `_liveVisible && _recoveryResolved && availableForOffers`, and the radar layer, dock, side menu and island all branch on _isOnline (home_map_sheet.dart:1654-1694, 1594, home.dart:713). `inactive` is a visible state: iOS during a phone call banner, Control Center/notification centre, Face ID prompt, app switcher; Android during a system dialog, the location-permission dialog, multi-window without focus. In all of these the app is on screen and after _pauseHomeUpdates() (line 190) it draws the offline face, cancels the dispatch subscription and offer timers, although DriverSessionController still says online and dispatch still sends offers. On return it snaps back. An incoming phone call while online is a routine driver situation.
confirmed.failure_scenario: Driver is online on Home; a phone call comes in on iOS (app stays visible behind the call banner, state = inactive). Home immediately shows "Radar · OFF · Tap to scan" and the offline dock for the whole call; the driver believes they were taken offline. When the call ends, the online face returns. Offers arriving during the call were not listed.
confirmed.evidence: home.dart:187-191 `void didChangeAppLifecycleState(AppLifecycleState state) { _foreground = state == AppLifecycleState.resumed; if (_liveVisible) { _resumeHomeUpdates(); } else { _pauseHomeUpdates(); } }` | home.dart:335 `bool get _isOnline => _liveVisible && _recoveryResolved && _driverSession.availableForOffers;` | home_map_sheet.dart:1686-1694 `child: _isOnline ? (holdOff ? _holdOffRadar() : ...) : _isGoingOnline ? _buildGoingOnlineButton() : _buildGoOnlineButton(),`
confirmed.suggested_fix: Treat `inactive` as foreground for rendering (only `paused`/`hidden`/`detached` pause updates), or keep rendering from the session state and use _liveVisible only to gate timers/subscriptions.

verdicts.reason: home.dart:189 sets _foreground = (state == resumed), so the inactive state makes _liveVisible false (line 165). _isOnline (line 335) is gated on _liveVisible, so Home draws the offline radar and dock while DriverSessionController.availableForOffers is still true. Line 190 also calls _pauseHomeUpdates, which cancels the radar and withdrawal subscriptions and the offer timers. No guard tells inactive apart from paused or hidden. In inactive, Flutter keeps drawing frames and the app stays on screen (for example Control Center, the Android notification shade, a system dialog, a full-screen incoming call). The finding is accurate. One correction: the offer card stays in the tree, but the online radar face is replaced by 'OFF · Tap to scan'.

(1110-1116). _goOffline() calls _HomeOfferRadar._cancelAllOfferTimers() without preserveClaim (home.dart:949), which sets _homeRadarMatchingOfferId = null (home_offer_radar.dart:796-800). When _dispatch.claimOffer later resolves with ClaimOutcome.success, _claimHomeRadarOffer returns at line 546 because `_homeRadarMatchingOfferId != offer.id`; nothing tells dispatch and nothing is shown. In the demo repository the offer was already removed from the feed by the claim (demo_dispatch_repository.dart:565-566), i.e. it is taken by this driver. The driver is offline, the rider is matched to a driver who is not coming.

Dispatch answers success → the trip is assigned to this driver server-side; the app shows nothing, stays offline, never opens the trip and never declines/cancels it.

confirmed.title: Two Radar offers lost within 2.8 s share one _homeRadarLostMatchTimer: only the last is dismissed, and the other stays in _radarHomeOffers (hidden by the deck), which keeps the deck slot and "trips found" up and holds back every Exclusive offer

Concrete demo path: two destination-mode trips on the deck (home_map_sheet.dart:463-465), then "Turn off destination" → _clearDemoDestinationTrips → DemoDispatchRepository.clearDestinationTrips emits a snapshot without both (demo_dispatch_repository.dart:614-624) → both resolved lost in one loop. verdicts.corrected_title: Two Radar offers lost within 2.8 s share one _homeRadarLostMatchTimer: only the last is dismissed, and the other stays in _radarHomeOffers (hidden by the deck), which keeps the deck slot and "trips found" up and holds back every Exclusive offer
verdicts.reason: _resolveHomeRadarMatchLost cancels and replaces the single field _homeRadarLostMatchTimer (home_offer_radar.dart:691-702), and the closure only dismisses the latest offer. When the snapshot loop (604-611) resolves two offers, or two withdrawals arrive within 2.8 s (_onOfferWithdrawn, 917-923), the first offer stays in state claimedElsewhere. Nothing else removes it on Home: _refreshRadarHomeOffers keeps it (386-399), the external-claim cleanup handles only its own offer, and only pause/resume (_resumeOfferTimers 765-784), × or going offline clear it. The finding's description of the result is wrong. RadarOfferDeck hides taken cards (radar_offer_deck.dart:126-139), so no "Taken" card stays visible. The real effect is that _radarHomeOffers stays non-empty: the deck slot stays up (home_map_sheet.dart:873-876), _hasRideOffers stays true, and _showOutsideRadarOffer refuses every Exclusive offer while `_radarHomeOffers.isNotEmpty` (home_offer_radar.dart:235). The demo path is real: destination-mode trips on the deck, then Turn off in the details sheet. That sheet pops first and then calls onTurnOff (destination_island.dart:187-188), so the live subscription receives a snapshot without both trips.

confirmed.title: Won admin direct assign or Exclusive reservation is lost (shows 'Trip matched' or 'accepted', no trip opens) when a drawer route covers Home as the claim resolves
confirmed.description: _claimExclusiveReservation (home_reservation.dart:484-509) and _claimAdminAssign (home_offer_radar.dart:843-860) await dispatch, then on success call ScheduledRideStore.take(offer.id) / show "matched" and _openOfferTrip, which pushes via pushSingle (home_offer_radar.dart:940). pushSingle silently does nothing when Home is not the current route (single_route_entry.dart:11-13). During the claim the Exclusive sheet covers the dock, but the Scaffold drawer is still reachable by edge swipe (it is not a route) and its items push screens (Ride history, Wallet, …). The claim result then arrives while a route covers Home: the reservation has left Scheduled rides (take()), _reservation.wonId is set, _outsideRadarOffer is cleared in the post-frame callback, and no trip opens. Unlike the Radar deck path (_openClaimedHomeOffer waits for _liveVisible and is retried from _scheduleVisibleOffers), these two paths have no deferral/retry.
confirmed.failure_scenario: Exclusive reservation (or admin direct assign) is up, driver taps Accept, edge-swipes the drawer and opens Ride history while the claim is pending. Dispatch answers success: the reservation disappears from Scheduled rides and from Home, the island says "accepted", but no trip screen ever opens and nothing is persisted; on the server the trip is this driver's.
confirmed.evidence: home_reservation.dart:505-509 `ScheduledRideStore.take(offer.id); _reservation.wonId = offer.id; IslandMessages.show(HomeIslandNotices.reservationAccepted); _HomeOfferRadar(this)._acceptOutsideRadarOffer();` | home_offer_radar.dart:858-860 `case ClaimOutcome.success: IslandMessages.show(HomeIslandNotices.matched); _openOfferTrip(offer, ExclusiveReasons.text(ExclusiveReasons.assigned));` | home_offer_radar.dart:940 `pushSingle(` | single_route_entry.dart:11-13 `if (!context.mounted || ModalRoute.of(context)?.isCurrent == false) { return Future<T?>.value(); }`
confirmed.suggested_fix: Route won Exclusive claims through the same deferred handoff as the Radar deck (_claimedHomeOffer + _openClaimedHomeOffer, retried from _scheduleVisibleOffers/didPopNext), and have _openOfferTrip verify that pushSingle actually pushed before clearing state.

verdicts.reason: While an Exclusive reservation claim or an admin-assign claim is pending (_claimReservation at home_reservation.dart:353-371 or _claimAdminAssign at home_offer_radar.dart:843-860), nothing stops Home from being covered. The Home Scaffold (home.dart:711-716) sets `drawer:` and does not disable drawerEnableOpenDragGesture; only accept_ride.dart:1120 turns it off. The drawer items call pushSingle(rootNavigator: true) (side_menu.dart:47-48). didPushNext (home.dart:174) runs _pauseHomeUpdates, and that uses _cancelAllOfferTimers(preserveClaim: true), which does not touch _outsideRadarOffer. So when the claim resolves, the guard `_outsideRadarOffer?.id != offer.id` still passes. On success, ScheduledRideStore.take(offer.id) removes the request without adding it to accepted (scheduled_rides.dart:589-598), wonId is set, and _openOfferTrip calls pushSingle(context, ...). pushSingle returns early because `ModalRoute.of(context)?.isCurrent == false` (single_route_entry.dart:11-13). The post-frame callback in _openOfferTrip then clears _outsideRadarOffer anyway. On return, didPopNext (home.dart:176-186) only restores a persisted active ride, and none was persisted because AcceptRide never ran. The Radar deck path has a retry that these paths lack: _openClaimedHomeOffer checks _liveVisible and is retried from _scheduleVisibleOffers. The demo claim takes 1.45 s (demo_dispatch_repository.dart:162) and the API claim is a network round trip, so the window is short but real.

confirmed.title: Native: the map padding switches between the 75% driving anchor and the plain top inset the instant a pan is reported or recenter starts, which the SDK realizes as an immediate content shift under the finger and a snap at the start of the 'no snap' recenter flight
confirmed.description: On native the 75% vehicle anchor is realized through `GoogleMap.padding` (`drivingInsets(... following:)` returns a top inset of `2*desired - height + bottom`, roughly 520 px on an 800 px screen with a 260 px top and 120 px sheet, versus 260 px when not following). `accept_ride.dart:1227-1234` passes `following: _camera.isGuidance && _camera.mode == DriverCameraMode.following`. `onUserGesture` (`accept_ride.dart:1242`) runs `_rebuild(_camera.userGesture)`, so on the first 6 px of a drag the widget rebuilds with the smaller top padding; Android `setPadding` and iOS `GMSMapView.padding` keep the camera target lat/lng and re-centre it in the new padded region, i.e. the map content jumps by about (520-260)/2 = 130 px while the driver's finger is on it. On recenter the padding flips back before the eased 1 s flight (`google_driver_camera_port.dart:102-106` documents the flight as landing with no snap), so the flight starts with an instant jump. The web path is guarded (`drivingInsets` returns `edgeInsets` on web and the JS `configure` only pans when `state.anchored`, which `release()` has already cleared); the native path has no equivalent guard. Not executable here (needs a device), hence the modest confidence.
confirmed.failure_scenario: Driver in guidance on Android/iOS starts dragging the map: as soon as the drag registers (6 px) the whole map lurches ~130 px up under the finger; tapping recenter produces an equal downward jump before the smooth flight begins.
confirmed.evidence: map_overlay_insets.dart:25-47: `EdgeInsets drivingInsets(double height, {required bool following}) { if (kIsWeb) { return edgeInsets; } ... final desired = (height * .75).clamp(top + margin, height - bottom - margin); return EdgeInsets.fromLTRB(32, following ? math.max(top, 2 * desired - height + bottom) : top, 32, bottom);`. accept_ride.dart:1227-1234: `padding: MapOverlayInsets.forActiveRide(...).drivingInsets(MediaQuery.sizeOf(context).height, following: _camera.isGuidance && _camera.mode == DriverCameraMode.following), cameraAnchor: ... ? .75 : .5,`. accept_ride.dart:1242: `onUserGesture: () { _rebuild(_camera.userGesture); ...`.
confirmed.suggested_fix: Keep the native padding constant across follow/browse (the anchor is only needed for follow frames, which the port can realize by offsetting the camera target instead), or defer the padding change until the gesture ends and apply it together with the first camera move.

verdicts.reason: On native, the 75% anchor exists only as GoogleMap.padding. drivingInsets (map_overlay_insets.dart:25-43) returns a top inset of max(top, 2*desired-height+bottom) while following and plain `top` otherwise. The web early return at line 26 is the only guard. accept_ride.dart:1230-1235 switches `following` on _camera.mode. onUserGesture (accept_ride.dart:1242) calls _rebuild(_camera.userGesture), which sets the mode to browsing (driver_camera_controller.dart:582-588). recenter (lines 599-607) sets it back to following before the flight starts. Each switch rebuilds CustomGoogleMap with new `padding: widget.padding` (custom_google_map.dart:429). The plugin forwards that straight to googleMap.setPadding (google_maps_flutter_android 2.18.2 GoogleMapController.java:576-578) with no camera compensation. On native, GoogleDriverCameraPort._move (google_driver_camera_port.dart:197-212) only calls moveCamera(target). The web bridge claim/configure does the anchor shift on web only. The Maps SDK keeps the camera target at the centre of the padded region. On an 800 px screen that region's centre moves by (520-260)/2, about 130 px, at drag start, and back at recenter before the 1 s eased flight. Only the visual effect is unconfirmed: it follows from documented SDK padding semantics, not from a device run.
verdicts.repro: Static trace of accept_ride.dart:1227-1250, map_overlay_insets.dart, driver_camera_controller.dart:582-607, google_driver_camera_port.dart:190-290, custom_google_map.dart:290-330/400-460, and the Android plugin's setPadding. verdicts.reason: accept_ride.dart:1230-1235 passes `drivingInsets(height, following: isGuidance && mode == following)` as the map padding. CustomGoogleMap forwards it to GoogleMap.padding (custom_google_map.dart:429) with no smoothing or compensation, and google_driver_camera_port.dart has no knowledge of padding. CustomGoogleMap reports a gesture after 6 px of pointer movement (custom_google_map.dart:368-370). The onUserGesture callback at accept_ride.dart:1242 calls `_rebuild` (accept_ride.dart:499, a synchronous setState) around `_camera.userGesture` (driver_camera_controller.dart:582-589), which sets mode to browsing. Native Maps keep the camera target at the centre of the padded region, so changing the padding without a camera move shifts the content on screen. With safeTop 24 and an 111 px sheet on an 800 px screen, the padded centre moves from y=600 to y=456.5, about 143 px. The web path is guarded (map_overlay_insets.dart:26-28); native is not. confirmed.title: A ride-category choice saved in Ride preferences is not applied to offers after a cold start until the driver reopens Ride preferences
confirmed.description: `DriverCategoryChoice.off` (the set offers are filtered by: home_offer_rules.dart `_offerAllowed`/`_rideAllowed` -> `DriverCategoryChoice.takes`) is only populated by `_publishChoice()` which runs from `_restoreSettings` (line 122) and `_toggle` (line 183) inside the Preferences screen. Nothing reads the `'categories'` settings section at startup: `main.dart` restores only `MapTrafficSetting.restore()` (line 41) and `DriverLanguage.restore()` (line 46); grep shows `read('categories')` exists only in preferences.dart. So the screen says '{n} ride categories saved' and persists the choice, but after a cold start `off` is `const {}` and the driver receives offers of every category they switched off, until they happen to open Ride preferences again.
confirmed.failure_scenario: Driver switches off 'Priority' and 'Comfort' in Ride preferences (snackbar '4 ride categories saved'), kills and relaunches the app, goes online: Priority/Comfort offers appear on Home and in the Live list; reopening Ride preferences shows them correctly off and only then stops the offers.
confirmed.evidence: preferences.dart:171-176 `void _publishChoice() { DriverCategoryChoice.off.value = { for (final index in _visible) if (!_selected[index]) _categories[index].title, }; }` is the only writer; ride_categories.dart `static final ValueNotifier<Set<String>> off = ValueNotifier<Set<String>>(const <String>{});`; main.dart:41 `unawaited(MapTrafficSetting.restore());` / :46 `await DriverLanguage.restore()...` with no categories restore.
confirmed.suggested_fix: Move the restore/publish logic into a `DriverCategoryChoice.restore(SettingsRepository)` and call it from the app root at startup next to MapTrafficSetting/DriverLanguage; Preferences keeps using the same code.

verdicts.reason: The only writer of DriverCategoryChoice.off is Preferences._publishChoice (preferences.dart:171-176). It is called only from _restoreSettings (:122) and _toggle (:183), and both run only while the Preferences screen is open. The notifier starts as const {} (ride_categories.dart:56-57). main.dart:41-49 restores only MapTrafficSetting and DriverLanguage, and nothing else in lib reads the 'categories' section (grep shows read('categories') only at preferences.dart:105). confirmed.title: Logout clears the saved category preferences but leaves the in-memory offer filter, so the next session filters offers by the previous driver's choice
confirmed.description: Logout runs `runtime.logout` (main.dart:180-193) which calls `clearLocalUserData()` (removes every `movera_driver_settings_section_*` key incl. 'categories') and resets `MapTrafficSetting` and `DriverLanguage`, but never calls `DriverCategoryChoice.reset()`. `DriverCategoryChoice.off` therefore keeps the switched-off set after logout and 'Return to demo'. Home's `_startAccount` only listens to the notifier, so offers of those categories stay hidden while a reopened Preferences screen shows all categories on (storage was cleared) and only then republishes an empty set. LOCAL_DATA.md says logout removes settings; this derived state survives.

verdicts.reason: _MoveraAppState._logout (main.dart:180-194) clears local data and resets MapTrafficSetting, DriverLanguage, the waybills, dispatch, safety alerts and the session.
