confirmed.title: System Back while a Radar claim is in flight unmounts Radar and drops a won trip (the on-screen Back is covered by the Matching banner)
confirmed.description: `_claimTrip` awaits `claimOffer` and then returns if `!mounted` (line 322) without handling the result. The Back button (`_closeRides`, line 270-282) stays enabled during Matching, and Home unmounts `RideRequests` on close (`showRideRequests = false`, home.dart:759-765, the whole Stack is replaced). `DemoDispatchRepository.claimOffer` removes the offer from the feed on success (line 565-566) and there is no other path that opens the accepted trip. So a Back tap during the ~1.45 s claim delay loses the trip: it is assigned (server side) but the driver never sees AcceptRide, and the card is gone from Radar when reopened.
confirmed.failure_scenario: Driver taps Match, changes their mind and taps Back within a second, then reopens Radar: the trip is no longer listed (claim succeeded and removed it) and no active trip exists on this phone, while dispatch considers it accepted.
confirmed.evidence: line 318 `result = await _dispatch.claimOffer(trip.id);` — line 322 `if (!mounted || _matchingOfferId != trip.id) { return; }` — line 567 (demo_dispatch_repository.dart) `_removeOffer(offerId); return ClaimResult.success(offer);` — home.dart:759-763 `onCloseRides: (hasOffers) { setState(() { showRideRequests = false; ...` (RideRequests is a child of the conditional Stack)
confirmed.suggested_fix: Disable Back while `_matchingOfferId != null`, or hand a successful claim result to Home (callback/repository) so the active trip opens even when the Radar sheet has been closed.

verdicts.corrected_title: System Back while a Radar claim is in flight unmounts Radar and drops a won trip (the on-screen Back is covered by the Matching banner)
verdicts.reason: The finding's mechanism is right but the trigger is misdescribed. The header Back button cannot be tapped during Matching because the match notice is Positioned at top:0 over the header (ride_requests.dart:530-536), and the hit test lands on the banner. System Back does reach it, though: Home's PopScope has canPop false while showRideRequests is true (home_back.dart:27-28), and _closeTopOverlay sets showRideRequests=false (home_back.dart:57-58). That swaps the body branch at home.dart:717 and unmounts RideRequests. RideRequests has no PopScope of its own and no guard on _matchingOfferId. Home's shared _dispatch is not disposed, so claimOffer still runs to completion. demo_dispatch_repository.dart:565-566 removes the offer and returns success. _claimTrip then returns at ride_requests.dart:322 on !mounted and drops the result. No other caller consumes it.

verdicts.corrected_title: System Back (or any Home close of Radar) during a pending Radar claim loses a won trip
verdicts.reason: The trip loss is real, but the trigger in the finding is wrong. During Matching the on-screen Back button cannot be tapped: the match banner is Positioned top:0 over the header (ride_requests.dart:528-534, TripStatusBanner is about 66px tall plus pad.top) and covers the Back button. confirmed.title: A withdrawal of another offer cancels the won-match timer: the claimed trip never opens and Radar is stuck in Matching
confirmed.description: `_resolveMatchWon` (line 351-418) keeps the AcceptRide push on `_matchNoticeTimer` (500 ms). `_resolveMatchLost` (line 435) unconditionally does `_matchNoticeTimer?.cancel()` for any trip, and `_onWithdrawn` (line 181-189) calls it for every `claimedElsewhere` withdrawal whose trip is still `available`. If dispatch withdraws trip B while trip A's win timer is pending, the timer is cancelled: `navigator.push(ActiveRideTransition(ride))` never runs, `_matchingOfferId` stays A (line 437 only clears it when it equals B), `_offerStates[A]` stays `resolving`, so A's card shows the spinner forever and every other card's Match is disabled (`blockOtherOffers`, line 724-725). The server already removed A from the feed (`DemoDispatchRepository.claimOffer` line 565-566), so the trip is lost. Reproduced: match A, complete claim with success, pump 100 ms, emit `OfferWithdrawal(offerId: 'b', reason: claimedElsewhere)`, pump 2 s → `AcceptRide mounted: false; matching text: 1`. The demo fires `withdrawOffer(radarGroupTaken)` on its own timer (demo_dispatch_repository.dart:710-714), so the window is real, and a backend's `offer_withdrawn` can arrive at any moment.
confirmed.failure_scenario: Driver taps Match on a Radar trip, dispatch answers success; within half a second another driver's accept withdraws a different card. The 'Matched' banner is replaced by 'Taken by another driver', no trip screen opens, the matched card spins forever, and no other trip can be matched until the driver closes and reopens Radar. The accepted trip is gone from the server feed.
confirmed.evidence: line 366-368 `_matchNoticeTimer = Timer(const Duration(milliseconds: 500), () { ... navigator.push(ActiveRideTransition(ride));` — line 435 `_matchNoticeTimer?.cancel();` in `_resolveMatchLost` — line 181-187 `void _onWithdrawn(OfferWithdrawal gone) { ... _resolveMatchLost(trip, _RadarGone.lostOwnMatch, notice: shown);` — test: `AcceptRide mounted: false; matching text: 1`
confirmed.suggested_fix: Use a separate timer for the won-match navigation (or push immediately and keep only the banner on a timer), and never let `_resolveMatchLost` for another offer touch the win timer; also ignore withdrawals while `_matchingOfferId` names a won trip.

verdicts.reason: _resolveMatchWon puts the AcceptRide push on _matchNoticeTimer (500 ms, ride_requests.dart:366). _onWithdrawn (ride_requests.dart:181-189) calls _resolveMatchLost for any other offer that is still 'available' and visible, with notice=true, and that cancels _matchNoticeTimer unconditionally (ride_requests.dart:435). Nothing re-arms the push. _matchingOfferId stays on the won trip because line 437 only clears it for the lost id, so the other cards stay blocked (lines 724-725). The demo fires withdrawOffer on its own timer (demo_dispatch_repository.dart:710-714).

confirmed.title: Reservation claim that succeeds after the list unmounts is lost and later reported 'No longer available'

ClaimResult.success(reservation); }`

confirmed.title: ReservationRequestPreview.pickupAt is one hour off on daylight-saving switch days (adds minutes as absolute Duration to local midnight)
confirmed.description: `pickupAt` builds the pickup instant as `DateTime(y, m, d + offset).add(Duration(minutes: minuteOfDay))`. `DateTime.add` adds absolute time, so when the 'Today'/'Tomorrow' date is a DST transition day in the zone (Sweden/France: last Sunday of March and October) the wall-clock result is shifted by an hour relative to the 'HH:mm' label. Reproduced with `TZ=Europe/Stockholm`: for 'Tomorrow 07:40' on 24 Oct 2026 the code yields 2026-10-25 06:40 (untilPickup 11h40 instead of 12h40); on 28 Mar 2026 it yields 08:40 (untilPickup 11h40 instead of 10h40). `untilPickup`, the 'leave now'/'go online for' island timers (home_scheduled.dart:94-131, 321-342), the Scheduled-rides sort (scheduled_rides.dart:630-632) and `SmartGap` clash detection (smart_gap.dart:67-68) all consume this value.
confirmed.failure_scenario: On Sunday 25 Oct 2026 (DST ends) a driver has a reservation 'Today 07:40'. The island says 'Leave now' and the reminder fires an hour early (06:40), and the countdown reads 1 h less than the clock; on 29 Mar it is an hour late, so 'leave now' appears after the pickup time.
confirmed.evidence: driver_home_admin_content.dart:244-245 `return DateTime(now.year, now.month, now.day + offset)\n        .add(Duration(minutes: minute));` · scratch run output: `Tomorrow 07:40 (DST ends 25 Oct): pickupAt()=2026-10-25 06:40:00.000 expected=2026-10-25 07:40:00.000` / `(DST starts 29 Mar): pickupAt()=2026-03-29 08:40:00.000 expected=07:40`
confirmed.suggested_fix: Construct the wall-clock time directly: `DateTime(now.year, now.month, now.day + offset, minute ~/ 60, minute % 60)`.

verdicts.reason: driver_home_admin_content.dart:244-245 builds DateTime(y,m,d+offset).add(Duration(minutes: minuteOfDay)), which adds absolute time to local midnight. confirmed.title: Corrupt-record warnings log the raw stored JSON (rider names, addresses, free-text notes) through FormatException.toString()
confirmed.description: `DriverLogRecord` documents that messages 'must not contain rider names, phone numbers or free text' (driver_log.dart:5-6), and the default sink prints to the console in release builds too (`debugPrint`, driver_log.dart:42). Several readers interpolate the `FormatException` thrown by `jsonDecode` into the message. Dart's `FormatException.toString()` appends a window of the `source` string around the failing offset, so the log line carries whatever personal data sits near the corruption. Verified with a dart script: `jsonDecode` of a truncated history blob logged `...:"Angelica Holm","pickup":"Sveavägen 12, Stockholm","phone":"+46701234567"` under 'History JSON malformed:'. Affected in-scope sites: history (`prefs_trip_history_repository.dart:88`, rider names/addresses), ride-check log (`ride_check_log.dart:104`, includes the driver's 'What happened' free text and answers), and settings (`settings_repository.dart:84` builds `reason: '$storageKey: $error'` which `local_quarantine.dart:62` logs; settings sections hold trusted-contact phone numbers and vehicle drafts). The same pattern exists in `prefs_active_ride_repository.dart:81` (out of scope) via `DriverLog.error(..., error, stack)` which the sink prints verbatim.
confirmed.failure_scenario: A localStorage write is cut off mid-blob (web quota, process kill). On the next History open the console/crash log receives 'WARN History JSON malformed: FormatException: Unexpected end of input (at character N) ..."riderName":"Angelica Holm","pickup":"Sveavägen 12...' — rider PII in a log that is meant to be shippable to a crash reporter.
confirmed.suggested_fix: Log only `error.message` (and offset) for FormatException, never `$error`/`error.toString()`; in `DriverLog._debugSink` scrub `FormatException.source` before printing so no sink can leak stored blobs.

verdicts.reason: prefs_trip_history_repository.dart:88 logs '$error' for a jsonDecode FormatException. On the Dart VM (Android/iOS), FormatException.toString() includes the source text around the offset. DriverLog._debugSink (lib/core/logging/driver_log.dart) prints it through debugPrint, which also reaches the console and logcat in release builds. That breaks the class's own rule that log messages must not contain rider names or free text (driver_log.dart:5-6). The same pattern is at ride_check_log.dart:104 and settings_repository.dart:84, which feeds local_quarantine. It needs a corrupt stored blob to trigger, so it is an edge path. On web, dart2js builds the FormatException from the JS SyntaxError message, which may include less of the source.
verdicts.repro: Throwaway test test/_audit_d16_test.dart (deleted) seeded SharedPreferences with a truncated history blob and called PrefsTripHistoryRepository().list() with a capturing DriverLog.sink. It logged: 'History JSON malformed: FormatException: Unterminated string (at character 90) ...n":1,"rows":[{"riderName":"Angelica Holm","pickup":"Sveavagen 12","note":"x'. Result: All tests passed.

verdicts.reason: prefs_trip_history_repository.dart:86-88 catches the jsonDecode error and logs `'History JSON malformed: $error'`. The default sink (driver_log.dart:33-43) prints it with debugPrint, which also runs in release builds. This breaks the rule at driver_log.dart:5-6 that messages carry no rider names or phone numbers. Nothing scrubs the text first. Limits: dart2js on web builds the FormatException without the source, and the default sink is only console or logcat, so for now this is a local-log privacy issue.
verdicts.repro: Same throwaway test: jsonDecode of a truncated history blob, then `DriverLog.warn('History JSON malformed: $error')`. Output: `[movera] WARN History JSON malformed: FormatException: Unexpected end of input (at character 114)\n...":"Angelica Holm","pickup":"Sveavagen 12, Stockholm","phone":"+46701234567"`. confirmed.title: The 'same fix reported again' guard compares the route by identity, so every route refresh/reroute resolves the same GPS fix twice and doubles the per-fix zoom, speed and bearing smoothing steps
confirmed.description: `update()` returns early only when `identical(location, _location) && identical(route, _route) && ...`. The trip calls `_camera.update(location, route: _navigation.route)` in `_applyDriverPosition` (`accept_ride_trip.dart:665`) and again from `_followVehicle()` after `_refreshRoadRoute()` (`accept_ride_trip.dart:731`). Whenever that refresh produced a new `RoadRoute` object (every 90 s silent refresh, every reroute, and `NavigationController.ensureRoute` always allocates a new `RoadRoute` at line 404), the second call passes the identity check and `DriverCameraPolicy.resolve` runs twice for one fix: `_smoothedSpeed` applies its 0.3 blend twice, `_cruiseZoom` may step up to 2×0.25 out / 2×0.4 in instead of once, and the bearing damping at lines 320-323 applies 0.65 of the remaining delta twice. The guard's own comment states the intent: 'Resolving it twice would smooth the turn twice.'
confirmed.failure_scenario: During a reroute mid-turn the camera rotates and zooms with a visibly bigger single step than on other fixes (e.g. zoom 0.5 instead of 0.25 in one frame), the exact effect the guard was written to prevent.
confirmed.evidence: driver_camera_controller.dart:550-557: `// The trip reports the same fix again once its route refresh is done. // Resolving it twice would smooth the turn twice. if (identical(location, _location) && identical(route, _route) && navigating == _navigating && waiting == _waiting) { return; }`. accept_ride_trip.dart:728-734: `Future<void> _followVehicle({bool force = false}) async { final location = _lastLocation; ... _camera.update(location: location, route: _navigation.route, ...`. navigation_controller.dart:404: `_route = RoadRoute(points: List<GeoPoint>.unmodifiable(route.points), ...`.
confirmed.suggested_fix: When only the route changed for an already-resolved location, update the policy's route/geometry without re-running the speed, zoom and bearing smoothing (e.g. resolve with `immediate: false` but skip the smoothing when `identical(location, _location)`).

verdicts.reason: The guard at driver_camera_controller.dart:550-557 needs identical(route, _route). After _applyDriverPosition calls update (accept_ride_trip.dart:665), _refreshRoadRoute -> ensureRoute allocates a new RoadRoute whenever it fetches (navigation_controller.dart:404), and _followVehicle (accept_ride_trip.dart:728-731) calls update again with the same location. DriverCameraPolicy.resolve then re-runs speed smoothing, the cruise-zoom step and the 0.65 bearing damping (:320-323) for the same fix. This happens only on fetched refreshes and reroutes; an unchanged route stays identical and is caught by the guard.
verdicts.repro: Same throwaway test, resolving a policy once versus twice for the same fix (heading 0 -> 90). Output: '21: once bearing 35.75 zoom 14.5; twice bearing 71.0125 zoom 14.5'. The bearing step for that fix doubles; zoom did not change in this case.

verdicts.reason: The guard in update() (driver_camera_controller.dart:550-557) needs identical(route, _route). _applyDriverPosition (accept_ride_trip.dart:665) calls update(location, R0). It then awaits _refreshRoadRoute, and on a silent refresh or reroute NavigationController.ensureRoute sets a new RoadRoute (navigation_controller.dart:404). _followVehicle (accept_ride_trip.dart:731) then calls update(_lastLocation, R1). The fix is the same, the guard is passed, and DriverCameraPolicy.resolve runs a second time. resolve has no per-fix guard of its own, so speed blending, cruise-zoom stepping and the 0.65 bearing damping each run twice. This happens once per route replacement (about every 90 s, or on a reroute), so the visible effect is one larger camera step.
verdicts.repro: Throwaway test test/_audit_cam21_test.dart (deleted). It drives DriverCameraPolicy with a few fixes at 5 m/s, then one fix at 30 m/s, heading 50. Resolving that fix once gives `zoom=14.607 bearing=18.85`. Resolving it again with a new RoadRoute holding the same points gives `zoom=14.357 bearing=25.45`: an extra 0.25 zoom step and an extra 6.6 degree bearing step for one fix.

Neighbouring builders in the same class use tr.* and driverText(...), so these strings were missed rather than left in English on purpose. A Swedish or French driver sees mixed-language cards and an English island popup. The event entry is meant to stand in for admin-authored text, so that one is arguable. The bonus, payout and scheduled-ride body text is app content. The effect is limited to text on the demo feed.
verdicts.repro: Read driver_notifications.dart:100-180 and :320-367. Confirmed that items and arrivals default to these demo lists and that the other notices go through tr/driverText.

confirmed.title: formatDistance chooses the unit before rounding: 999.5-999.99 m shows '1000 m' and 9950-9999 m shows '10.0 km'
confirmed.description: The branch chooses the metre format on the raw value (`meters < 1000`) but prints `meters.round()`, so 999.5..999.99 rounds up to 1000 and is rendered as `1000 m`, while 1000.0 renders as `1.0 km`. This is the live banner distance (`navigation_controller.dart:593` `distanceLabel: RouteInstructionCopy.formatDistance(meters)`), fed every fix with continuous metres from `RouteProgressCalculator`.
confirmed.failure_scenario: Island reads 'Turn left in 1000 m' for one or more fixes just before switching to '1.0 km'/'999 m', an inconsistent unit boundary visible to the driver.
confirmed.evidence: route_instruction.dart:536-545: `if (meters < nowMeters) { return l.navDistanceNow; } if (meters < 1000) { return l.navMeters('${meters.round()}'); } final km = meters / 1000; return l.navKilometers(km.toStringAsFixed(km < 10 ? 1 : 0)...`
confirmed.suggested_fix: Round first (`final rounded = meters.round();`) and branch on the rounded value, or use `meters < 999.5`.

confirmed.title: Ride-check recordings are written to the iOS Documents directory, which is included in iCloud/iTunes backups, contradicting the 'saved only on this phone' permission text
confirmed.description: `start()` saves audio under `getApplicationDocumentsDirectory()/ride_check_audio`. On iOS that is `NSDocumentDirectory`, which Apple backs up to iCloud/Finder by default unless the file is flagged `NSURLIsExcludedFromBackupKey` or stored under Application Support/Caches. `ios/Runner/Info.plist:9-10` tells the user 'The recording is saved only on this phone' and `safety_alert_repository.dart:36` repeats 'recordings stay on the phone'. Cabin audio of riders therefore leaves the device whenever the driver has iCloud backup on, which the stated promise and GDPR expectations do not cover.
confirmed.failure_scenario: Driver with iCloud Backup enabled records a Ride check conversation with a rider; the .m4a is uploaded to Apple's servers with the next device backup although the app told the driver it stays only on the phone.
confirmed.evidence: ride_check_recorder_native.dart:31-33 `final directory = Directory('${(await getApplicationDocumentsDirectory()).path}/ride_check_audio');` · ios/Runner/Info.plist:9-10 `NSMicrophoneUsageDescription` … 'The recording is saved only on this phone.'
confirmed.suggested_fix: Store recordings under `getApplicationSupportDirectory()` and mark the folder excluded from backup (or set `NSURLIsExcludedFromBackupKey` on each file).

verdicts.reason: ride_check_recorder_native.dart:31-37 writes .m4a files to getApplicationDocumentsDirectory()/ride_check_audio. On iOS that folder is included in iCloud/Finder backups by default. Nothing in ios/ or lib/ sets NSURLIsExcludedFromBackupKey (grep found nothing), yet Info.plist:9-10 and the UI ('saved only on this phone', app_en.arb:511/841; ride_check_card.dart:980 'The file never leaves it') say the file stays on the phone. The project clearly means local-only: Android sets allowBackup=false and excludes the whole file domain (AndroidManifest.xml:13-15, res/xml/backup_rules.xml). iOS has no equivalent, and an iOS release build is part of CI (drider-ci.yml:130-149). This does not affect the web/PWA build, where the recorder is a stub.
verdicts.repro: Static check of the recorder path, Info.plist, a grep for backup exclusion across ios/ and lib/, and a comparison with the Android backup rules.

verdicts.reason: ride_check_recorder_native.dart:31-37 writes `<Documents>/ride_check_audio/<id>.m4a`. On iOS this recorder is the one in use: ride_check_recorder.dart:3 picks it under dart.library.io, and `supported` is true when Platform.isIOS. Nothing sets NSURLIsExcludedFromBackupKey (grep of lib/ios finds none). iOS includes Documents in iCloud and Finder backups by default, so the recording leaves the device when the driver's backup is on. That contradicts Info.plist:9-10 ('The recording is saved only on this phone') and safety_alert_repository.dart:36. The effect is real but minor: it applies only to the iOS native build (on the web/PWA the recorder is the unsupported stub), and the copy goes into the driver's own encrypted device backup. The suggested fix is also partly wrong: Library/Application Support is backed up as well. Only setting the exclude-from-backup flag, or using Caches/tmp, keeps the file out.
verdicts.repro: Traced it statically: the conditional import (ride_check_recorder.dart:2-3) leads to NativeRideCheckRecorder.start (native.dart:30-38), which uses the path_provider Documents directory. A grep for excludedFromBackup/isExcludedFromBackup in lib and ios found nothing. Info.plist has no UIFileSharingEnabled. The backup behaviour follows Apple's documented iOS rule that Documents and Library (except Caches) are backed up. I could not run it on a device here.

confirmed.title: NativeRideCheckRecorder never disposes its AudioRecorder, so each trip leaks a native recorder; an empty capture's file is also left on disk
confirmed.description: `stop()` returns null for an empty capture but does not delete the file it just created in `ride_check_audio/` (line 48), so every failed/instant stop leaves an orphan `.m4a` under the app documents folder; nothing in the app ever lists or prunes that directory. Separately, `AudioRecorder` (record 7.1.1 exposes `Future<void> dispose()`, record.dart:173) is created per `RideCheckController` via `services.createRecorder()` (ride_check_controller.dart:234) and neither `NativeRideCheckRecorder` nor `RideCheckController.dispose()` releases it, so each trip in which the driver taps Record leaves a native recorder instance (method-channel/stream subscription) alive.
confirmed.failure_scenario: Driver taps Record then immediately Stop on several trips: each leaves an empty `ride-check-<trip>-<ms>.m4a` in Documents/ride_check_audio (grows forever) and one undisposed native recorder per trip for the life of the process.
confirmed.evidence: ride_check_recorder_native.dart:47-48 `final file = File(path);\n    if (!await file.exists() || await file.length() == 0) return null;` (no delete) · ride_check_recorder_native.dart:15-56 has no `dispose` · ride_check_controller.dart:406-423 `dispose()` never disposes `_recorder` · record-7.1.1/lib/src/record.dart:173 `Future<void> dispose()`
confirmed.suggested_fix: Delete the empty file before returning null; add `dispose()` to `RideCheckRecorder` that calls `AudioRecorder.dispose()` and invoke it from `RideCheckController.dispose()`.

verdicts.reason: lib/core/safety/ride_check_recorder_native.dart:20 lazily builds an AudioRecorder. Its constructor (record-7.1.1/lib/src/record.dart:32-33) registers a native recorder under a UUID, and only dispose() (record.dart:173) releases it. NativeRideCheckRecorder has no dispose, and the RideCheckController that owns it (ride_check_controller.dart:234, created per trip screen) does not release it in dispose() (ride_check_controller.dart:407-423), which only calls stop(). So each trip where the driver taps Record leaves one native recorder alive for the whole process. Also, stop() at ride_check_recorder_native.dart:48 returns null for a missing or zero-byte file without deleting it. Nothing else in lib/ touches ride_check_audio/, and clearLocalUserData (docs/LOCAL_DATA.md) only clears SharedPreferences, so empty .m4a files pile up. Keeping non-empty recordings on the phone is intended (comment at controller:413); the empty files and the never-disposed recorder are not.
verdicts.repro: Static trace: grepped lib/ and docs for ride_check_audio, AudioRecorder and dispose, and read the record 7.1.1 constructor and dispose(). No test was run because native audio is not available headless.

verdicts.corrected_title: NativeRideCheckRecorder never disposes its AudioRecorder, so each trip leaks a native recorder; an empty capture's file is also left on disk
verdicts.reason: The leak is real. RideCheckController creates one recorder per controller at ride_check_controller.dart:234 (`_recorder ??= services.createRecorder()`). Its dispose() at ride_check_controller.dart:407-422 only calls stop() if a recording is running and never releases the recorder. NativeRideCheckRecorder (ride_check_recorder_native.dart:15-56) has no dispose at all. The AudioRecorder constructor (record-7.1.1/lib/src/record.dart:32-40) calls `_platform.create(id)`. On Android that puts a RecorderWrapper, with its event channels, into the `recorders` map (record_android-2.2.0 MethodCallHandlerImpl.kt createRecorder). It only leaves the map through `disposeRecorder` (`recorders.remove`, MethodCallHandlerImpl.kt:98-100), which is reached only from AudioRecorder.dispose() (record.dart:173) or when the plugin detaches. So one native recorder stays alive per trip in which the driver taps Record (requestPermission alone is enough to create it). Second part: stop() at ride_check_recorder_native.dart:47-48 returns null for a zero-length file without deleting it. The plugin's own cleanup (Utils.deleteFile) runs only on cancel (delete=true), never on stop (RecorderController.kt:93). Nothing in lib lists or prunes ride_check_audio (grep finds only line 32), and LOCAL_DATA.md does not cover audio files. The effect is small and has no user-visible failure, so low.
verdicts.repro: I could not run this: it needs the native plugin on a device. I traced it instead: ride_check_controller.dart:234, :274-290 and :407-422; record.dart:32-40, :73-81 and :173-179; record_android MethodCallHandlerImpl.kt create/dispose and RecorderController.kt:93-98 (stop keeps the file, cancel deletes it). A grep for `dispose` and `ride_check_audio` across lib confirms no release path and no pruning. Whether a real device produces a 0-byte .m4a on an instant stop depends on the encoder/muxer. That part is plausible but not reproduced. The undisposed recorder is certain.

confirmed.title: French plurals written as =1{1 ...} render a literal '1 course' / '1 arrêt' for count 0 (gen-l10n maps =1 to the CLDR 'one' slot, which in fr covers 0)
confirmed.description: French grammar uses the singular for 0 and 1 (CLDR 'one' covers 0 and 1 for fr). The ARB strings tripsCount (713), stopsCount (714), riderBags (676), inDaysCount (861), schedRidesHidden (904) and ratingAndRides (1319) are written as `{count, plural, =1{...} other{...}}`, so count 0 selects the 'other' branch and the UI shows '0 courses', '0 arrêts', 'Le passager a 0 bagages', 'dans 0 jours', '0 courses masquées'. The gen-l10n plural rules would do the right thing if the `one` category were used instead of `=1`. The English and Swedish files are fine with =1/other.
confirmed.failure_scenario: French driver opens history with no rides or a reservation with zero stops; the counters read '0 courses' / '0 arrêts' instead of '0 course' / '0 arrêt'.
confirmed.evidence: lib/l10n/app_fr.arb:713 `"tripsCount": "{count, plural, =1{1 course} other{{count} courses}}"`; :714 stopsCount; :676 riderBags; :861 inDaysCount; :904 schedRidesHidden; :1319 ratingAndRides
confirmed.suggested_fix: In app_fr.arb use `one{...}` (CLDR category) instead of `=1{...}` for these keys, or add `=0{0 course}` branches.

verdicts.corrected_title: French plurals written as =1{1 ...} render a literal '1 course' / '1 arrêt' for count 0 (gen-l10n maps =1 to the CLDR 'one' slot, which in fr covers 0)
verdicts.reason: The diagnosis is wrong but the bug is real. gen-l10n compiles `=1{1 course}` to `Intl.pluralLogic(count, one: '1 course', other: ...)` (lib/l10n/app_localizations_fr.dart:2493-2499). The French CLDR rule puts 0 in ONE, so for count 0 the app shows the hard-coded text '1 course', not '0 courses'. Most call sites never pass 0: home.dart:1065 (totalTrips > 0), radar_offer_card.dart:106 (stops <= 0 gives ''), radar_offer_card.dart:236 (riderTrips > 0), document_expiry.dart:199-201 (<=0 and 1 are handled first), trip_island_controller.dart:318 (bags > 0), scheduled_rides.dart:100 (clashing.isNotEmpty). One site has no guard: accept_ride_panel.dart:985 `tr.ratingAndRides(..., widget.riderTrips)`. That value comes from home_offer_radar.dart:953 offer.riderTrips, which is `(json['riderTrips'] as num?)?.toInt() ?? 0` in api_dispatch_repository.dart:71. The contract makes riderTrips optional with minimum 0 (contracts/CONTRACT.md:60, openapi.yaml:5513). So a first-time rider, or an offer without the field, shows a French driver '4.9 ★ · 1 course', which is a wrong number. English and Swedish are fine because their 'one' covers only 1. Fix: use `one{{count} course}` in app_fr.arb instead of the literal '1'.
verdicts.repro: Throwaway test test/_audit_frplural33_test.dart called AppLocalizationsFr().tripsCount, stopsCount, inDaysCount, schedRidesHidden and riderBags with 0, 1 and 2. Output: '0 -> 1 course | 1 arrêt | dans 1 jour | 1 course masquée | Le passager a 1 bagage', '1 -> (same)', '2 -> 2 courses | 2 arrêts | ...'. All tests passed; file deleted. I then traced every call site for count guards.

verdicts.corrected_title: French plurals written as =1{1 ...} make a count of 0 show '1 course' / '1 arrêt' (wrong number); the accept-ride panel can show it for a rider with 0 trips
verdicts.reason: gen-l10n turns `=1{...}` into the `one:` argument of Intl.pluralLogic (lib/l10n/app_localizations_fr.dart:2493-2512: `one: '1 course'`). In CLDR, French puts both 0 and 1 in the 'one' category, so count 0 picks the hard-coded literal '1 course'. The finding claims the result is '0 courses', but it is actually '1 course', which is worse because the number is wrong. Most callers guard against 0: home.dart:1065 (totalTrips > 0), radar_offer_card.dart:106 and :236, trip_island_controller.dart:318 (bags > 0), document_expiry.dart:199 (<=0 and 1 handled separately), and scheduled_rides.dart:100 (clashing.isNotEmpty). One caller has no guard: accept_ride_panel.dart:985 `tr.ratingAndRides(..., widget.riderTrips)`. riderTrips really can be 0: api_dispatch_repository.dart:71 sets `?? 0` when the field is missing, and dispatch_repository.dart:47 and home_offer_radar.dart:108 default to 0. Those values reach AcceptRide through ride_requests.dart:380 and home_offer_radar.dart:953. A brand-new rider shown to a French driver therefore reads '4.9 ★ · 1 course'.
verdicts.repro: Wrote a throwaway test, test/_audit_fr_plural_d33_test.dart, that calls AppLocalizationsFr directly. Output: `n=0 trips=1 course | 4.9 ★ · 1 course | stops=1 arrêt`, `n=1 trips=1 course | ...`, `n=2 trips=2 courses | ...`, then 'All tests passed!'. The test file was deleted afterwards. I traced callers with grep to check which ones guard against 0.

confirmed.title: A failed clearLocalUserData leaves the driver logged in with every long-lived storage repository invalidated (generation already bumped) and no recovery
confirmed.description: `clearLocalUserData()` calls `LocalWriteSession.beginCleanup()` (local_data.dart:114), which increments the generation before any key is removed; every repository instance created earlier (`_activeRide = PrefsActiveRideRepository()` in main.dart:93, the settings/vehicle stores held by open screens) now fails `LocalWriteSession.check` with 'Local session ended; reopen the screen before saving'. If a `prefs.remove` returns false the function throws (local_data.dart:135-137/148-150), `_logout` rethrows before reaching `_activeRide = PrefsActiveRideRepository()` (main.dart:187) and `_session.reset()`, and Profile just shows 'could not clear' and keeps the driver signed in (profile.dart:397-406). From then on active-ride snapshots and terminal markers can no longer be written (every enqueued op logs 'Active-ride storage operation failed'), so crash recovery of a trip silently stops working, and local data is half-cleared, until the process restarts.
confirmed.failure_scenario: On a device where SharedPreferences commit fails for one key (full disk, broken prefs file), the driver taps Log out, sees 'Could not clear local data', continues driving; the next accepted trip is not persisted, so a crash mid-trip comes back to an empty Home.
confirmed.suggested_fix: Recreate the composition-root repositories (and reset the session) in a `finally`, or bump the generation only after the removals succeeded / roll it back on failure.

verdicts.reason: lib/core/storage/local_write_session.dart:13-17: beginCleanup() increments _generation before any key is removed, and endCleanup() (local_data.dart:152-153) only clears _clearing. It never restores the generation. When prefs.remove returns false (local_data.dart:135-137/148-150), clearLocalUserData throws, so main.dart:184 rethrows before the line `_activeRide = PrefsActiveRideRepository()` (main.dart:187) and before `_session.reset()`. Profile catches the error, shows profCouldNotClear and keeps the driver on Profile, logged in (profile.dart:397-406). Every repository created earlier, such as the composition-root PrefsActiveRideRepository (main.dart:93, which DriverHome receives at main.dart:202), now fails LocalWriteSession.check (prefs_active_ride_repository.dart:34, 72, 136 ...). _enqueue logs those failures (lines 52-57), so active-ride snapshots silently stop being saved. The precondition can happen: shared_preferences_android 2.4.11 LegacySharedPreferencesPlugin.java:103 returns `preferences.edit().remove(key).commit()`, which is false when the disk write fails. It is rare, so the severity is low. A later logout retry that succeeds does rebuild the repository.
verdicts.repro: Throwaway test test/_audit_d34_test.dart: created a PrefsActiveRideRepository, called clearLocalUserData(load: a SharedPreferences fake whose remove returns false), then called repo.clear(). Output: 'repo.clear after failed logout: Bad state: Local session ended; reopen the screen before saving', then '+1: All tests passed!'. The file was deleted afterwards.

verdicts.reason: lib/core/storage/local_write_session.dart:13-17 beginCleanup() increments _generation before any key is removed. If a remove fails, lib/core/privacy/local_data.dart:135-137 and 148-150 throw, and the finally block (line 152-153) only resets _clearing; it never rolls the generation back. lib/main.dart:184 then rethrows before line 187 (`_activeRide = PrefsActiveRideRepository()`) and before _session.reset(). profile.dart:397-406 catches the error, shows profCouldNotClear and returns with the driver still signed in, and the existing DriverHome keeps the stale repository from main.dart:93/205. PrefsActiveRideRepository stores _generation at construction (prefs_active_ride_repository.dart:34), and every read, save or clear calls LocalWriteSession.check(_generation), so they now throw. The trigger is real but rare: on Android, shared_preferences_android 2.4.11 LegacySharedPreferencesPlugin.java:103 is `preferences.edit().remove(key).commit()`, which returns false when the disk write fails. The existing test 006 expects this failure but only checks a retry, not instances made before it. A successful retry recreates the repository, so the effect lasts until the driver retries logout or restarts the app.
verdicts.repro: Wrote test/_audit_d34_test.dart: built PrefsActiveRideRepository() and read once, swapped SharedPreferencesStorePlatform.instance for a store whose remove returns false, and expected clearLocalUserData() to throw StateError, which it did. Then the same instance's clear() printed 'clear after failed cleanup: Bad state: Local session ended; reopen the screen before saving' (its read failed the same way). Result: '00:00 +1: All tests passed!'. Test file deleted.

confirmed.title: Disposing AcceptRide while a Ride check is open makes Home call setState during finalizeTree: a debug-only 'widget tree was locked' error, and in debug the held radar offers are not released
confirmed.description: `_AcceptRideState.dispose` calls `_rideCheck.dispose()` (679). `RideCheckController.dispose` calls `_syncGate(false)` (ride_check_controller.dart 409), which, when the gate was held (a Ride check pill/card was open), sets `RideCheckGate.set(false)` → `ValueNotifier` notifies synchronously. Home is still mounted underneath and its listener `_rideCheckGateListener` → `_onRideCheckGate` (home_offer_radar.dart 473-478) runs `_rebuild(() {})`, i.e. `setState` (home.dart 338), from inside another State's `dispose`. State.dispose runs in `BuildOwner.finalizeTree` under `lockState`, where `markNeedsBuild` asserts "setState() or markNeedsBuild() called when widget tree was locked". In debug/profile builds the FlutterError is thrown out of `_rideCheck.dispose()`, so the remainder of `AcceptRide.dispose` (camera, realtime subscription/unsubscribe, timers, animation controllers at 680-700+) never runs, leaking the realtime subscription, the 20 s ride-check ticker already cancelled but `_waitTimer`, `_nextTrip*` timers and the two AnimationControllers (which then also report "disposed with an active Ticker"). Release builds only mark Home dirty and rebuild.
confirmed.failure_scenario: A Ride check card is open (long stop / off-route) when the rider cancels (or admin releases the trip); the trip screen pops. In a debug or profile build the framework reports "setState() or markNeedsBuild() called when widget tree was locked" during finalizeTree and AcceptRide's dispose is cut short, leaving its realtime subscription and timers alive.
confirmed.evidence:
accept_ride.dart 675-679: `void dispose() { RideCheckGate.listenable.removeListener(_onRideCheckGateListener); ... _rideCheck.dispose();`
ride_check_controller.dart 407-409: `void dispose() { _disposed = true; _syncGate(false);` and 400-404: `if (open == _holdsGate) return; _holdsGate = open; RideCheckGate.set(open);`
home_offer_radar.dart 473-475: `void _onRideCheckGate() { if (!mounted || RideCheckGate.open) { return; } _rebuild(() {});`
home.dart 338: `void _rebuild(VoidCallback update) => setState(update);`
confirmed.suggested_fix: Close the gate before the route is popped (e.g. in `_pauseLiveUpdates`/the exit paths) or defer the Home reaction with `WidgetsBinding.instance.addPostFrameCallback`/`scheduleMicrotask` in `_onRideCheckGate`; alternatively have `RideCheckController.dispose` schedule `RideCheckGate.set(false)` asynchronously.

verdicts.corrected_title: Disposing AcceptRide while a Ride check is open makes Home call setState during finalizeTree: a debug-only 'widget tree was locked' error, and in debug the held radar offers are not released
verdicts.reason: The mechanism is real. RideCheckController.dispose calls _syncGate(false), which calls RideCheckGate.set(false) (ride_check_controller.dart:400-409). Home is still mounted underneath (pushSingle, home_offer_radar.dart:940; home.dart:567). Its listener _onRideCheckGate then calls _rebuild(() {}), which is setState (home_offer_radar.dart:473-478), while finalizeTree holds lockState (flutter framework.dart:3357). Element.markNeedsBuild then throws 'called when widget tree was locked' (framework.dart:5387). A real path exists: _leaveAfterAuthoritativeOutcome and _leaveAfterRelease pop the route (accept_ride_trip.dart:371-410), and _pauseLiveUpdates does not close the Ride check. The claimed leak is wrong, though. ValueNotifier.notifyListeners catches the listener's exception and reports it, so the rest of AcceptRide.dispose still runs and nothing leaks. In debug the throw skips _releasePendingRadarOffers() and _maybeShowSoonReservation() for that gate change. Release builds have no assert and behave correctly.
verdicts.repro: Wrote a throwaway test, test/_audit_d36_test.dart (deleted afterwards), using the real RideCheckGate and RideCheckController: a Home whose RideCheckGate listener calls setState, a pushed route that opens a long-stop check (instant) and disposes the controller in dispose(), then pop. Result: takeException() returned 'setState() or markNeedsBuild() called when widget tree was locked. This Home widget cannot be marked as needing to build because the framework is locked.', and the code after c.dispose() still ran (trailingRan=true, gate=false). The test passed.

verdicts.corrected_title: Disposing the trip screen while a Ride check is open makes Home call setState in a locked tree: debug builds report a FlutterError and skip releasing held offers (dispose itself is not cut short)
verdicts.reason: The chain is real. AcceptRide.dispose (accept_ride.dart:679) calls RideCheckController.dispose, which calls _syncGate(false) (ride_check_controller.dart:409). That runs RideCheckGate.set(false), so the ValueNotifier fires Home's listener synchronously (home.dart:261 -> home_offer_radar.dart:473-475), and its _rebuild calls setState while finalizeTree holds the lock. Home is still mounted under the trip route (it pushes AcceptRide with pushSingle, home_offer_radar.dart:941), and the exit paths (accept_ride_trip.dart:389/406/457/1445) pop without closing the Ride check. The claimed leak is wrong, though. ChangeNotifier.notifyListeners catches errors thrown by listeners and reports them, so nothing propagates out of _rideCheck.dispose() and the rest of AcceptRide.dispose still runs. What actually goes wrong: (a) in debug builds the framework reports 'setState() or markNeedsBuild() called when widget tree was locked'; (b) the listener throws at _rebuild, before _releasePendingRadarOffers() and _maybeShowSoonReservation() (home_offer_radar.dart:476-477), so in debug, offers held back during the check are not released at that moment. The lock assert exists only in debug builds, so profile and release builds are unaffected.
verdicts.repro: Throwaway test test/_audit_d36gate_test.dart (deleted). A Home stand-in had the same listener body as home_offer_radar.dart:473-475. It pushed a route whose State owns a real RideCheckController, opened it (instant), then popped the route. Output: 'EXCEPTION: setState() or markNeedsBuild() called when widget tree was locked. This FakeHome widget cannot be marked as needing to build because the framework is locked.' and 'afterRideCheckDispose=true gateOpen=false'. The second line shows the code after _rideCheck.dispose() did run, so there is no leak.

confirmed.title: After 'I've arrived', the pickup route line stays on the map during the wait until the car moves at least 0.4 m (or a GPS snapshot persist fires), because the route-cleared notification is dropped while _stageTransitioning is set
confirmed.description: `_confirmPickupArrival` sets `_stageTransitioning = true` (541) and awaits `transitionTo(waitingForRider)`; the controller's commit notifies `_syncNavigationStage` → `NavigationController.setStage` which clears `_route` and notifies (navigation_controller.dart:163-188). `_onNavigationChanged` returns at once because `_stageTransitioning` is still true (562), so `_roadGeoPoints`/`_routeDurationSeconds` keep the pickup route; the following `_rebuild(() {})` (558) calls `_syncRouteLines()` which redraws that stale route. During waiting `ensureRoute` returns early and `setVehicle` does not notify while the car is parked (moved < 0.4 m, navigation_controller.dart:242-246), so nothing clears it until the car moves. `_routeEtaText` likewise keeps the old duration (`routeFraction` is null → full duration) while waiting.
confirmed.failure_scenario: Driver taps 'I've arrived' at the pickup. The waiting stage starts but the black route line to the pickup (and the old ETA value) remain on the map for the whole wait.
confirmed.evidence: accept_ride_trip.dart:561-562 `void _onNavigationChanged() {\n      if (!mounted || _stageTransitioning) { return; }` ; 547-559 `_waitSeconds = 0; ... if (mounted) { _rebuild(() {}); }\n      _unlockStageAfterFrame();` ; navigation_controller.dart:168 `_route = null;` inside setStage
confirmed.suggested_fix: Do not skip `_onNavigationChanged` during a stage transition (or re-run it in `_unlockStageAfterFrame`), and clear `_roadGeoPoints`/`_routeDurationSeconds` explicitly when entering waiting.

verdicts.reason: _confirmPickupArrival sets _stageTransitioning=true (accept_ride_trip.dart:541). The navigation controller clears the route and notifies on every lifecycle notify: setStage -> _rebuildBanner -> notifyListeners (navigation_controller.dart:163-188, 448-468). Every one of those notifications arrives while the flag is still true: the transition commit, then both notifies of persistNow at :550. _onNavigationChanged drops them (:562). The flag is only cleared in a post-frame callback (:980-983), and nothing replays the cleared route afterwards. TripRouteLines draws whatever _roadGeoPoints holds, whatever the stage (trip_route_lines.dart:23-56; accept_ride.dart:1545). So the pickup route stays on the map until something makes the navigation controller notify again. That is either a fix that moves at least 0.4 m or turns at least 1 degree (navigation_controller.dart:242-246), or the GPS-driven snapshot persist that runs at most every 2 minutes (accept_ride_trip.dart:672-676). With a parked car, or with no GPS callbacks at all, the route stays drawn. The ETA part is overstated: the island receives _routeEtaText, but while waiting it shows the wait clock, and _legFraction returns null when _countingWait (accept_ride.dart:900).
verdicts.repro: I wrote and ran a throwaway widget test, test/_audit_d42route_test.dart (deleted afterwards). Setup: simulatedArrival and externalRouting on, a stub route repository, a fix 50 m from pickup, then a tap on active-ride-arrived-button after expanding the panel. Output: 'before arrive lines=2', 'after arrive lines=2', 'after 10 identical fixes lines=2', 'after 2m jitter fix lines=0', then 'All tests passed!'. The stale polylines survive arrival and identical fixes, and clear only once a fix moves.

The commit notifies _syncNavigationStage, which calls NavigationController.setStage (navigation_controller.dart:163-188): that sets _route = null, and _rebuildBanner calls notifyListeners (navigation_controller.dart:467). _onNavigationChanged then returns early at accept_ride_trip.dart:562, so _roadGeoPoints keeps the old route, and _rebuild at :558 redraws it through _syncRouteLines (:637-638). confirmed.title: DECISIONS.md's '20 m web GPS filter' is not applied: the active ride passes distanceFilter 0 on web, so every browser fix is processed (the per-fix rebuild cost is already handled by D-07)

LocationAccuracy.high : LocationAccuracy.bestForNavigation, distanceFilter: distanceFilterMeters); }`

confirmed.title: A next-trip offer hidden for a Ride check comes back with a new full exclusiveAcceptTime, ignoring the time it was already on screen
confirmed.description: `_onRideCheckGate` (1137-1162) hides an open offer while the Ride check is up and records `_nextTripOfferHeldAt`. After the answer it checks only whether the full lifetime has elapsed since `heldAt` and then calls `_presentOnTripOffer()`, which calls `_armOnTripOfferExpiry()` with `left == null` → `_nextTripOfferDeadline = now + lifetime` (1163-1173). Time already spent before the check (and `_nextTripOfferDeadline`) is ignored, so the rider's offer is held open longer than Dispatch's time to accept; the comment and D-05 say a surviving offer counts down the rest.
confirmed.failure_scenario: Offer shown with 20 s left; a Ride check opens and is answered after 10 s; the offer returns with the full exclusiveAcceptTime again instead of ~10 s.
confirmed.evidence: accept_ride_trip.dart:1157-1161 `if (DateTime.now().difference(heldAt) >= _AcceptRideState._onTripOfferLifetime) { _maybeScheduleOnTripRadarDemoOffer(); return; }\n      _presentOnTripOffer();` ; 1166-1167 `final time = left ?? _AcceptRideState._onTripOfferLifetime;\n      if (left == null) { _nextTripOfferDeadline = _offerNow().add(time); }`
confirmed.suggested_fix: Keep `_nextTripOfferDeadline` when holding and re-arm with `left: deadline - now` (drop the offer when it is <= 0), as `_resumeOnTripOffer` does.

verdicts.reason: _onRideCheckGate (accept_ride_trip.dart:1137-1162) cancels the expiry and stores _nextTripOfferHeldAt=now when a Ride check opens over a visible offer. On the answer, it compares only the time spent held against the full lifetime (:1157), then calls _presentOnTripOffer (:1161). That calls _armOnTripOfferExpiry() with left==null, which resets _nextTripOfferDeadline to now plus the full exclusiveAcceptTime (:1166-1167). The offer is the same one: the same id comes from _uniqueDemoNext (accept_ride.dart:963) or the '-next-destination' id. So the time it was already shown is discarded, and the window can run to about twice Dispatch's accept time plus the check. This contradicts the method's own doc ('comes back if its time has not passed') and the D-05 handling in _resumeOnTripOffer (:158-167), which re-arms with the remaining time. Dispatch is a mock, so the effect is a wrong local countdown, not a server-side acceptance.
verdicts.repro: Static trace of _onRideCheckGate, _presentOnTripOffer and _armOnTripOfferExpiry (accept_ride_trip.dart:1122-1175), compared with _resumeOnTripOffer (:158-167). No test covers this timing: test/widget/ride_check_test.dart is the only test that references RideCheckGate, and it has no lifetime or remaining-time assertions.

verdicts.corrected_title: A next-trip offer hidden for a Ride check comes back with a new full exclusiveAcceptTime, ignoring the time it was already on screen
verdicts.reason: _onRideCheckGate (accept_ride_trip.dart:1137-1162): when the gate opens it cancels _nextTripOfferExpiry and sets _nextTripOfferHeldAt = now (:1144-1145). It does not use _nextTripOfferDeadline. When the gate closes, the only check is now - heldAt >= lifetime (:1157). After that, _presentOnTripOffer (:1161 -> :1131) calls _armOnTripOfferExpiry() with left == null, which sets _nextTripOfferDeadline = now + lifetime and starts a full-length Timer (:1166-1168). The panel countdown is also a fresh TweenAnimationBuilder over the full lifetime (accept_ride_panel.dart:350-353), because the offer widget was removed while scanning. Compare _resumeOnTripOffer (:158-167), which re-arms with deadline - now. The D-05 comment there says 'one with time left counts down the rest', and this path does not do that.
verdicts.repro: Worked by hand from the code. Let L = exclusiveAcceptTime and suppose the offer is shown at t0. A Ride check opens at t0+10 s, so heldAt = t0+10 and the expiry timer is cancelled. It is answered at t0+15 s: 5 s < L, so the offer is shown again and the deadline becomes t0+15+L. Total exposure is L+15 s instead of L. In the worst case the hold lasts just under L, and exposure approaches about 2L plus the time shown before the hold. No guard uses the original deadline.

confirmed.title: Cancelling the current trip with a secured next trip starts the next AcceptRide without destination mode, unlike completion and the journal snapshot
confirmed.description: `_submitTripCancellation` builds the next `AcceptRide` (1394-1414) without `destinationModeActive`, `destinationAddress` or `destinationPosition`, whereas `_completeCurrentTrip` (954-956) passes them and the journal's `next` snapshot (`_snapshotForOffer`, 971-979) stores them. After a driver cancel the next trip therefore runs with destination mode off (no on-the-way filter for next-trip offers, the trip options row shows 'next trips on your way' as off), while a crash restore of that same trip from the journal snapshot would restore destination mode on — the two paths disagree.

              destinationAddress: _destinationAddress,
              destinationPosition: _destinationPosition,`

The constructor defaults destinationModeActive to false (accept_ride.dart:138), and the state reads it only from the widget (accept_ride.dart:471-473), so destination mode is off on the next trip. _completeCurrentTrip passes all three (:954-956). The journal handoff snapshot from the same cancel call, _snapshotForOffer (:971-979 via :1374), stores them, so a crash restore would bring destination mode back on. The two paths disagree. With the mode off, _dropoffFollowsDestination and _onTripRadarOfferForDestination (:1023, :1033) stop filtering next-trip offers to the destination.

confirmed.title: feeSuffix hardcodes 'kr' and a /100 divisor for whole cancel fees, ignoring the Money currency and exponent (latent until a non-SEK cancelFee arrives)
confirmed.description: `feeSuffix(Money? fee)` prints `'${fee.minorUnits ~/ 100} kr'` whenever the amount is a whole number of minor-hundreds, ignoring `fee.currency` and its exponent (Money supports SEK/EUR with exponent 2 and TND with exponent 3; zone_settings maps EUR->FR and TND->TN). Only the non-whole branch uses `fee.formatted`. Callers: reservationCancelled island message (line 60-66), RiderCancelledSheet status line (rider_cancelled_sheet.dart:59-62), ScheduledRideStore.riderCancelled (scheduled_rides.dart:678). The fee is the backend's decision (R15-7) in the zone currency.
confirmed.failure_scenario: In a French zone the backend sends cancelFee {amountMinor: 500, currency: 'EUR'}: the island and the rider-cancelled sheet say '· +5 kr' instead of '· +5,00 €'; for TND 5000 millimes they say '+50 kr' instead of '5,000 DT'.
confirmed.evidence: lib/presentation/driver/home/components/home_island_notices.dart:72-74 `final amount = fee.minorUnits % 100 == 0\n        ? '${fee.minorUnits ~/ 100} kr'\n        : fee.formatted;`
confirmed.suggested_fix: Use `fee.formattedShort` (already drops a zero fraction and keeps the currency symbol/exponent) for both branches.

verdicts.reason: home_island_notices.dart:72-74: when `minorUnits % 100 == 0` the code returns `'${fee.minorUnits ~/ 100} kr'` and ignores `fee.currency` and its exponent. The fee comes off the wire: driver_realtime.dart:179-201 reads `cancelFee` with `Money.fromJson`, and that accepts EUR and TND (money.dart:43, exponents SEK/EUR 2, TND 3). The app is built for more than one zone: driver_app_config.dart:112-116 takes the zone currency from config, and zone_settings.dart:66-67 and 104-105 handle EUR and TND. accept_ride_trip.dart:278/312 passes event.cancelFee to rider_cancelled_sheet.dart:62, which calls feeSuffix. A EUR 500 fee shows as '+5 kr'. A TND 5000-millime fee shows as '+50 kr' (correct is '5,000 DT'), so both the currency and the size are wrong. Money.formattedShort (money.dart) already handles every currency correctly. Severity is low because the main market is SEK (DECISIONS.md P2) and SEK output is correct.
verdicts.repro: Traced feeSuffix's callers (rider_cancelled_sheet.dart:62, home_island_notices.dart:52/61, scheduled_rides.dart:678) back to the realtime wire parsing and the zone currency config. Worked through the integer arithmetic by hand for EUR 500 and TND 5000.

verdicts.reason: The code defect is real but no runtime path reaches it. Every fee that reaches feeSuffix (home_island_notices.dart:67-76) comes from DriverRealtimeEvent.cancelFee or ScheduledRideStore.riderCancelled(fee:). driver_realtime.dart:11 says there is no transport yet. The only event source in the app is MemoryDriverRealtime (accept_ride.dart:592), and no code in lib calls emit(cancelFee: ...). DriverRealtimeEvent.tryParse/fromJson is called only from tests. ScheduledRideStore.riderCancelled (scheduled_rides.dart:674) is also called only from tests, with Money.sek(105). So no fee, and certainly no EUR or TND fee, reaches the island or the RiderCancelledSheet today. It becomes a real bug once a transport delivers a non-SEK cancelFee, and the suggested fix (fee.formattedShort) is right.
verdicts.repro: Ran throwaway test test/_audit_d73_test.dart (since deleted) calling HomeIslandNotices.feeSuffix. EUR 500 gave ' · +5 kr', TND 5000 gave ' · +50 kr' and SEK 10500 gave ' · +105 kr'. So the function ignores the currency, but tracing found no caller in lib that produces a fee (grep of `cancelFee:` and `.riderCancelled(` hits only definitions and tests).

verdicts.reason:
The defect is in the code. lib/presentation/driver/home/components/home_island_notices.dart:72-74 hardcodes `' kr'` and divides by 100 whenever `minorUnits % 100 == 0`. It ignores `fee.currency` and `fee.exponent`, but the other branch uses the currency-aware `fee.formatted`, so the function contradicts itself. The input type allows other currencies. Contract v0.3 (docs/DECISIONS.md, "Contract v0.3": Money JSON with exponents SEK/EUR 2, TND 3) and money.dart:43 accept EUR and TND. DriverRealtimeEvent.fromJson (driver_realtime.dart:179-201) parses them from the wire. The app also ships a French locale and test fixtures for the FR-PC and TN-TC zones.

The code sits on a live chain in lib, not dead code. accept_ride.dart:594 subscribes the realtime stream. accept_ride_trip.dart:278 and :312 pass `event.cancelFee` to `_handleRiderCancelled`. From there it goes to `riderCancelledWithFee` (:455) and `showRiderCancelledSheet` (:461 to rider_cancelled_sheet.dart:62), and both call feeSuffix.

The reproducer is right that nothing in lib produces a fee today. There is no transport (driver_realtime.dart:11), MemoryDriverRealtime is the only source, and nothing calls `emit(cancelFee:)` or `ScheduledRideStore.riderCancelled`. That is true of every backend-fed path in this demo frontend (REVIEW_AND_MERGE_GATES.md:45), so it does not make a wrong consumer of a contract-typed value correct. No decision document records SEK-only formatting for Money values. The "Other trip models still carry SEK labels (follow-up)" note covers string-typed trip fields, not Money values. DECISIONS P2 (SEK market) explains why the severity is low, not why this would be intended. The bug is latent and only shows for non-SEK fees, while SEK output is correct, so severity is low.
verdicts.repro:
Ran a throwaway test, test/_audit_d62_decide_test.dart, since deleted. It confirmed DriverRealtimeEvent.tryParse accepts `cancelFee: {amountMinor: 500, currency: 'EUR'}`, giving parsed fee EUR 500. It then called HomeIslandNotices.feeSuffix and compared the result with Money.formattedShort:
EUR 500: feeSuffix=" · +5 kr", formattedShort="5 €"
TND 5000: feeSuffix=" · +50 kr", formattedShort="5 DT"
SEK 10500: feeSuffix=" · +105 kr", formattedShort="105 kr"
SEK 10550: feeSuffix=" · +105,50 kr", formattedShort="105,50 kr"
Result: "All tests passed!" The wire accepts the non-SEK fee and feeSuffix gets both the currency and the amount wrong for it. Using `fee.formattedShort` in both branches gives the correct output.

Over a long online session (online/offline, matching, waiting tips are not posted here, but every match/taken/unavailable/cash/reminder/notification message is) the list keeps growing and keeps old State closures alive.

confirmed.title: _activateDestinationMode calls _goOnline() after its awaits without re-checking that destination mode is still active, so a driver who went offline or turned the destination off during the route fetch is put online
confirmed.description: After the synchronous setup, `_activateDestinationMode` awaits `_refreshDestinationRoadRoute()` (a network road-route request) and `_fitDestinationRoute()` (341-342) and then unconditionally runs `_seedDemoDestinationTrips()`, `_maybeShowSoonReservation()` and `if (!_isOnline && !_isGoingOnline) { _goOnline(); }` (343-348). The inner helpers guard themselves, but `_goOnline` (home.dart 884-930) has no `mounted` check and calls `showDriverSuspendedSheet(context)`, `setState(...)`, `_startDriverLocation` and arms timers. If the driver turned the destination off during the fetch (island → details sheet → "Turn off destination" → `_endDestinationMode`, or the admin time limit timer at 313-318 fired) the driver is still switched online because of a destination that no longer exists; if Home was disposed during the await, `setState`/`context` are used after dispose.
confirmed.failure_scenario: Driver confirms a destination, the road-route request is slow, and within those seconds they open the island sheet and tap "Turn off destination". The route request returns, and `_goOnline()` flips the driver online (radar starts, offers arrive) although destination mode is off and they never asked to go online.
confirmed.evidence:
home_map_sheet.dart 341-348: `await _refreshDestinationRoadRoute(); await _fitDestinationRoute(); _seedDemoDestinationTrips(); _HomeOfferRadar(this)._maybeShowSoonReservation(); if (!_isOnline && !_isGoingOnline) { _goOnline(); }`
home.dart 884-887: `void _goOnline() { if (_driverSession.isSuspended) { IslandMessages.show(...); unawaited(showDriverSuspendedSheet(context)); return; }` (no mounted guard)
confirmed.suggested_fix: After the awaits add `if (!mounted || !_destinationModeActive || _destinationPosition != destination) { return; }` before seeding/going online (the same guard `_fitDestinationRoute` already uses at 404-406).

verdicts.corrected_title: _activateDestinationMode calls _goOnline() after its awaits without re-checking that destination mode is still active, so a driver who went offline or turned the destination off during the route fetch is put online
verdicts.reason: In home_map_sheet.dart:341-347, after `await _refreshDestinationRoadRoute(); await _fitDestinationRoute();` the function runs `if (!_isOnline && !_isGoingOnline) { _goOnline(); }` with no check of mounted or _destinationModeActive. The OSRM request has an 8 s timeout (road_route_service.dart:29,96). CoalescingMapRouteRefresh.cancelPending (coalescing_map_route_refresh.dart:41-43) only drops queued work, so the running await still completes. Path 1: an online driver sets a destination and taps Go offline during the fetch. _goOffline (home.dart:939-964) sets online false and clears destination mode. When the fetch returns, the inner helpers bail out on their own guards, but _goOnline() (home.dart:884+, no mounted or destination guard) switches the driver back online and offers start. Path 2: an offline driver turns the destination off (_endDestinationMode, home_map_sheet.dart:473-490) during the fetch and is still put online. Only _seedDemoDestinationTrips guards itself (440-443). The window is the length of the network request, so this is an edge path, but the result is that the driver is put online against their action.
verdicts.repro: Static trace: _activateDestinationMode (301-348), _fetchLatestDestinationRoadRoute and its ownership guards (352-393), _fitDestinationRoute early return (395-408), CoalescingMapRouteRefresh.request and cancelPending, _goOffline (home.dart:939-964) and _goOnline (home.dart:884-930).

verdicts.reason: After the awaits in _activateDestinationMode (home_map_sheet.dart:341-348), nothing checks again whether destination mode is still on before calling _goOnline(). _endDestinationMode (home_map_sheet.dart:473-490) cancels only the queued refresh (cancelPending), not the fetch already running (coalescing_map_route_refresh.dart:38-42). So request() still completes, up to the 8 s RoadRouteService timeout (road_route_service.dart:29). _fitDestinationRoute and _seedDemoDestinationTrips return early on their own guards, but `if (!_isOnline && !_isGoingOnline) _goOnline();` runs anyway, and _goOnline (home.dart:884-935) has no destination or mounted guard. While offline, the island middle opens the destination details sheet during that window (home_map_sheet.dart:1105), and its 'Turn off destination' button calls _endDestinationMode (destination_island.dart:186-189). Result: a driver who started destination mode while offline and then turned it off during the route request is switched online anyway. The 'Home disposed' variant is speculative, because Home is the root screen.
verdicts.repro: Throwaway widget test test/_audit_d66dest_test.dart (deleted), built from test/widget/destination_mode_route_refresh_test.dart with a fake route repository that takes 3 s. Steps: real DriverHome, driver offline, open the picker, pick Solna, confirm. After 0.6 s, tap 'last-trip-launcher' (destination details) and then 'destination-mode-end'. Output: 'after turn off posted=[]' and then 'after fetch posted=[Radar online]'. The HomeIslandNotices.online message comes from _goOnline after destination mode had been turned off.

confirmed.title: Re-showing the Exclusive offer already on screen restarts its countdown; the demo _directOfferTimer re-fires on every resume, so returning from any route resets the offer's time to the full lifetime (contradicts the D-04/R13-3 "time left" rule)
confirmed.description: _showOutsideRadarOffer lets an offer whose id equals the current _outsideRadarOffer through its guard (232) and then cancels _outsideOfferTimeoutTimer and calls _raiseExclusive → _startExclusiveClock, which resets the clock to 1 and the deadline to now+lifetime (251-259, home_exclusive.dart:89-93). _resumeHomeUpdates (home.dart:204-213) first restores the time left via _resumeOfferTimers → _resumeExclusiveTimeout, but it also calls _scheduleVisibleOffers, which re-arms _directOfferTimer (2.2 s) to show the demo Exclusive again (1175-1189). If the same offer is still up (e.g. the driver dismissed the Go-offline dialog, or came back from Ride history inside the 15 s), 2.2 s later its ring and pill jump back to 15 s. _seedDemoDestinationTrips (home_map_sheet.dart:458-466) and _releasePendingRadarOffers → _pendingAdminAssign have the same re-show shape.
confirmed.failure_scenario: Exclusive offer shows 9 s left; driver long-presses the radar, gets "Go offline?", taps "Stay online". The offer resumes at ~8 s, then 2.2 s later jumps back to 15 s and the Q16 miss clock runs again from scratch.

confirmed.suggested_fix: In _showOutsideRadarOffer return early when `_outsideRadarOffer?.id == offer.id` (the offer is already up), so only a new offer starts a clock.

verdicts.reason: _showOutsideRadarOffer lets the offer already on screen through its guard (`_outsideRadarOffer!.id != offer.id`, home_offer_radar.dart:232). It then cancels the timeout and calls _raiseExclusive -> _startExclusiveClock, which resets the clock and deadline to the full lifetime (251-259, home_exclusive.dart:89-93), and it arms a full-lifetime miss timer (275-282). _resumeHomeUpdates first restores the time left (_resumeOfferTimers -> _resumeExclusiveTimeout, home_exclusive.dart:98-120). But _scheduleVisibleOffers (home.dart:208) has already re-armed the 2.2 s demo _directOfferTimer (home_offer_radar.dart:1175-1189), and that timer re-shows the same _veryCloseDirectOffer. So every resume while the Exclusive offer is up resets its countdown to 15 s.
verdicts.repro: Throwaway widget test (now deleted). Go online, let the Exclusive offer show, pump 6 s, send AppLifecycleState.paused then resumed, and read ExclusiveRequestSheet.secondsLeft. Output: `shown left=15`, `after 6s left=9`, `resumed left=8`, `resumed+3s left=14`, `resumed+11s left=6`. The offer was still up about 20 s after it first appeared. `All tests passed!`

verdicts.reason: On resume, _resumeHomeUpdates (home.dart:204-213) calls _scheduleVisibleOffers. The guard at 232 only blocks a different id, so the same offer passes. The code at 251-259 then cancels the timeout and calls _raiseExclusive, and _startExclusiveClock (home_exclusive.dart:89-93) resets the clock to the full lifetime with a new deadline. This undoes the time-left restore that _resumeExclusiveTimeout had just applied (home_exclusive.dart:97-121).

confirmed.title: On first open, Profile shows 'Vehicle data unavailable' until primaryIdentity() resolves
confirmed.description: The Vehicles link detail is `snapshot.data?.vehicle ?? tr.vehicleDataUnavailable` with no check of `snapshot.connectionState`. `primaryIdentity()` is async (SharedPreferences read through the serialized settings queue), so every open of Profile first paints the error text 'Vehicle data unavailable' and then replaces it with the vehicle name; after `_vehicleChanged` the same flash repeats. The same text is meant for the read-failure case (`primaryIdentity` returns null on error).

verdicts.corrected_title: On first open, Profile shows 'Vehicle data unavailable' until primaryIdentity() resolves
verdicts.reason: On first build, the FutureBuilder at profile.dart:156-166 has no initialData, and primaryIdentity() is asynchronous (local_vehicle_store.dart:100-114). So snapshot.data is null and the row shows tr.vehicleDataUnavailable, the same text used when the read fails, until the future completes. The finding's second claim is wrong: on _vehicleChanged or _openPage (profile.dart:38-43, 61-64), FutureBuilder.didUpdateWidget uses _snapshot.inState(ConnectionState.none), which keeps the previous data (flutter widgets/async.dart:619). The vehicle name therefore stays visible during a refresh and nothing flashes again.
verdicts.repro: Read profile.dart:25-64 and 156-166, and FutureBuilder in /opt/flutter/packages/flutter/lib/src/widgets/async.dart:605-619 and 665. The first build has no data, and later future swaps keep the data.

verdicts.corrected_title: Profile's Vehicles row briefly shows 'Vehicle data unavailable' on every open before the identity loads
verdicts.reason: profile.dart:162 uses `snapshot.data?.vehicle ?? tr.vehicleDataUnavailable` with no initialData and no connectionState check. `primaryIdentity()` (local_vehicle_store.dart:100) is async, so the first frame always shows the error text, and this happens during the RightToLeftTransition entry. The claimed repeat after `_vehicleChanged` does not happen. When FutureBuilder gets a new future, it calls `_snapshot.inState(waiting)` (flutter/widgets/async.dart:619,665), and inState keeps the previous data (:280-281). So only the initial open flashes.

verdicts.reason: Cancelled and no-show trips do go into history with a completedAt. Both archive callers set one: PrefsTripHistoryRepository.archive defaults `completedAt ?? DateTime.now()` (prefs_trip_history_repository.dart:188), and they are called from accept_ride_sheet.dart:273 (the next trip is cancelled and sent back to dispatch) and completion_journal.dart:170 (any terminal status). So _periodRidesList (ride_history.dart:99-111) includes them. But _periodRides (line 145) counts only TripStatus.completed, and that number feeds the Rides metric (line 330) and the All rides header (line 448, '{n} rides in {period}'). Meanwhile the 'View all N rides' button (line 403) uses _periodRidesList.length, the Latest rides cards (392) show any status, and the 'No completed rides' text (390) appears only when the whole list is empty. A period with only cancelled trips therefore shows 'Rides 0', two cancelled cards, 'View all 3 rides', and '0 rides in Last 7 days' above three cards. No document records this split as intended.
verdicts.repro: Static trace of ride_history.dart:60-160 and 304-460, the archive callers and their completedAt default, and the app_en.arb strings (lines 875-885).

verdicts.reason: _periodRidesList (ride_history.dart:99-111) contains every record with a completedAt. confirmed.title: On web, if the Maps JavaScript script is blocked or fails to load, every CustomGoogleMap stays a plain land-colour box with no 'map unavailable' message (the poll is cancelled on dispose)
confirmed.description: On web `_mapsReady` starts as `web.ready`, which is false until `google.maps` is installed by driver_map_camera.js. If the Maps script never arrives (ad/privacy blocker, key referrer rejection returning an error script, captive portal, offline PWA start) the widget keeps a `Timer.periodic(50 ms)` running for its whole lifetime and renders `ColoredBox(color: MoveraMapPalette.land)` indefinitely. Nothing surfaces the failure to the driver: Home's own 8 s `_startWaitLimit` only covers the start position, not the SDK, and no caller of CustomGoogleMap can observe the not-ready state. The driver sees a flat colour where the map should be, with markers, routes and offer previews silently missing, and the DemoModeBanner/offer flow continue as if the map existed.
confirmed.failure_scenario: Driver opens the PWA with a content blocker that blocks maps.googleapis.com -> Home shows the beige placeholder forever, 'Finding your location' resolves, offers arrive, but no map, route or car is ever drawn and no message explains why; the 50 ms timer keeps polling until the screen is disposed.
confirmed.evidence: custom_google_map.dart:273-286 `bool _mapsReady = web.ready; Timer? _mapsReadyPoll; ... _mapsReadyPoll = Timer.periodic(const Duration(milliseconds: 50), (timer) { if (!web.ready) return; timer.cancel(); if (mounted) setState(() => _mapsReady = true); });`; custom_google_map.dart:407-408 `if (!_mapsReady) const ColoredBox(color: MoveraMapPalette.land) else GoogleMap(`; driver_map_web_bridge.dart:11-17 `bool get ready { final adapter = _adapter; if (adapter == null) return false; ...}`
confirmed.suggested_fix: Bound the wait (e.g. 10-15 s) and then show a 'Map unavailable' state / retry, or expose an onUnavailable callback so Home and AcceptRide can tell the driver.

verdicts.corrected_title: On web, if the Maps JavaScript script is blocked or fails to load, every CustomGoogleMap stays a plain land-colour box with no 'map unavailable' message (the poll is cancelled on dispose)
verdicts.reason: web/index.html:40 loads https://maps.googleapis.com/maps/api/js with a plain script tag and has no onerror handling. web/driver_map_camera.js:615-626 polls for google.maps.Map every 25 ms with no limit, and ready() stays false while sdk is null. lib/widgets/custom_google_map.dart:273-286 polls web.ready every 50 ms with no limit, and :407-408 draws only ColoredBox(MoveraMapPalette.land) until it turns true. No caller in lib/ (accept_ride.dart:1535, home_map_sheet.dart:678/752, destination_confirm.dart:255, reservation_route_map.dart:288, history_detail.dart:78) can see that state, and nothing in lib/ or web/ shows a map-unavailable message. So when a content blocker, firewall or offline start stops the SDK, the driver gets a blank box and no explanation. Parts of the finding are overstated. The timer does not run past the widget's life: dispose cancels it at custom_google_map.dart:477. A rejected or referrer-restricted key still installs google.maps, so ready() becomes true and Google draws its own error inside the map; that sub-case does not reach this path. The waiting is intentional (code comment at :268-272, to avoid ErrorWidget over Home's overlays). What is missing is only a bound or notice. The app does not claim a success it did not get: offers still work and no map is presented as drawn. That makes it a low-severity edge-path UX gap.
verdicts.repro: Static trace only: index.html script tags, then driver_map_camera.js sdkLoaded/setInterval/ready, then driver_map_web_bridge.dart ready getter, then custom_google_map.dart initState poll, build branch and dispose cancel, then grep of all CustomGoogleMap callers and of gm_authFailure / 'unavailable' in lib and web (no matches). No test run, because the web-only path cannot be exercised under flutter test, which uses the bridge stub (custom_google_map.dart:16).

verdicts.corrected_title: Web: if the Maps JavaScript script is blocked or fails to load, CustomGoogleMap shows a plain land-coloured box with no error or retry, and a 50 ms poll runs until the widget is disposed
verdicts.reason: lib/widgets/custom_google_map.dart:273-286 sets `_mapsReady = web.ready` and, when it is false, starts a `Timer.periodic(50ms)` that only stops once `web.ready` turns true. Nothing limits how long it waits. Lines 407-408 draw `ColoredBox(MoveraMapPalette.land)` for as long as `_mapsReady` is false. `ready` (lib/widgets/driver_map_web_bridge.dart:11-17) calls `driverMapCamera.ready()`, and that returns `sdk !== null` (web/driver_map_camera.js ~624). `sdk` is only set by installSdk(), which only runs once `google.maps.Map` and `OverlayView` exist (js:614-622, its own 25 ms setInterval, also unbounded). web/index.html:40 loads the Maps script with a plain `<script src=https://maps.googleapis.com/...>` tag and has no onerror handler. So if that request is blocked (content blocker, captive portal, network failure), google.maps never appears, both polls run indefinitely, and the box stays blank. No caller can see the not-ready state: grep finds no use of web.ready outside the widget. The only related message, `mapCameraUnavailable`, comes from google_driver_camera_port.dart and needs a built map. dispose (custom_google_map.dart:477) does cancel the Dart timer, so this is not a leak past the widget's life. Part of the finding is misdescribed: a rejected API key still loads google.maps, and Google draws its own error overlay, so that case does not produce the blank box. The offline case would have no map tiles anyway. The real trigger is the script being blocked or failing to load. This is web-only and an edge path, there is no crash or data loss, and the offer flow keeps working, so severity is low.
