confirmed.title: With reduced motion (and on the far-cut path) a GPS retarget that arrives during the single moveCamera await is dropped: retarget() requires _looping but _run has already captured the goal, and the controller nulls its pending pose after calling retarget
confirmed.description: `animate()` marks `_looping = true` and starts `_run`. In the `reducedMotion || _logical == null` branch `_run` reads `initial = _goal`, awaits one `_move(...)` and returns; the same happens on the `_far` cut (`await _move(destination ...); break;`). While that `moveCamera` platform call is in flight the controller still sees `_busy == true`, so a new fix goes through `_request` → `_port?.retarget(pending); _pending = null;` (driver_camera_controller.dart:732-737). `retarget` stores the pose in `_goal` (it passes the `_looping` check), but nobody reads `_goal` again: `_run` returns, `finally` clears `_looping`, the session completes, the controller sets `_busy = false` and arms a 16 ms throttle with `_pending` already null. The fix is lost until the next one, so under reduced motion the car/camera skip fixes whenever a platform round-trip overlaps a GPS event. Narrow window (a few ms per fix) but a real contract break of `DriverCameraPort.retarget` ('the in-flight animation steers toward this pose').
confirmed.failure_scenario: Driver with 'reduce motion' enabled on a 1 Hz GPS trip: occasionally a fix lands while the previous moveCamera is awaiting acknowledgement; that fix never reaches the map and the camera holds the previous position for an extra second.
confirmed.evidence: google_driver_camera_port.dart:259-263: `if (reducedMotion || _logical == null) { await _move(_at(initial, initial.target), trackVehicle: true, generation: generation); return; }`; :283-287: `if (_far(from, destination)) { _flightPending = false; await _move(destination, trackVehicle: true, generation: generation); break; }`; :223-229: `void retarget(DriverCameraPose pose) { if (_disposed || !_looping) { return; } _goal = pose; ...`. driver_camera_controller.dart:732-737: `if (_busy && pending != null) { _port?.retarget(pending); _pending = null; }`.
confirmed.suggested_fix: After the single move / far cut, re-check `_goal` and issue one more `_move` if it changed during the await (or keep `_pending` in the controller until the port confirms it consumed the retarget).

verdicts.reason: I traced this and it holds. animate() sets _looping=true and calls _run (lib/widgets/google_driver_camera_port.dart:241-249). On the reduced-motion branch (:259-262), _run awaits a single _move and returns. On the far-cut branch (:283-287), it awaits _move and then breaks. The settled+first case (:310-320) also breaks right after its await. In none of these paths does _run read _goal again after the await. During that await, retarget() (:223-229) still passes the _looping check and writes _goal. Meanwhile the controller, which is still _busy, has already cleared its copy: DriverCameraController._request calls _port.retarget(pending) and then sets _pending=null (lib/core/navigation/driver_camera_controller.dart:732-737). After the await, finally (:340-345) clears _looping and the session completes. _flush then sets _busy=false and arms a 16 ms throttle (:765-770), but _pending is null so nothing is replayed. The fix is lost until the next GPS event. This is a real path for users: reducedMotion is wired to MediaQuery.disableAnimationsOf at home_map_sheet.dart:713/791, accept_ride.dart:1266 and adaptive_trip_island.dart:493. It also breaks the port contract at driver_camera_controller.dart:43-45, which says the in-flight animation steers toward the retargeted pose. The impact is small: the window is one platform round-trip, and the next fix (about 1 s later) corrects the camera. So severity is low.
verdicts.repro: Static trace only, no test run. GoogleMapController.moveCamera needs a platform map to fake. I read _run, retarget, animate and the finally block in google_driver_camera_port.dart:223-350, and _request/_flush/_invalidate in driver_camera_controller.dart:705-770. Nothing re-checks _goal after the single or far-cut _move, and the controller does not keep _pending after calling retarget. accept_ride_trip.dart:252-255 `if (event.status != null || event.kind == DriverRealtimeKind.riderCancelled) { _pendingProjection = event; unawaited(_drainProjection()); return; }`

refuted.title: Paid pickup wait is added to _paidWaitSeconds only after the Waiting->OnTrip snapshot was persisted, so a crash between the two writes drops the waiting fee
refuted.description: `_advanceRide` captures `paidWait = _paidWaitNow`, then awaits `_rideLifecycle.transitionTo(onTrip)`, which immediately writes the snapshot built by `_buildSnapshot` (`paidWaitSeconds: _paidWaitSeconds`, line 39) — still the pre-increment value — and commits stage=onTrip. Only afterwards `_paidWaitSeconds += paidWait` runs and a second `persistNow()` (line 846) writes it. On restore `_paidWaitSeconds = restored?.paidWaitSeconds ?? 0` (accept_ride.dart:609) and the wait clock is no longer running, so `_paidWaitTotal`, `_fareWithWaiting` and the finish journal's `paid` amount lose the pickup waiting fee if the app is killed between the two saves (the second save can also be delayed by a pending background save, active_ride_controller.dart:73-75).
refuted.failure_scenario: Driver waited 9 minutes at pickup (4 paid minutes), slides 'Start trip'; the first snapshot (stage onTrip, paidWaitSeconds 0) lands, the process is killed before the second persistNow; after restart the trip resumes on-trip with no paid wait and the completed fare/earnings omit the 4 paid minutes.
refuted.suggested_fix: Fold the paid wait into `_paidWaitSeconds` (or into the snapshot builder) before calling `transitionTo`, rolling it back if the transition is refused, so the single stage write already carries the fee.

verdicts.reason: The two writes are not atomic, but the gap between them cannot realistically be hit. After transitionTo's write commits (active_ride_controller.dart:255-260), its future resolves through microtasks. Lines 837-845 of accept_ride_trip.dart are synchronous, and persistNow at :846 starts at once, without yielding to the event loop. So no GPS event, timer or lifecycle callback can slip a background save in between. The finding's claim that the second save 'can be delayed by a pending background save' is therefore wrong: _write would only drop it if _writing were true (:241-243), and nothing can set that here. The only losing case is the process dying during the single prefs.setString of that second save (prefs_active_ride_repository.dart:155), a window of milliseconds. Any app pause also persists the corrected value (accept_ride.dart:724). That is a speculative crash timing, not a realistic path.
verdicts.repro: Static trace of _advanceRide (accept_ride_trip.dart:830-846), ActiveRideController.transitionTo, _write and persistNow (active_ride_controller.dart:72-108, 236-279), and PrefsActiveRideRepository.save (prefs_active_ride_repository.dart:134-158). I confirmed _buildSnapshot reads _paidWaitSeconds before the increment (:39), and that on restore _countingWait is false for an on-trip stage (accept_ride.dart:775-776). So the loss happens only if the second write never lands, and it starts with no interleaving.

refuted.title: Crash/reload restore drops pickupKm, so the far-pickup waiting rule disappears and the waiting fee / no-show terms change mid-trip
refuted.description: `_waitTerms` is computed from `widget.pickupKm` (accept_ride.dart:989-996). Home passes the offer's `pickupKm` (home_offer_radar.dart:974) so a pickup over `farPickupKm` (5 km) gets the 'Pickup far away' rule: 1 free minute and an 85 kr no-show fee instead of 5 free minutes / 65 kr (waiting_rules.dart). `PersistedActiveRide` has no pickupKm field, `_buildSnapshot` (accept_ride_trip.dart:8-62) does not store it, and `AcceptRide.fromPersisted` (accept_ride.dart:240-292) never passes it, so after the documented crash/reload/PWA restore (`Home restores AcceptRide.fromPersisted`) the trip runs with the base terms. The pickup wait that was paid from minute 1 before the restore is now free until minute 5 (`_inIncludedWait`, `_paidWaitNow` = `_waitSeconds - 300`), the no-show option appears later, and the fee the trip earns (`_paidWaybill`, `_cashToCollect`) is lower than the terms shown before the restore. `WaitingTerms.active` and the waiting sheet also lose the 'Rule for this pickup' line. (`bags` and `offerId` are lost the same way; cosmetic.)
refuted.failure_scenario: Driver accepts a 7 km pickup (far-pickup rule), arrives, waits 3 minutes: 2 paid minutes shown. The PWA reloads; the restored screen now shows 'included wait' until 5 min, the no-show button is gone until 5 min, and the final waiting fee/cash to collect is computed with 5 free minutes.
refuted.evidence:
accept_ride.dart:989-996 `late final WaitingTerms _waitTerms = WaitingRules.current.termsFor(
    category: widget.category,
    type: ..., pickupKm: widget.pickupKm,
  );` ; fromPersisted 253-291 passes no `pickupKm`; active_ride_repository.dart PersistedActiveRide fields contain no pickupKm; waiting_rules.dart `if (pickupKm != null && pickupKm > farPickupKm) { ... terms._with(farPickup ...) }`
refuted.suggested_fix: Persist `pickupKm` (and `bags`) in `PersistedActiveRide`/`_buildSnapshot` and pass it in `AcceptRide.fromPersisted`; alternatively persist the resolved `WaitingTerms`.

verdicts.reason: The persistence gap is real: PersistedActiveRide (lib/core/ride/active_ride_repository.dart:101-133) has no pickupKm field, and AcceptRide.fromPersisted (accept_ride.dart:240-292) passes none, so a restored trip gets pickupKm == null. But the far-pickup rule only applies when pickupKm > farPickupKm (5 km) (waiting_rules.dart:226), and no reachable offer is that far. Every RideOffer the app builds comes from demo_dispatch_repository.dart (0.5 to 3.6 km), demo_destination_trips.dart:40 (0.8), dispatch_repository.dart:67 (2.1), home.dart:410/428 (0.9, 3.3) or the next-trip demo (1.6). ApiDispatchRepository, the only source that could give pickupMeters over 5000, is never instantiated in lib/ (`grep 'ApiDispatchRepository(' lib` finds only its own constructor). A null pickupKm and any reachable pickupKm both give the same base terms, so the waiting fee and no-show terms are the same before and after a restore. This is a latent gap to fix when a real dispatch backend is wired, not a failure that can happen today.
verdicts.repro: Static trace: grep of every `pickupKm:` literal and RideOffer( construction site in lib/, the termsFor branch at waiting_rules.dart:194-238, the fromPersisted argument list, and a check that ApiDispatchRepository is never constructed.

refuted.failure_scenario: Legacy auth build: Profile > Log out > 'Legacy sign-in preview': the user is stuck on Sign in; on iOS/web there is no way to reach the demo home again without restarting the app.
refuted.evidence: starter.dart:79-82 `Navigator.pushReplacement( context, BottomToTopTransition(const DriverSignIn()), );`; sign_in.dart has no IconButton/pop and no DriverRuntimeScope use; profile.dart:414-417 `pushAndRemoveUntil(MaterialPageRoute<void>(builder: (_) => const DriverStarter()), (route) => false)`.
refuted.suggested_fix: Use `Navigator.push` (as the registration button already does) or give DriverSignIn a back/return-to-demo action.

verdicts.reason: The pushReplacement at starter.dart:79-82 only runs when `legacyAuthEnabled` is true (starter.dart:77). That is a compile-time define that defaults to false (lib/core/session/demo_features.dart:2) and is never set anywhere in the repo. In the canonical build the button is disabled (onPressed: null) and shows tr.signInUnavailableDemo, so the starter is never replaced. docs/ROUTES.md:56 records 'Logout: DriverStarter displays demo account boundary; legacy sign-in is disabled by default.' The legacy screens are documented opt-in previews (ROUTES.md:3, :27).
verdicts.repro: Read starter.dart:70-100 and demo_features.dart:2, and grepped the repo for MOVERA_ENABLE_LEGACY_AUTH: only the definition and the docs that say it is off by default. No test run.

refuted.title: Queue position sheet shows hard-coded English '15-30 mins EST time'
refuted.description: The sheet opened from `in_airport_queue.dart:20` (`showMyQueuePositionSheet`) localizes its title (`tr.queueMediumWait`) but the line under it is a literal English string with a non-standard abbreviation.
refuted.failure_scenario: Swedish driver opens Min plats i kön: 'Medellång väntan' followed by '15-30 mins EST time'.
refuted.evidence: my_queue_pos.dart:113-121: `TextWidget( text: tr.queueMediumWait, ...), 2.height, TextWidget( text: "15-30 mins EST time",`
refuted.suggested_fix: Add an ARB key and use `tr`.

verdicts.reason: No driver can reach this text. The queue-position sheet opens only from InAirportQueue (in_airport_queue.dart:20). InAirportQueue renders only under `if (isDestinationPanel)` (home_map_sheet.dart:841-844), and that is true only for the DestinationSetPanel body built when `hideMainPanel` is true (home.dart:769-777). The only write that sets hideMainPanel to true is in openDestinationPanel() (home_map_sheet.dart:535-538), and neither it nor its wrapper (home.dart:339) has a caller in lib/ or test/. The string is hard-coded English, but it sits in dead UI.
verdicts.repro: Traced callers: grep for showMyQueuePositionSheet led to InAirportQueue, then home_map_sheet.dart:844 (only when isDestinationPanel), then home.dart:777 (only when hideMainPanel is true). grep 'hideMainPanel' showed the only `= true` write at home_map_sheet.dart:538 inside openDestinationPanel. grep 'openDestinationPanel' over lib and test found only the two declarations, with no call sites or tear-offs. No test run.

refuted.title: Vacuous assertion: GoogleMap property check after asserting no GoogleMap exists
refuted.description: After `expect(find.byType(GoogleMap), findsNothing)` the test iterates `tester.widgetList<GoogleMap>(find.byType(GoogleMap)).any(...)` and expects false; with no GoogleMap widgets `any` is always false, so the second assertion can never fail and does not verify the start-position property it appears to cover.
refuted.failure_scenario: The Home map starts rendering at a wrong initial camera position; this assertion still passes because the list it inspects is empty by construction.
refuted.evidence: test/audit/home_start_position_test.dart:81-85 `expect(find.byType(GoogleMap), findsNothing);` followed by `expect(tester.widgetList<GoogleMap>(find.byType(GoogleMap)).any(...), isFalse);`
refuted.suggested_fix: Assert the initial camera position on the real map widget once it is built (or drop the dead assertion).

verdicts.reason: The failure scenario cannot happen. In test/audit/home_start_position_test.dart, the second expect (lines ~82-85) is redundant, but the line just before it, `expect(find.byType(GoogleMap), findsNothing)`, already fails the test if Home builds any GoogleMap, whatever its camera or markers. So a Home map at a wrong or Stockholm position cannot pass this test. The camera-target property the finding says is uncovered is checked by the first test in the same file ('saved last position is the first camera target and car'). It asserts isNotEmpty on the GoogleMap list and then checks map.initialCameraPosition.target == saved and the driver_location marker position for every map. The extra `any(...)` line is dead, harmless code, not a hole in coverage.
verdicts.repro: Read test/audit/home_start_position_test.dart in full. Followed the logic: if findsNothing passes, the list is empty and any() is false. If any GoogleMap exists, findsNothing fails first. The first testWidgets covers initialCameraPosition with a non-empty guard. The test was not run because no runtime question remained.

refuted.title: localDataInventory omits the home_island_hint_seen SharedPreferences key, so the 'inventory of keys' is incomplete (non-personal device flag, no privacy exposure)
refuted.description: local_data.dart:38 declares `localDataInventory` as the 'Inventory of Driver keys written through SharedPreferences' and clearLocalUserData removes only inventoried keys. `_showIslandHintOnce` writes `prefs.setBool(_islandHintSeenKey, true)` directly, outside the inventory and outside the SettingsRepository sections, so it is neither documented nor cleared. LOCAL_DATA.md says logout removes 'settings'; this per-driver first-launch setting is kept, and the next driver signing in on the same device never gets the one-time earnings hint the islandHint feature exists to show. The inventory test (test/core/local_data_test.dart) only checks that listed keys are listed, so it cannot catch unlisted writers.
refuted.failure_scenario: Driver A sees the island hint once; A logs out (LOCAL_DATA.md: settings cleared); driver B on the same phone/browser never sees the first-launch hint because `flutter.home_island_hint_seen` is still true.
refuted.evidence: home_map_sheet.dart:26 `const String _islandHintSeenKey = 'home_island_hint_seen';`; home_map_sheet.dart:1337-1339 `final prefs = await SharedPreferences.getInstance(); if (!mounted || (prefs.getBool(_islandHintSeenKey) ?? false)) { return; } await prefs.setBool(_islandHintSeenKey, true);`; local_data.dart:38-41 `/// Inventory of Driver keys written through SharedPreferences.` with no such record; local_data.dart:123-132 `const exact = <String>[ PrefsActiveRideRepository.key, ... DriverStartPosition.key ];`
refuted.suggested_fix: Add the key to localDataInventory (class preference) and to the logout clear list, or store it as a SettingsRepository section so the existing prefix clear covers it.

verdicts.corrected_title: localDataInventory omits the home_island_hint_seen SharedPreferences key, so the 'inventory of keys' is incomplete (non-personal device flag, no privacy exposure)
verdicts.reason: local_data.dart:38-41 says localDataInventory is the inventory of Driver keys written through SharedPreferences. A grep of every prefs.set* call in lib/ shows home_map_sheet.dart:1339 (`prefs.setBool(_islandHintSeenKey, true)`) is the only writer missing from it, and clearLocalUserData's exact list (local_data.dart:123-132) does not include it. That is a real completeness gap in the record. The privacy framing does not hold: the key is a boolean holding no personal data. LOCAL_DATA.md explicitly says 'Keys that are not in localDataInventory are not removed'. The code comment at home_map_sheet.dart:1334 ('First launch only') makes this a per-device hint, so it surviving logout is arguably intended. The real defect is only the incomplete inventory.
verdicts.repro: grep of all SharedPreferences writes in lib/ compared against localDataInventory and the clear list. Read docs/LOCAL_DATA.md, test/core/local_data_test.dart and test/widget_test.dart:1804, which asserts the flag is set.

verdicts.reason: The key is written outside the inventory (home_map_sheet.dart:26, 1337-1339) and survives logout, but that is documented and harmless. LOCAL_DATA.md states 'Keys that are not in `localDataInventory` are not removed.', and clearLocalUserData's doc says keys outside the inventory are left untouched (local_data.dart:105-108). The value is a single non-personal boolean with no rider or driver data, so there is no privacy exposure. The method is commented 'First launch only' (home_map_sheet.dart:1334), meaning first launch on the device. Driver B not seeing a one-time UI hint on a device where it was already shown fits that intent, and the hint is gated by DriverRuntimeConfig.islandHint anyway. The only real gap is that the inventory's doc comment ('Inventory of Driver keys written through SharedPreferences', local_data.dart:38) is incomplete. That is a documentation nit, not a privacy or behaviour bug.
verdicts.repro: Traced by hand. The only writer of home_island_hint_seen is _showIslandHintOnce (home_map_sheet.dart:1335-1341), called once from _startIslandWake. clearLocalUserData's exact list and its prefix sweep (local_data.dart:123-152) do not match the key, which is consistent with the stated policy in docs/LOCAL_DATA.md. No test run was needed.

verdicts.reason: The two facts in the finding are correct, but the defect it describes is not. The privacy issue, the claim that logout should clear the key, and the driver-B harm all contradict the documented design. (1) clearLocalUserData only removes "classified personal and recovery keys" and leaves keys outside the Movera inventory alone (lib/core/privacy/local_data.dart:106-110). docs/LOCAL_DATA.md:17-18 says the same: "Keys that are not in `localDataInventory` are not removed". The existing test pins that behaviour by asserting that a non-personal `unrelated_preview_flag` is kept after logout (test/core/local_data_test.dart:19,34). (2) `home_island_hint_seen` is a single non-personal boolean. If it were inventoried it would be class `preference` ("Non-personal preview preferences", local_data.dart:20-21), and that class is not personal or recovery, so logout would still leave it. The proposed fix of adding it to the logout clear list therefore goes against the design. (3) The hint is meant to show once per device. Its comments say "Set once the first-launch hint has been shown" (home_map_sheet.dart:25) and "First launch only" (home_map_sheet.dart:1334). Driver B on a phone that has already launched the app is not on a first launch, so not seeing the hint matches the design, and DriverRuntimeConfig.islandHint gates it anyway (home_map_sheet.dart:1336). (4) LOCAL_DATA.md's "settings" means the SettingsRepository blob and sections (local_data.dart:79-91), not this UI flag. One real gap remains. The doc comment "Inventory of Driver keys written through SharedPreferences" (local_data.dart:38) is incomplete: a grep of every prefs.set* in lib/ shows home_map_sheet.dart:1339 is the only writer missing, and the `preference` class has no records. But nothing reads localDataInventory at runtime except the test, so this is a documentation nit with no behaviour, privacy or data effect. It is not the privacy bug that was filed.
verdicts.repro: I wrote a throwaway test, test/_audit_driver67_test.dart, deleted it afterwards and confirmed it was gone. It seeded mock prefs with {'home_island_hint_seen': true, 'movera_driver_settings_section_contacts': '{}'}, called clearLocalUserData(), and printed the state. Output: "after logout: hint=true contacts=null inInventory=false preferenceRecords=0", then "00:00 +1: All tests passed!". The personal settings section is cleared and the hint flag survives. That matches the stated policy at local_data.dart:106-110 and docs/LOCAL_DATA.md:17-18, and the kept `unrelated_preview_flag` in test/core/local_data_test.dart:34. A grep of prefs.set* in lib/ confirms home_map_sheet.dart:1339 is the only uninventoried writer.
verdicts.corrected_title: localDataInventory doc comment (local_data.dart:38) omits the non-personal home_island_hint_seen preference; documentation nit, no privacy or logout defect

refuted.title: Expired Radar offers dropped by _refreshRadarHomeOffers keep their entry in _radarOfferTimeoutTimers, so the same offer re-listed later never gets a pick window
refuted.description: _refreshRadarHomeOffers removes offers in _radarOfferExpired from the list and clears _radarOfferExpired and their _radarOfferDeadlines (400-404), but leaves the fired Timer objects in _radarOfferTimeoutTimers (only _dismissRadarHomeOffer and _cancelAllOfferTimers remove them). _startRadarPickWindow returns early whenever `_radarOfferTimeoutTimers.containsKey(offer.id)` (425-428). An offer with the same id that comes back onto the deck (the demo's _showDispatchOfferAt(0..2) re-run on every _resumeHomeUpdates for nearby-1..3 which stay in the feed; a reservation re-joining via _reservationToDeck) is listed with no deadline and no timer, so its Match never fades.
refuted.failure_scenario: nearby-1's 15 s window runs out, a pending trip triggers a refresh (nearby-1 leaves). Driver opens and closes a side-menu screen; _scheduleVisibleOffers re-lists nearby-1. Its card now shows an active Match indefinitely instead of expiring after the radar time.
refuted.evidence: home_offer_radar.dart:400-404 `next.removeWhere((offer) => _radarOfferExpired.contains(offer.id)); _radarOfferExpired.clear(); _radarOfferDeadlines.removeWhere((id, _) => !next.any((offer) => offer.id == id));` | home_offer_radar.dart:424-428 `void _startRadarPickWindow(_HomeDirectOffer offer) { if (_radarOfferTimeoutTimers.containsKey(offer.id) || _radarOfferExpired.contains(offer.id)) { return; }`
refuted.suggested_fix: Remove (and cancel) the _radarOfferTimeoutTimers entry for every offer dropped in _refreshRadarHomeOffers, or key the early-return on an active (not yet fired) timer.

verdicts.reason: The cited path cannot reach the stale entry. An expired offer can only come back onto the deck through _scheduleVisibleOffers (the demo _showDispatchOfferAt timers). That function first calls _cancelAllOfferTimers(preserveClaim: true) at home_offer_radar.dart:1163, which cancels and clears every _radarOfferTimeoutTimers entry (801-804). Opening any screen from the side menu also pauses Home first (didPushNext -> _pauseHomeUpdates, home.dart:174/198), and that clears the map too. So when nearby-1 is listed again, _startRadarPickWindow finds no entry. Its _radarOfferExpired and _radarOfferDeadlines entries were already removed by the refresh (401-404), so it gets a fresh deadline. One residual path exists: a reservation that was dropped as expired, then left the dispatch feed and came back via _reservationToDeck (590-594) with no pause, offline or trip in between. That path is speculative, and the only harm would be a Match that does not fade; dispatch still decides the claim.
verdicts.repro: Static trace of every writer of _radarOfferTimeoutTimers (home_offer_radar.dart:433, 480, 801-804) and every caller of _activateRadarHomeOffer/_startRadarPickWindow (350, 372, 406, 762). Re-listing goes through _scheduleVisibleOffers (1161-1205) or _reservationToDeck (home_reservation.dart:534-544), and the first of these clears the map before re-listing.

refuted.title: A fresh Idempotency-Key is generated on every request, so a retry after a lost response is a new mutation instead of a replay
refuted.description: The contract (contract.json#headers, openapi IdempotencyKey: 'the same key replays the committed response', DriverCommand doc 'Reuse it on retry') makes the key the only way to recover from a committed-but-unanswered mutation. `_headers(mutation: true)` calls `_key()` (a random 32-hex string) each time it is invoked, and `claimOffer`/`declineOffer` call `_headers` per HTTP request with no key kept per offer/attempt. On a transport exception `claimOffer` returns `networkError`; Home/Ride requests then let the driver tap Match again (home_offer_radar.dart:559-564, ride_requests.dart:338-341), which sends the same body under a new key. If the first POST had been committed server-side (response lost), the second accept is a separate command against an offer this driver already holds; the server answers 409 (invalid_transition/conflict with the offer, status != open/claimed_elsewhere), and the 409 branch (lines 364-380) withdraws the offer locally and reports `unavailable`/`alreadyClaimed`, so the UI tells the driver the trip is gone while the server has assigned it to them.
refuted.failure_scenario: Flaky mobile network: POST /offers/{id}/accept commits on the server but the response times out -> app shows 'No connection', driver taps Match again -> new Idempotency-Key -> 409 -> island 'Trip no longer available' / 'Taken by another driver'; the trip never opens on this phone although dispatch locked it to this driver.
refuted.evidence: api_dispatch_repository.dart:178-187 `Future<Map<String, String>> _headers({bool mutation = false}) async { ... if (mutation) 'Idempotency-Key': _key(), }`; :347-351 `response = await _client.post(_uri('/offers/.../accept'), headers: await _headers(mutation: true), body: jsonEncode({'expectedVersion': version}));`; :352-353 `} catch (_) { return const ClaimResult.networkError(); }`; driver_trip_gateway.dart:101-102 `/// 16–128 characters (contract.json#headers). Reuse it on retry.`
refuted.suggested_fix: Derive/keep one key per (offerId, body) attempt (e.g. store it in a map until a definitive 2xx/4xx arrives) and reuse it on the network-error retry; only mint a new key when the body changes (the version_mismatch retry).

verdicts.reason: No runtime path reaches this. ApiDispatchRepository is never constructed in lib/; its class doc says 'nothing installs this class in the app; the demo builds use the in-process demo dispatch' (api_dispatch_repository.dart:134-135). Grep finds it only in test/round3/driver_admin_offers_dispatch_test.dart:55. The Home/Ride request screens therefore never reach claimOffer's per-request _key() (line 185) over HTTP. The scenario also depends on an unspecified server reply: what a re-accept by the same driver under a new key returns is not defined for a backend that does not exist. The missing key reuse is a valid hardening note for when the adapter is wired, but it is dormant code today.
verdicts.repro: Grepped lib/ and test/ for 'ApiDispatchRepository': no production callers, test only. Read api_dispatch_repository.dart:130-187 and 337-389, and checked contract.json:868-872 and openapi.yaml:4499-4504 for the idempotency semantics.

refuted.title: The SSE offer feed subscription has no onError/onDone handling, so a dropped stream raises an unhandled error and the feed silently dies with no resync
refuted.description: connect() subscribes with `.listen((line) {...})` only. A transport error on the body stream (connection reset, TLS error) has no onError handler, so it is forwarded to the zone's uncaught-error handler, and onDone (server closed the stream) is ignored: `_feed` keeps pointing at a finished subscription, nothing reconnects from `lastSequence` or reloads `GET /driver/offers`, and the driver's offer list stays frozen with stale open offers. The contract's realtime rules require resync after gaps/disconnects. ApiDispatchRepository is not installed by the app today (class doc: 'nothing installs this class in the app'), so this is dormant.
refuted.failure_scenario: With the API dispatch adapter in use, the phone loses connectivity for a minute; the SSE stream errors. The error surfaces as an uncaught exception (debug) and the offer list never updates again until the app restarts; offers that were withdrawn server-side remain tappable and accept returns 404/409.
refuted.evidence: api_dispatch_repository.dart:255-271 `_feed = response.stream.transform(utf8.decoder).transform(const LineSplitter()).listen((line) { ... });` (no onError, no onDone, no reconnect)
refuted.suggested_fix: Pass onError/onDone to listen; on either, clear `_feed`, schedule a reconnect with backoff using `after=$_lastSequence`, and call `_load()` to resync the open-offer list.

verdicts.reason: The code is unreachable. connect() at api_dispatch_repository.dart:245-272 is called by nothing in lib/ (grep for ApiDispatchRepository and .connect() finds only the test file). The class doc says nothing installs it (lines 134-135), and the finding itself calls it dormant. No real caller opens the SSE feed, so neither the missing onError nor the missing onDone/resync can affect the app as built.
verdicts.repro: Grepped lib/ and test/ for ApiDispatchRepository and connect(): only test/round3/driver_admin_offers_dispatch_test.dart constructs it. Read connect() at lines 244-272.

refuted.title: clearForTrip/save/handoff call jsonDecode on the raw snapshot without tolerating an undecodable value, so a corrupt snapshot makes the completion journal unrepayable and Home recovery permanently fails
refuted.description: read() and quarantineUnreadable() go through _decodeSnapshot and convert a decode failure into ActiveRideUnreadable (lines 77-83, 117-127), matching LOCAL_DATA.md ("A corrupt value is treated as missing by the readers"). The three writers do not: clearForTrip (line 290 `final data = jsonDecode(raw);`), save (line 143) and handoff (line 168) let a FormatException from invalid JSON propagate (save also does `ActiveRideStage.values.byName(current['stage'] as String)` at 151, which throws on a valid-JSON map with a bad stage). CompletionJournal._replay runs history.archive -> markTerminal -> clearForTrip(id) (completion_journal.dart:259) with no guard, so the thrown FormatException leaves the journal in prefs and makes finish() throw; every retry replays the same journal and fails at the same step. On the next Home, _restoreActiveRideIfNeeded awaits CompletionJournal.reconcile() BEFORE repo.read() (home.dart:508-514); reconcile throws the FormatException, which is caught by the generic `catch (_)` (home.dart:519) and shown as recoveryFailed, so the ActiveRideUnreadable path that offers 'Close unreadable trip' (home.dart:515-517) is never reached, _recoveryResolved stays false and the driver cannot go online (home.dart:335). Only logout (clearLocalUserData) clears it. Reproduced with a throwaway flutter test: prefs key set to '{not json'; read() -> ActiveRideUnreadable (handled), clearForTrip('T1') -> FormatException, CompletionJournal.finish(...) -> FormatException with the journal left in prefs, reconcile() -> FormatException.
refuted.failure_scenario: The movera_driver_active_ride value becomes undecodable mid-trip (truncated localStorage write on the PWA, storage corruption). The driver taps Finish: the trip is archived to history and marked terminal, then clearForTrip throws -> 'Could not finish saving this trip'; every retry fails the same way and the driver cannot leave the trip. After a restart, Home shows 'saved trip could not be opened' on every launch, never offers the unreadable-trip closure dialog, and the driver cannot go online until they log out.
refuted.evidence: prefs_active_ride_repository.dart:283-297 `Future<void> clearForTrip(String tripId) => _enqueue(() async { ... final raw = prefs.getString(key); if (raw == null) { return; } final data = jsonDecode(raw); if (data is! Map || data['tripId'] != tripId) { return; } ...`  |  :141-151 `final raw = prefs.getString(key); if (raw != null) { final current = jsonDecode(raw); ... final stage = ActiveRideStage.values.byName(current['stage'] as String);`  |  completion_journal.dart:258-259 `if (repository is TerminalRideRepository) { await (repository as TerminalRideRepository).clearForTrip(id); }` (no try/catch; journal removed only afterwards at :268)  |  home.dart:508 `final journal = await CompletionJournal(active: repo).reconcile();` precedes :514 `snapshot = await repo.read();`  |  test output: `clearForTrip() -> FormatException: Unexpected character (at character 2)` / `finish() -> FormatException; journal left = true` / `reconcile() -> FormatException`
refuted.suggested_fix: In clearForTrip/save/handoff decode the raw value with a guarded helper (try jsonDecode, treat non-Map/invalid JSON as 'not owned by any trip'); for clearForTrip that means returning without error, for save/handoff it means treating the slot as free (or quarantining it first). Alternatively have Home call repo.read() (or a cheap decode probe) before reconcile() so ActiveRideUnreadable is surfaced and the closure dialog still appears.

verdicts.reason: The mismatch is real: clearForTrip (prefs_active_ride_repository.dart:290), save (:143) and handoff (:168) call jsonDecode without a guard, while read() and quarantineUnreadable() turn the same failure into ActiveRideUnreadable (:77-83, :117-127). No realistic path reaches it, though. The app writes this key in only two places, and both write jsonEncode output with one atomic setString (:156, :184). No code writes a truncated value or an empty string to it. localStorage.setItem and Android/iOS SharedPreferences writes are atomic, so a 'truncated write' does not happen. A snapshot already corrupt at startup is handled: reconcile() finds no journal (a journal exists only while finish() is running, completion_journal.dart:128-132), then repo.read() throws ActiveRideUnreadable and Home offers the closure dialog (home.dart:515-517). Valid JSON with a bad shape also passes clearForTrip (the data is! Map / tripId check at :291). The only way to fail is invalid JSON put into storage by something outside the app, during a running trip and before Finish. That is speculative.
verdicts.repro: Traced every writer of PrefsActiveRideRepository.key in lib/ (grep: only :156 and :184 write it; local_data.dart only removes it). Traced CompletionJournal.finish/_replay (completion_journal.dart:91-133, 144-273) and Home._restoreActiveRideIfNeeded (home.dart:500-525). Read the existing tests test/audit/recovery_ownership_test.dart:27-32 and storage_integrity_test.dart N04, which show the startup corruption path is handled. No new test needed: the failure only happens after storage is corrupted from outside the app.

refuted.title: Release-evidence gate step cannot fail: check_frontend_release.py is run without --require-complete
refuted.description: The 'Frontend release evidence contracts' step runs `python3 tool/check_frontend_release.py docs/frontend-completion/09-release-candidate.json` with no `--require-complete` flag. In tool/check_frontend_release.py `validate()` only raises on malformed metadata; `main()` returns 0 whenever the document parses, printing 'release NOT complete: ...' as an info line. With every required check in 09-release-candidate.json at PENDING (and even if some were FAIL) the step is green. Running it now prints 'Manifest valid; release NOT complete: accessibility, automated, deployment-smoke, device-lifecycle, layout, performance, real-maps, secondary-screens, trip-journeys' and exits 0. docs/REVIEW_AND_MERGE_GATES.md presents this as a merge/release gate, but the only thing it blocks is a syntactically broken JSON file.
refuted.failure_scenario: A release candidate with FAIL or PENDING evidence rows passes the verify job, deploy-pages.yml (workflow_run on 'Drider CI' success, main) then publishes the web build to GitHub Pages although the evidence manifest says the release is not complete.
refuted.evidence: .github/workflows/drider-ci.yml:55 `python3 tool/check_frontend_release.py docs/frontend-completion/09-release-candidate.json`; tool/check_frontend_release.py:54 `if require_complete and incomplete:` ... :75 `return 0`; local run output: `Manifest valid; release NOT complete: accessibility, ... trip-journeys` / `exit=0`
refuted.suggested_fix: Either pass `--require-complete` in the CI step (and only on release branches/tags if PENDING must be allowed on PRs), or make a FAIL status a hard error regardless of the flag.

verdicts.reason: Leaving out --require-complete is the documented design. docs/frontend-completion/09-release-verification.md:9 says that without the flag the command only validates the manifest and prints incomplete checks, and that `--require-complete` is for final sign-off on a copied, per-candidate evidence record. The file CI checks (docs/frontend-completion/09-release-candidate.json) is the template, and the docs say it stays PENDING. docs/REVIEW_AND_MERGE_GATES.md:31-35 lists the merge gate jobs (analyze, test, lifecycle, web build, native release jobs) and does not count release evidence completion among them. Line 49 states the RELEASE_EVIDENCE_MATRIX "stays PENDING" and that no device or visual PASS is claimed. Turning the flag on in CI would fail every run by design. The GitHub Pages deploy is the demo web build, not a signed-off release.

refuted.title: On web the last-known-position fallback throws UnsupportedError from inside the catch block, replacing the original GPS error and skipping the error log
refuted.description: `getCurrentPosition()` catches the live-fix error and calls `Geolocator.getLastKnownPosition()`. geolocator_web 4.1.4 implements that method as `throw _unsupported('getLastKnownPosition')` (geolocator_web.dart:68-71). The throw happens inside the `catch` clause, so it propagates out of the method before `vetCachedFix`, `DriverLog.error('No recent accurate GPS fix available', error, stack)` and `rethrow` run. Callers catch everything, so the screen outcome (`Location updating…`) is unchanged, but the diagnostic record of why GPS failed on web is lost and an unrelated `UnsupportedError` is what surfaces.
refuted.failure_scenario: On the PWA a timeout/permission error from the browser is reported as 'Unsupported operation: getLastKnownPosition is not supported on the web platform' with no 'No recent accurate GPS fix available' log, making field diagnosis of web GPS failures misleading.
refuted.evidence: driver_location_service.dart:37-49: `} catch (error, stack) { DriverLog.warn('Current GPS failed, trying last known: $error'); final last = await Geolocator.getLastKnownPosition(); ... DriverLog.error('No recent accurate GPS fix available', error, stack); rethrow; }`. geolocator_web-4.1.4/lib/geolocator_web.dart:68-71: `Future<Position> getLastKnownPosition({...}) { throw _unsupported('getLastKnownPosition'); }`.
refuted.suggested_fix: Skip the fallback on web (`if (kIsWeb) rethrow;`) or wrap `getLastKnownPosition()` in its own try/catch so the original error is logged and rethrown.

verdicts.reason: geolocator_web.dart:68-71 does make `getLastKnownPosition` throw UnsupportedError inside the catch, but the effect is harmless. The original GPS error has already been logged with its text at driver_location_service.dart:38 (`DriverLog.warn('Current GPS failed, trying last known: $error')`), so the diagnostic is not lost; only the duplicate error-level record is skipped. Both callers catch every error without looking at its type (accept_ride_trip.dart:620 `catch (_)`, home_map_sheet.dart:50 `catch (_)`) and show the same 'Location updating…' or failed state either way. DriverLog.sink is only a console print (driver_log.dart), with no crash reporter that would mis-classify the error. Users see no difference.
verdicts.repro: Static trace of the catch block, the DriverLog sink and both callers' catch clauses.

refuted.title: DriverRealtimeEvent.tryParse throws TypeError on a non-string `kind` although it is documented to skip broken envelopes

The kind check `DriverRealtimeKind.tryParse(map['kind'] as String?)` is executed outside the try block, so an envelope whose kind is not a String (e.g. a number or an object) throws TypeError from the cast instead of returning null; only exceptions raised inside fromJson are caught. No transport calls tryParse in lib yet (only test/core/realtime_unknown_kind_test.dart), so this is dormant until an SSE/WebSocket adapter uses it.

refuted.evidence: driver_realtime.dart:147-162 `static DriverRealtimeEvent? tryParse(Object? json) { if (json is! Map) return null; final map = Map<String, dynamic>.from(json); if (DriverRealtimeKind.tryParse(map['kind'] as String?) == null) { return null; } try { return DriverRealtimeEvent.fromJson(map); } on FormatException { return null; } on TypeError { return null; } on ArgumentError { return null; } }`
refuted.suggested_fix: Read the kind defensively: `final kind = map['kind']; if (kind is! String || DriverRealtimeKind.tryParse(kind) == null) return null;` or move the check inside the try.

The only callers are in test/core/realtime_unknown_kind_test.dart, and DECISIONS.md:75 says 'Screens do not subscribe yet'. No real input can reach the throw today, so there is no runtime path. It is a latent defect to fix before a transport adapter is written.

It printed `result=null err=_TypeError`, so the call throws instead of returning null. The file was deleted afterwards.

refuted.title: 37 bare tester.takeException() calls silently discard flow exceptions in widget tests
refuted.description: Across 15 widget test files (account_flow_test.dart x10, offer_rules_flow_test.dart x7, reservation_near_pickup_test.dart x5, radar_offer_gone_test.dart x3, d3_trip_options_test.dart x2, and one each in round3/driver_admin_offers_home_test, offer_rules_cards_test, d3_home_back_test, radar_offer_close_test, d11_home_map_keep_test, home_offer_route_test, reservation_request_popup_test, exclusive_sheet_test, home_scheduled_test, adaptive_trip_island_test) a bare `tester.takeException();` is placed before tear-down or before the real assertions. It consumes any FlutterError raised during the flow (overflows, setState after dispose, null errors in build) without checking it, so layout regressions in Home/account/offer flows cannot fail these tests. In d3_trip_options_test.dart:100-101 the comment even states the trip screen itself overflows at the tested sizes ('Layout of the trip screen itself is not what this test covers.').
refuted.failure_scenario: A change introduces a RenderFlex overflow or a 'setState() called after dispose()' in the Home account menu; account_flow_test's ten cases still pass because the exception is swallowed at lines 242/263/304/347/359/386/411/427/442/490.
refuted.evidence: grep count: 37 occurrences of `^\s*tester.takeException();` across 15 files; test/widget/d3_trip_options_test.dart:100-101 `// Layout of the trip screen itself is not what this test covers.\ntester.takeException();`; test/widget/adaptive_trip_island_test.dart:472 `tester.takeException();`
refuted.suggested_fix: Replace bare calls with `expect(tester.takeException(), isNull)` where the flow is expected to be clean, or assert the specific expected exception type; fix the underlying trip-screen overflow referenced in d3_trip_options_test.

verdicts.reason: The finding says the bare `tester.takeException();` calls currently swallow flow exceptions, and that d3_trip_options_test.dart:100-101 hides a live trip-screen overflow. I converted every bare call to `expect(tester.takeException(), isNull)` in 5 of the 15 files, covering 27 of the 37 calls: account_flow_test (10), d3_trip_options_test (2), offer_rules_flow_test (7), reservation_near_pickup_test (5) and radar_offer_gone_test (3). Every test still passed. No exception is pending at any of those points today, including the d3_trip_options overflow the comment mentions, which no longer happens. Tests that actually cover layout still assert strictly, for example d3_trip_options_test.dart:104 `expect(tester.takeException(), isNull, reason: 'the options sheet overflows')`. So no current bug or regression is hidden. The only remaining point is that a future regression at those exact spots could go unnoticed. That is a speculative test-hygiene concern, not a failure reachable today. At most it is a cleanup: replace the bare calls with asserting ones and delete the stale comment at d3_trip_options_test.dart:100.
verdicts.repro: Wrote throwaway copies test/_audit_d105_{acct,d3_trip_options,offer_rules_flow,reservation_near_pickup,radar_offer_gone}_test.dart with the bare calls replaced by `expect(tester.takeException(), isNull)`. Ran each with `flutter test`. Results: account_flow "00:11 +10: All tests passed!", d3_trip_options "00:03 +4: All tests passed!", offer_rules_flow "00:12 +12: All tests passed!", reservation_near_pickup "00:15 +7: All tests passed!", radar_offer_gone "00:03 +3: All tests passed!". All throwaway files were deleted afterwards.

Getting no offers after switching every category off is the behaviour the driver asked for. The disabled Save button (:465-467, guard at :188) only means there is no '0 ride categories saved' announcement. It does not claim the state was discarded, and the UI never reports success it did not achieve, so the product-truth gate (REVIEW_AND_MERGE_GATES.md:43-45) is not violated. The 'screen implies zero was never saved' reading is the finding's inference, not something the UI says.
verdicts.repro: Static trace of _toggle, _persistSettings, _save, _buildSaveArea and the header in preferences.dart; checked test/widget/preferences_explicit_save_test.dart for the intended Save semantics.

refuted.title: The web verifier stubs MutationObserver as a no-op, so the documented 'listeners and overlays are released when their map is disposed' path in driver_map_camera.js is never executed
refuted.description: docs/driver-camera-architecture.md:77-78 and :87-89 claim the adapter releases Flutter listeners and the vehicle overlay when the map is disposed and that `tool/verify_driver_map_web.cjs` covers 'listener removal'. The adapter implements disposal with a `MutationObserver` on `document.body` (`driver_map_camera.js:501-510`: `state.car?.setMap(null); overlay.setMap(null); state.callbacks.clear(); ... states.delete(id); observer.disconnect();`). The verifier's context defines `MutationObserver: class {observe() {} disconnect() {}}` and never toggles `div.isConnected`, so that callback cannot run; the only 'removal' asserted is the explicit unsubscribe returned by `listen()` (`cjs:477-479`). A regression in the disconnect cleanup (e.g. a stale `states` entry keeping a disposed map and its gesture callbacks alive across a map re-create) would pass CI.
refuted.failure_scenario: A change that breaks the disconnect cleanup in driver_map_camera.js ships green; after a Home map re-create the old map's JS state keeps calling the previous Flutter gesture callback and holding the old overlay.
refuted.evidence: tool/verify_driver_map_web.cjs:72: `MutationObserver: class {observe() {} disconnect() {}}};`; :477-479: `remove(); const count = gestures; div.fire('pointerdown', [], mouse(100,100)); ... assert.equal(gestures,count,'Disposed Flutter listener released');`. web/driver_map_camera.js:503-509: `const observer = new MutationObserver(() => { wasConnected ||= div.isConnected; if (wasConnected && !div.isConnected) { state.car?.setMap(null); overlay.setMap(null); state.callbacks.clear(); ... states.delete(id); observer.disconnect(); } });`. docs/driver-camera-architecture.md:87-89: `tool/verify_driver_map_web.cjs (CI): ... vehicle overlay and listener removal.`
refuted.suggested_fix: Give the verifier a MutationObserver double that captures the callback, set `div.isConnected = false`, invoke it, and assert `states` no longer serves the id (configure/listen become no-ops) and that the overlay/car `setMap(null)` ran.

verdicts.reason: This is a test-coverage observation with no runtime defect. The disconnect cleanup in web/driver_map_camera.js:502-510 is correct as written: it sets car and overlay setMap(null), clears callbacks, removes the renderer listener, runs states.delete(id) and disconnects the observer. The failure scenario is a hypothetical future regression, not a path that fails today. The document's claim of 'listener removal' (docs/driver-camera-architecture.md:87-89) is in fact exercised by the explicit unsubscribe assertion at tool/verify_driver_map_web.cjs:477-479. Doc line :77-78 describes adapter behaviour, not verifier coverage. The no-op MutationObserver stub (cjs:72) is a deliberate SDK and DOM double; the doc states 'Uses SDK doubles'.
verdicts.repro: Static read of tool/verify_driver_map_web.cjs:7, 60-80, 440-479 and web/driver_map_camera.js:495-510, with grep of the states.get/delete use sites (:168, :507, :628-672).

refuted.title: Final anchor/look-ahead/sheet-glide contract assertions run only inside nested queueMicrotask callbacks; script exits 0 if the chain never runs
refuted.description: Lines 607-649 wrap the last group of assertions (claim/anchor, look-ahead, sheet glide, locate view) in five nested queueMicrotask callbacks, and the only 'PASS: ...' log is at the innermost level (line 644). Nothing at top level records that the callbacks executed (no counter, no process.on('exit') check, no explicit process.exitCode set when the PASS line is not reached). If a future adapter change causes an earlier await/microtask to never resolve, or an exception inside the mocks is caught by the adapter, the script finishes with exit 0 and the CI step `node tool/verify_driver_map_web.cjs` (drider-ci.yml:58) stays green with those contracts unverified.
refuted.failure_scenario: driver_map_camera.js changes so that the claim() path returns before scheduling the pan; the nested callbacks' assertions never execute; CI reports success and the look-ahead/sheet-glide regression ships to Pages.
refuted.evidence: tool/verify_driver_map_web.cjs:607 `queueMicrotask(() => {` ... :619, :626, :633, :641 nested `queueMicrotask(() => {`; :644 `console.log('PASS: vector palette, ... locate view');` (only completion marker)
refuted.suggested_fix: Set a `done = false` flag, flip it after the innermost assertions, and add `process.on('exit', () => { if (!done) { console.error('FAIL: async contracts did not run'); process.exitCode = 1; } })`.

verdicts.reason: The nested callbacks cannot be skipped silently. Each queueMicrotask at tool/verify_driver_map_web.cjs:607, 619, 626, 633 and 641 is scheduled by the test itself, unconditionally and synchronously from its parent (the first one at top level). None of them is scheduled by the adapter. Node always drains the microtask queue before it exits, so all five run. The finding's scenario (claim() returns before scheduling the pan) only means the pan assertion inside the callback sees the wrong camera; the AssertionError is then uncaught and Node exits 1. The assertions are test code, so the adapter cannot catch them. The script has no uncaughtException handler or exitCode override (grep count 0) and no await or promise that could hang the chain.
verdicts.repro: Read tool/verify_driver_map_web.cjs:600-649 and grepped it for process.on, uncaughtException and exitCode (0 hits). In node v22.22.0, `queueMicrotask(()=>{queueMicrotask(()=>{assert.equal(1,2)})})` exits with exit=1 and an AssertionError, and the same nesting with a console.log prints 'ran'.

refuted.title: applyProjection refuses while a background save is in flight instead of waiting (unlike every driver command), and its terminal caller does not retry after the journal step, leaving an authoritative terminal unapplied
refuted.description: D-09 (comment at lines 261-264) makes transitionTo/complete/cancel/noShow `await _afterBackgroundSave()` so a command that lands during a GPS/lifecycle persistNow waits instead of being dropped. applyProjection does not: `if (saving || _disposed || ...) return false;` (line 115). Its caller _drainProjection checks `_rideLifecycle.saving` only before the journal step (accept_ride_trip.dart:301-306, 100 ms retry); in the terminal branch it then `await`s CompletionJournal.finish (archive + markTerminal + handoff, :316) and only afterwards calls applyProjection (:319). If a persistNow started during that await (GPS snapshot every 2 min at :672-677, lifecycle pause at accept_ride.dart:724, secured-next at :1206), applyProjection returns false and _drainProjection returns without clearing _pendingProjection and without _scheduleProjectionRetry (no retry is scheduled in that branch). The trip is already archived and marked terminal on disk, but the controller is not terminal: subsequent Arrive/Start slides call transitionTo -> save, which throws 'Cannot revive a terminal trip' (prefs_active_ride_repository.dart:139) and the driver sees 'Trip progress could not be saved' with a Retry that also fails, until a Finish/Cancel tap reaches _yieldToAuthoritativeTerminal.
refuted.failure_scenario: With a realtime transport delivering an authoritative cancelled_by_rider / cancelled_by_admin projection: the event arrives just as a throttled GPS snapshot save begins; the journal archives the trip, but the screen stays on the live trip, every Arrive/Start slide is rejected with a 'could not be saved' snackbar, and the outcome sheet only appears after the driver taps Finish or Cancel. Only reachable with a real transport (MemoryDriverRealtime is per-screen today).
refuted.evidence: active_ride_controller.dart:111-119 `Future<bool> applyProjection(TripStatus status) async { ... if (saving || _disposed || (terminal && (!status.isTerminal || _terminalStatus == status))) { return false; }`  vs :72-76 `Future<bool> transitionTo(ActiveRideStage next) async { if (_backgroundSave != null) { await _afterBackgroundSave(); } if (_disposed || terminal || saving) { return false; }`  |  accept_ride_trip.dart:316-319 `await CompletionJournal(...).finish(... authoritative:true, next:next); if (!mounted) { return; } if (!await _rideLifecycle.applyProjection(status)) { return; }` (no _scheduleProjectionRetry on this return)
refuted.suggested_fix: Have applyProjection `await _afterBackgroundSave()` like the driver commands before checking `saving`, and/or make _drainProjection call _scheduleProjectionRetry() whenever applyProjection returns false for a terminal/released status.

verdicts.reason: The race is real in the code but cannot be reached today. The terminal branch of _drainProjection (accept_ride_trip.dart:316-319) does return without retrying when applyProjection rejects it while saving (active_ride_controller.dart:115). But it only runs for a status event from realtime. AcceptRide uses `widget.realtime ?? MemoryDriverRealtime()` (accept_ride.dart:592), and no code under lib/ calls emit or publish on it: grep for `.emit(` in lib returns nothing, and only tests inject a realtime. Without a transport, no authoritative cancelled_by_admin, completed or no_show projection reaches the screen, and the finding itself says so. Rider cancels go through _handleRiderCancelled, and when that fails the drain path calls _scheduleProjectionRetry (accept_ride_trip.dart:340-345). It is a latent hardening item for when a real transport lands, not a reachable defect now.
verdicts.repro: Traced the _drainProjection callers (accept_ride_trip.dart:254, 303, 352, 366, 900), the persistNow callers, and the MemoryDriverRealtime construction. `grep -rn "\.emit(" lib` returned no hits, so in the shipped app no event source produces status projections.

refuted.title: Settings re-runs MapTrafficSetting.restore on open; a quick toggle of 'Show traffic' is reverted in the UI while the opposite value is saved
refuted.description: `MapTrafficSetting.restore(_settings)` is fired unawaited in `initState` although main.dart:41 already restored it at startup. The restore enqueues a read; if the driver flips the switch before that read resolves, `MapTrafficSetting.set` sets `enabled.value` immediately and enqueues the save behind the read. When the read completes it overwrites `enabled.value` with the old stored value, so the switch snaps back, while the queued save then writes the driver's new value. UI and storage disagree until the next restore.
refuted.failure_scenario: Open Settings and immediately tap 'Show traffic on map' off: the switch flips back to ON; relaunch the app and it is OFF.
refuted.evidence: settings.dart:33-36 `void initState() { super.initState(); MapTrafficSetting.restore(_settings); }`; map_traffic_setting.dart `restore`: `enabled.value = saved is bool ? saved : defaultValue;` after the await; `set`: `enabled.value = value; return ... .save(section, {key: value});`
refuted.suggested_fix: Drop the restore in Settings (startup already restores) or have `restore` skip applying when a `set` happened after it started.

verdicts.reason: The race needs a tap on the switch before the Settings initState restore finishes, and in practice that does not happen. The restore is a SharedPreferences read (settings_repository.dart read(), with the getInstance result already cached after the restore in main.dart:41). It resolves within a few microtasks, long before the Settings route's push transition ends and a person can tap. The only delay is the static _enqueue queue, which waits only on settings writes already in flight, and those also finish in milliseconds. If the read did finish late, it would also report the value already stored, which matches the value already in `enabled` from startup. Divergence would need a tap in the gap of a few milliseconds before the read returns. The redundant restore is harmless.
verdicts.repro: Read map_traffic_setting.dart (restore/set), settings.dart:33-36, main.dart:41, and SettingsRepository.read/_enqueue. No caller holds the queue long enough for someone to tap first.

refuted.title: Evidence-matrix test forbids any PASS row, so recording real evidence breaks CI
refuted.description: The test asserts `expect(matrix, isNot(contains('| PASS |')))` on docs/certification/RELEASE_EVIDENCE_MATRIX.md. That freezes the current all-PENDING state as a rule: the first legitimately PASSed check (with an artifact, which tool/check_evidence_matrix.py explicitly supports) makes `flutter test` fail in the verify job. The test does not verify the matrix's correctness; it verifies that no progress has been made.
refuted.failure_scenario: The team completes the layout certification, records `| PASS |` with an artifact path; drider-ci verify job fails on evidence_matrix_test and the only ways out are deleting the test or lying in the matrix.
refuted.evidence: test/audit/evidence_matrix_test.dart:17 `expect(matrix, isNot(contains('| PASS |')));`
refuted.suggested_fix: Replace with 'PASS rows must have an artifact' (or delegate to check_evidence_matrix.py) instead of forbidding PASS.

verdicts.reason: The no-PASS assertion at test/audit/evidence_matrix_test.dart:17 is a deliberate tripwire. The test is named 'release evidence matrix does not claim unproven certification' (line 6). docs/REVIEW_AND_MERGE_GATES.md:49 says the matrix "stays PENDING. Device, browser, visual, accessibility, and performance PASS is not claimed." docs/FRONTEND_16_POINT_RECORD.md (F06) says "Rows were left PENDING on purpose." The matrix itself (RELEASE_EVIDENCE_MATRIX.md, closing paragraph) says physical/browser/visual/performance rows stay PENDING until a human records the artifact for the shipped candidate. When the team records real evidence, it is expected to update this documented gate in the same reviewed change. That is an ordinary edit to a test that encodes a documented policy, not "lying or deleting". The test also runs tool/check_evidence_matrix.py (lines 7-10), which separately enforces that a PASS row carries an artifact (check_evidence_matrix.py:25-27). No runtime or user path is affected.
verdicts.repro: Static trace. Read test/audit/evidence_matrix_test.dart:6-17, tool/check_evidence_matrix.py:18-28 and docs/certification/RELEASE_EVIDENCE_MATRIX.md (all 15 rows are PENDING). Cross-checked docs/REVIEW_AND_MERGE_GATES.md:49 and docs/FRONTEND_16_POINT_RECORD.md F06, which record that the PENDING state is intentional. No test was run, since the behaviour (any '| PASS |' fails) is not in dispute; only its intent is.

refuted.title: PASS evidence accepted with any non-empty artifact string; artifact path existence is never checked
refuted.description: A PASS row only has to carry a non-empty `artifact` string; the script never verifies that the path exists in the repository or is a URL. A typo'd or deleted artifact path therefore still counts as evidence, and with --require-complete the release would be declared complete on the strength of a string. The companion script tool/check_evidence_matrix.py has the same shape (PASS requires a non-empty artifact cell only).
refuted.failure_scenario: Someone records status PASS with artifact 'docs/evidence/layout.png' that was never committed; both gates stay green and the release is signed off on missing evidence.
refuted.evidence: tool/check_frontend_release.py:46-48 `artifact = row.get("artifact")\nif not isinstance(artifact, str) or not artifact.strip():\n    raise ValueError(f"{check}: PASS requires an artifact")`
refuted.suggested_fix: Resolve `artifact` relative to the repo root (or accept http(s) URLs) and fail when the file does not exist.

verdicts.reason: Accepting any non-empty artifact string is the documented scope of the checker. tool/check_frontend_release.py:2 says "Validate candidate evidence metadata; never substitute for running checks." Even on full success it prints "review artifacts before release sign-off" (line 74). docs/frontend-completion/09-release-verification.md says "The checker cannot prove an artifact is truthful, so review the linked logs/screenshots/traces." It also says final sign-off is a human review step. Artifacts are explicitly allowed to be workflow runs (RELEASE_EVIDENCE_MATRIX.md header: "a log, screenshot, or workflow run"), so they are often external URLs. The suggested repo-path existence check would therefore wrongly reject valid evidence, and an existing file still would not prove the evidence is true. The --require-complete gate is never treated as the sign-off. CI (drider-ci.yml:53-55) runs it only without --require-complete, against the all-PENDING template.
verdicts.repro: Static trace. Read tool/check_frontend_release.py:15-75, tool/check_evidence_matrix.py:25-27, .github/workflows/drider-ci.yml:53-55 (no --require-complete), docs/frontend-completion/09-release-candidate.json (all PENDING) and docs/frontend-completion/09-release-verification.md ("cannot prove an artifact is truthful"). No test was run.

The guidance text at :634-637 is already wrapped in Expanded plus MediaQuery.withClampedTextScaling(maxScaleFactor: 1.2), so it fits. The strip Row (:837-861) has an unscaled-clamp Text for _arrivalLine() at 13 pt, then SizedBox(12), Expanded(progress bar), SizedBox(8) and Text('$percent%'). refuted.title: A rider cancel that arrives during or just before the Start-trip slide is shown as 'Rider ended the trip' (mid-trip copy) because the start is committed first and the stage is read afterwards
refuted.original_title: A rider cancel that arrives during or just before the Start-trip slide is shown as 'Rider ended the trip' (mid-trip copy) because the start is committed first and the stage is read afterwards
refuted.description: `_drainProjection` holds back a pending projection while `_stageTransitioning` or `_rideLifecycle.saving` is set (line 301). The Waiting->OnTrip branch of `_advanceRide` (lines 830-853) commits `transitionTo(onTrip)` and starts the trip: it starts the ride-check detector and demo drive, persists the snapshot and sets `_onTripStartedAt`. Unlike Finish (line 919) and driver cancel (line 1382), it never calls `_yieldToAuthoritativeTerminal`, even though `_pendingTerminal` already holds a rider cancel. When the held event is finally drained, `_handleRiderCancelled` works out `wasOnTrip = _stage == ActiveRideStage.onTrip` from the stage the app just set locally, not from when the cancel happened. Per contract.json transitions (`trip_transitions.dart:144-145`), a cancel from `arrived` is a pickup cancel, not an `end_early`. The driver gets the end-early copy for a pickup cancel: island 'Rider ended trip', or the sheet 'Rider ended the trip / {rider} cancelled while the trip was active / Keep control of the vehicle… / I have stopped safely'. The cancel event's own `occurredAt` is never compared with `_onTripStartedAt`, so a cancel delivered late over the network is mislabelled in the same way. Reachable whenever a DriverRealtime is injected (the widget's public seam; `test/audit/pending_terminal_event_test.dart` drives exactly this sequence).
refuted.failure_scenario: The driver is waiting at pickup (stage arrived). The rider taps Cancel and the backend sends rider_cancelled with cancelFee 45 kr. The event lands while the driver is sliding 'Start trip', so the drain is deferred. The start is committed (stage onTrip, ride check started), then the cancel is drained. Home's island reads 'Rider ended trip · +45 kr', or, with a secured next trip, the sheet reads 'Rider ended the trip… cancelled while the trip was active… I have stopped safely'. refuted.title: The next trip started after a rider cancel (or another authoritative outcome) drops the injected DriverRealtime, so trip B never receives rider events; a shared bus would also be unsubscribed by A's dispose

refuted.description: Both authoritative handoffs build trip B with `AcceptRide.fromPersisted(next, waybillRepository:…, sessionController:…, locationRepository:…, routeRepository:…, activeRideRepository:…, dispatchRepository:…)`. `fromPersisted` has a `realtime` parameter (accept_ride.dart:249, 284), but these calls never forward `widget.realtime`. B's initState then creates and subscribes to its own private `MemoryDriverRealtime` (accept_ride.dart:591-594), so a rider cancel, an admin cancel or any projection for B is never delivered on the trip screen. If the bus were forwarded, A's dispose would call the global `_realtime.unsubscribe()` (accept_ride.dart:692). That runs after B's initState in pushReplacement, and `MemoryDriverRealtime.unsubscribe` bumps `_generation` and clears `_tripId` (driver_realtime.dart:488-491), which silences B's subscription. The same omission exists for the completion and driver-cancel handoffs (lines 936-957 and 1395-1413).

A's rider cancels, the driver taps 'I have stopped safely', and B opens. B's rider then cancels and the backend emits rider_cancelled for B. accept_ride_trip.dart:382-385 (same)

accept_ride.dart:692 `_realtime.unsubscribe();`
driver_realtime.dart:488-491 `void unsubscribe() { _generation++; _tripId = null; }`
refuted.suggested_fix: Forward `realtime: widget.realtime` in every handoff (lines 382, 472, 936, 1395). Make unsubscribe per-subscription (cancel only this screen's stream) instead of a global generation bump.

verdicts.reason: Every AcceptRide in production already runs on its own private, never-emitting MemoryDriverRealtime. Home, the offer radar and ride requests all construct it without `realtime:`, and DECISIONS.md D8/D9 says 'Screens do not subscribe yet'. So when the handoffs at accept_ride_trip.dart:382, 472, 936 and 1395 omit `realtime: widget.realtime`, trip B behaves exactly like every other trip today, and no rider event is lost. The shared-bus unsubscribe problem (driver_realtime.dart:488-491, accept_ride.dart:692) only applies if a shared bus is injected, and no caller does that. It is worth noting for when a transport is wired, but it has no effect now.

refuted.title: Stage slides are not blocked while a driver cancel is saving, so the cancel can abort silently after the trip is already archived as cancelled
refuted.original_title: Stage slides are not blocked while a driver cancel is saving, so the cancel can abort silently after the trip is already archived as cancelled
refuted.description: `_submitTripCancellation` sets `_cancellationInFlight` and awaits `CompletionJournal.finish`. That call archives the trip to history, writes the terminal marker and clears the snapshot. Afterwards `_rideLifecycle.cancel/noShow` runs. `_advanceRide` (820) only checks `_stageTransitioning || !mounted || _rideLifecycle.terminal`, not `_cancellationInFlight`. The confirm sheet has already closed, so the slide is live during the journal await. If the driver slides Start during that window, `transitionTo(onTrip)` takes the controller write lock. `ActiveRideController.cancel` then sees `saving` from a non-background write and returns false (active_ride_controller.dart:186). `_submitTripCancellation` resets the flag and returns with no message (1384). If instead the transition lands first, `cancel()` recomputes the target from in_trip, gives `cancelled_by_driver`, and disagrees with the `searching` already journalled.
refuted.failure_scenario: At pickup the driver confirms 'Cancel trip' and right away slides 'Start trip' while the journal write is pending. History and the terminal marker now say the trip was cancelled ('Cancelled by driver · reassigned'), but the trip screen stays open and goes on trip. Every later snapshot save fails with 'Cannot revive a terminal trip', and no error tells the driver the cancel did not take effect. Traced by hand through the code; nothing was run.
refuted.evidence: accept_ride_trip.dart:821 `if (_stageTransitioning || !mounted || _rideLifecycle.terminal) { return; }`; :1357-1358 `if(_cancellationInFlight || _completionInFlight || _handlingRiderCancellation) { return; } _cancellationInFlight=true;`; :1384 `if (!await (noShow ? _rideLifecycle.noShow(clearSnapshot: false) : _rideLifecycle.cancel(clearSnapshot: false))) { _cancellationInFlight=false; return; }`; active_ride_controller.dart:186 `if (_disposed || terminal || saving) { return false; }`
refuted.suggested_fix: Make `_advanceRide` (and the arrive path) return while `_cancellationInFlight`/`_completionInFlight`. In `_submitTripCancellation`, set `_stageTransitioning` for the duration and pass the precomputed `outcome` to `cancel(status: outcome)`. If the lifecycle refuses after the journal has run, tell the driver and leave the screen instead of returning silently.

verdicts.reason: The missing guard is real: `_advanceRide` at line 821 does not check `_cancellationInFlight`, and the slide at accept_ride_panel.dart:935-944 is not disabled during a cancel. But the window is not realistically reachable. `_submitTripCancellation` starts only when the modal confirm sheet's future completes (line 1354). The journal step then takes a few SharedPreferences reads and writes, the history archive and the terminal marker (completion_journal.dart:91-133), which is milliseconds. To land inside that window, the driver would need a full 320px slide gesture that began while the modal sheet still covered the screen. If the slide's save does run after the terminal marker, prefs_active_ride_repository.dart:138-139 throws 'Cannot revive a terminal trip', so transitionTo returns false. In the other order, cancel() just resolves cancelled_by_driver and the screen leaves normally. The fully silent case needs both writes to overlap inside a millisecond window, so it is speculative.
verdicts.repro: Hand trace of the order of `_submitTripCancellation` (1356-1384), ActiveRideController.transitionTo, cancel and _write (active_ride_controller.dart:72-100, 180-196, 271-307), and the repository save guard. Nothing run.

refuted.description: `_completeCurrentTrip` checks `_pendingTerminal` once, at line 919. A rider_cancelled (end_early) event arriving in that window passes the gate. `_drainProjection` then re-arms a 100 ms retry indefinitely, because `_completionInFlight` is never cleared on success (line 301). The retry timer is cancelled in dispose (accept_ride.dart:686). History keeps `completed` with full earnings, and the waybill is marked completed.

The driver's history and earnings show a completed trip that the backend recorded as cancelled_by_rider.

The rider-cancel path gets an authoritative `cancelFee` and still only shows it in the island notice or sheet: it is not passed to CompletionJournal.finish (accept_ride_trip.dart:425-431, 455). History shows earnings only for completed trips (ride_history.dart:82). Per DECISIONS.md:69 (D4), the Earnings repository is an in-memory seam and is not wired to screens. Fee settlement belongs to the backend, and the no-show amount is the server's to decide. The missing local figure follows that design and is harmless.
